method: Source and official documentation audit of the recorded revision, with 1.16.0 kept as the baseline. Selected integrations include live HTTP or WebSocket recordings and focused regressions; each cell separates implementation support from validation evidence. The comparison covers application-owned conversations, tools, media, embeddings, transcription, speech and batches. Realtime conversations and provider-managed conversation storage are outside the scope; their provider offerings remain recorded but are excluded from comparison totals. One-shot streaming speech and transcription remain in scope. Access restrictions and upstream errors are recorded explicitly. Provider offerings are not an exhaustive endpoint inventory.

native.label: Built in
native.description: A RubyLLM API handles the feature on supported models and protocols. Selecting a protocol or passing options to a registered alias does not make the integration partial. The cell records model and endpoint restrictions.

partial.label: Partial
partial.description: Some paths or result formats are supported; others are missing or need operational verification. The cell explains the limitation.

passthrough.label: Raw options
passthrough.description: Requires provider-specific request options, raw content, or a tool definition rather than a dedicated RubyLLM interface.

missing.label: Missing
missing.description: The provider offers this feature, but the audited version has no integration for it.

na.label: Not in this API
na.description: The audited API inventory does not document this operation. The cell identifies the scope; separate products, client-side tools and chat prompts doing a similar task are not counted.

unknown.label: Unverified
unknown.description: Provider availability or implementation behavior remains unresolved. The cell records the specific uncertainty and the sources checked.

deprecated.label: Deprecated
deprecated.description: The provider has deprecated this API and scheduled its removal. It is excluded from missing-integration work; the cell records the shutdown date.

out_of_scope.label: Outside scope
out_of_scope.description: The provider offers this feature through realtime conversations or provider-managed conversation state. These integrations are outside RubyLLM's coverage and excluded from the comparison totals.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.notes: The audit covers the public OpenAI inference APIs, built-in tools and their supporting resources: Responses, Chat Completions, Decisions, media, Files and Batch. The Agents API, GPT-Live, Multi-agent, organization administration and evals have no shared rows or are not exhaustively audited.

chat.notes: Chat runs on the Responses API by default, and on Chat Completions for audio and search models or when you select that protocol.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality openai/gpt-5-nano can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Basic exchange through Responses.

streaming.notes: Both Responses and Chat Completions stream through server-sent events into chunks and a final Message.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses openai/gpt-5-nano supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streams through Responses.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders text.format with a JSON Schema on Responses and response_format on Chat Completions. Availability depends on the model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#with_schema with openai/gpt-5-nano accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: Schema request and parsed result.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as input_image on Responses and image_url on Chat Completions, by URL, data URI or uploaded file ID, with low, high and original detail. Original detail applies to supported models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models openai/gpt-5-nano can understand local images
verification.notes: Local image as input_image.

pdf_input.notes: PDFs and other documents render as Responses input_file through file_data, file_url or file_id. Chat Completions accepts PDFs only, and not by external URL. Large files upload automatically to the Files API.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat pdf models openai/gpt-5-nano understands PDFs
verification.notes: Inline PDF as input_file.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat document URL models openai/gpt-5-nano reads PDFs the provider fetches from their URL
verification.notes: PDF fetched by OpenAI from file_url.

audio_input.notes: Audio attachments render as input_audio on Chat Completions, which RubyLLM selects for audio model IDs. The Responses protocol rejects audio attachments. OpenAI retires the gpt-audio and gpt-4o-audio families on January 20, 2027 in favor of GPT Audio 1.5.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat audio models openai/gpt-audio-mini can understand audio
verification.notes: input_audio on Chat Completions.

video_input.notes: The Responses input schema and the images and vision guide document no video content part. Sampling frames yourself is image input.

thinking.notes: Reasoning summaries, encrypted reasoning state and reasoning token counts come back on the Message, and replay across turns while store stays false. Models return summaries, not raw reasoning, and only when asked or configured.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking openai/gpt-5.4 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Reasoning state through Responses.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking sets reasoning.effort and a summary request on Responses, and reasoning_effort on Chat Completions. Accepted levels depend on the model. reasoning.mode for Pro mode goes through provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking openai/gpt-5.4 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Effort sent on the request.

citations.notes: URL, file search and container file annotations become typed Citation objects with offsets that survive joined output parts, in sync and streamed replies. Chat Completions search models return url_citation annotations.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with openai/gpt-5-search-api returns url citations when web search is enabled
verification.notes: url_citation on Chat Completions.

tools.notes: Ruby tools render as flat function definitions on Responses and nested ones on Chat Completions. Call results replay from local history. GPT-6 Astra needs Responses for tool calling.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling openai/gpt-5-nano can use tools
verification.notes: Function call and result through Responses.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) maps to auto, none, required and a named function.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control openai/gpt-5-nano respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Named function choice.

parallel_tools.notes: Several function_call items in one response become several tool calls, indexed by call ID.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling openai/gpt-5-nano can use parallel tool calls
verification.notes: Several calls in one response.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls:) sets parallel_tool_calls on the request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control openai/gpt-5-nano respects calls: :one for sequential execution
verification.notes: parallel_tool_calls set to false.

server_web_search.notes: The web_search alias adds the Responses tool and asks for its sources. Message#web_sources lists them, ServerToolCall keeps each search, and billed searches reach usage. gpt-5-search-api remains a Chat Completions search route. The older search preview models shut down on July 23, 2026.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with openai/gpt-5.2 searches and records the tool call items with the sources they found
verification.notes: Search items and sources.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with openai/gpt-5.2 streams searches and counts the ones it bills
verification.notes: Streamed search with billed count.

server_web_fetch.notes: OpenAI has no separate fetch tool. Reasoning models open pages and search within them as open_page and find_in_page actions of web_search, which RubyLLM keeps on ServerToolCall and lists through Message#web_sources.

verification.example: RubyLLM::WebSource Message#web_sources lists what a openai search found and opened, each address once
verification.notes: Parses a stubbed open_page action. The committed OpenAI search recordings contain search actions only.

server_code_execution.notes: The code_execution and code_interpreter aliases send code_interpreter with an automatic container. Container options merge in as keywords. Calls and outputs stay on ServerToolCall and replay from raw items.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat request rendering renders OpenAI Responses aliases
verification.notes: Request rendering only.

server_file_search.notes: The file_search alias takes vector_store_ids as keywords, and file citations come back typed. Stores are created outside RubyLLM.

server_mcp.notes: The mcp alias connects a remote server with url and name keywords. Approval requests appear as remote tool calls you approve or deny, then resume through mcp_approval_response items. Completed calls stay on ServerToolCall. Replay is stateless and streaming works.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat remote MCP tools openai executes a remote read-only tool after approval using stateless continuation
verification.notes: Approval, execution and stateless continuation.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat remote MCP tools openai denies a remote call without executing it
verification.notes: Denial path.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat remote MCP tools openai streams a remote approval and its completed result
verification.notes: Streamed approval and continuation.

prompt_caching.notes: Caching is automatic on supported models. Cached reads and cache writes reach the Tokens buckets. with_caching(key:) sets prompt_cache_key.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat prompt cache round-trip openai/gpt-5.2 reuses the prompt cache with a shared key
verification.notes: Second request reports cached tokens.

cache_boundaries.notes: cache_until_here renders prompt_cache_breakpoint on a content part and moves system messages into input items, since top-level instructions cannot hold one. Explicit breakpoints need GPT-5.6 or later.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#with_caching renders explicit breakpoints for OpenAI cache boundaries
verification.notes: Request rendering only.

explicit_cache.notes: The prompt caching guide documents automatic caching, breakpoints and lifetimes. The reference lists no cache resource to create, read or delete.

compaction.notes: with_compaction sends context_management with a compaction entry and an optional compact_threshold through at:. The returned compaction item replays on later turns. The truncation request field is recorded under Context editing.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat provider mapping maps to a compact_threshold entry on the OpenAI Responses API
verification.notes: Request rendering. The live recording covers the standalone endpoint, under Manual context compaction.

token_counting.notes: count_tokens posts to the Responses input_tokens endpoint and counts text, images, files, function tools, schemas and deferred tools. Hosted provider tools and provider_options are not part of the count request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#count_tokens with openai/gpt-5-nano counts a staged message without mutating the chat
verification.notes: Staged message count.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#count_tokens with openai/gpt-5-nano counts instructions, tools and structured output
verification.notes: Instructions, tools and schema.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint posts to images/generations and returns one or several images. Quality and output format go through provider_options. SVG and animated GIF output apply to GPT Image 2.6 models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image basic functionality openai/gpt-image-1-mini can paint images
verification.notes: Single image.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image basic functionality openai/gpt-image-1.5 paints several images in one request
verification.notes: Multiple images.

image_editing.notes: paint with with: and mask: posts to images/edits, as JSON image references for GPT Image models and as multipart uploads otherwise.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::ChatCompletions::Images#images_url targets the edits endpoint for a bare IO without reading it
verification.notes: Endpoint selection. No committed OpenAI edit recording.

video_generation.notes: OpenAI shut down the Videos API and Sora 2 models on September 24, 2026 and names no replacement. Video generation is not available. The remaining guide and reference pages are kept for history.

speech.notes: RubyLLM.speak posts to audio/speech and returns binary audio. OpenAI shuts down the models on this endpoint (tts-1, tts-1-hd, gpt-4o-mini-tts) on January 6, 2027 and points to Realtime, which RubyLLM does not implement.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech basic functionality openai/gpt-4o-mini-tts can speak
verification.notes: Complete speech result.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe posts files to audio/transcriptions with language, prompt, temperature, timestamps and response format. gpt-transcribe takes languages and keywords through provider_options, and the language: keyword sends the singular field that model replaces. whisper-1 and the gpt-4o transcribe models shut down on February 26, 2027.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openai/whisper-1 can transcribe audio
verification.notes: File transcription.

streaming_transcription.notes: A block on transcribe streams a recorded file into TranscriptionChunk objects and a final Transcription. Live audio sessions belong to Realtime transcription, recorded under Realtime sessions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openai/gpt-4o-transcribe streams text deltas and returns the final transcription
verification.notes: Text deltas and final event.

diarization.notes: Diarization models default to diarized_json, return speaker segments and accept known speaker names and references. The documented model, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, shuts down on February 26, 2027.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openai/gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize can transcribe audio
verification.notes: Speaker segments.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openai/gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize streams segments labelled with speakers
verification.notes: Streamed speaker segments.

moderation.notes: RubyLLM.moderate posts text and images to moderations and returns typed results.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Moderation.moderate with OpenAI provider moderates content and returns a Moderation instance
verification.notes: Text moderation.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Moderation.moderate with OpenAI provider moderates an image attachment without text
verification.notes: Image moderation.

ocr.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog document no OCR or document parsing endpoint. File inputs and high-detail images go through a chat model, which is not an OCR API.

embeddings.notes: RubyLLM.embed posts one or several texts to embeddings and supports dimensions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality openai/text-embedding-3-small can handle a single text with custom dimensions
verification.notes: Custom dimensions.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The embeddings reference accepts strings and token arrays only.

reranking.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog document no rerank endpoint. File search ranking options apply inside that tool.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload posts to the Files API with purpose and expires_in, and UploadedFile.find reads metadata. Uploaded IDs attach to chat. Multipart Uploads for larger files have no integration.

verification.example: RubyLLM::UploadedFile live uploads openai uploads a PDF through the Files API
verification.notes: Upload through the Files API.

verification.example: RubyLLM::UploadedFile live uploads openai/gpt-5-nano reuses an uploaded file in chat
verification.notes: file_id in a chat request.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM.download reads files/{id}/content and returns a DownloadedFile.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch uploads JSONL and creates batches for Responses or Chat Completions, then reads results back by custom_id, with a 50 percent cost multiplier.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with openai/gpt-5-nano answers staged chats and appends the answers to their conversations
verification.notes: Full batch lifecycle.

embedding_batches.notes: RubyLLM.embed_later targets /v1/embeddings through the Batch API and checks record positions in the results.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with openai/text-embedding-3-small embeddings embeds staged texts and hydrates each request result
verification.notes: Embedding batch lifecycle.

advisor_tool.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document an advisor tool..

agent_responses.notes: This row names the Perplexity Agent API, which is not an API of this provider. OpenAI's own Agents API is a separate hosted session product outside this row.

agent_skills.notes: A raw shell tool Hash passed to with_provider_tools can reference skills prepared elsewhere through environment.skills. RubyLLM has no Skills upload or version API. RubyLLM's own Skill class runs locally and does not touch this API.

async_research.notes: OpenAI shut down its deep research models on July 23, 2026 and documents no dedicated research API. Long reasoning runs use background mode, recorded under Background Responses jobs.

background_responses.notes: provider_options can set background: true, so a job can start. RubyLLM has no retrieve, poll or cancel path for the response, so the result stays out of reach and the returned Message holds no answer.

browser_use.notes: A Ruby function tool can drive your own browser through the code-execution pattern in OpenAI's guide. The built-in computer tool goes through a raw Hash, its computer_call is kept as a ServerToolCall, and RubyLLM has no way to return computer_call_output. The hosted browser belongs to the Agents API.

classification.notes: RubyLLM.judge posts to the Decisions API, whose choice, predicate and score questions classify text and images against fixed options. RubyLLM selects this protocol for judgments. gpt-6-luna is the only supported model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::OpenAI with the Decisions API judges all three question types through the compact DSL
verification.notes: Predicate, choice and score answers.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::OpenAI with the Decisions API judges an image without text input
verification.notes: Image input.

computer_use.notes: A raw computer tool Hash is forwarded and the model's computer_call is kept as a ServerToolCall, but RubyLLM cannot send computer_call_output, so the action loop stops there. A Ruby function tool works for the code-execution pattern in OpenAI's guide.

context_editing.notes: The Responses truncation field set to auto drops the oldest items when the input exceeds the context window, reachable through provider_options. OpenAI documents no selective tool result clearing.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document contextual embeddings..

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: audio/transcriptions is a dedicated file transcription operation. This row overlaps Transcription and is not a separate gain.

dubbing.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog document no dubbing operation. Realtime translation is a live session.

fast_inference.notes: Fast and Ultrafast processing are selected with service_tier, which with_provider_options forwards. RubyLLM has no dedicated switch and no WebSocket route, which OpenAI recommends for Ultrafast. Ultrafast covers GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.

file_management.notes: The Files API lists and deletes files. UploadedFile offers upload, find and download only, and raw options cannot reach those endpoints.

file_search_store_management.notes: Vector stores have their own creation, file indexing and search endpoints. RubyLLM can use a prepared vector_store_id with file_search but cannot manage the store.

fill_in_middle.notes: The legacy Completions reference still lists suffix, only for gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, which OpenAI shut down on September 28, 2026. No current model is documented for it.

fine_tuning.notes: OpenAI is winding down fine-tuning. Eligible existing customers can create jobs until January 6, 2027. RubyLLM has no fine-tuning job API. Calling an already fine-tuned model works as ordinary chat until its base model shuts down.

google_maps.notes: This row names Google Maps grounding, which is not an API of this provider.

guardrail_configuration.notes: The moderation request field on Responses sets a moderation model and a score or block policy for input and output. with_provider_options forwards it. RubyLLM has no named setting and does not type the returned scores. Agents SDK guardrails are a client library feature outside this row.

hosted_conversations.notes: OpenAI documents stored responses, previous_response_id and a Conversations resource. These are provider-stored conversation state, outside RubyLLM's coverage. RubyLLM sends store: false and builds requests from the local transcript.

image_batches.notes: The Batch API accepts /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits. RubyLLM batches raise for payloads that are not chat or embeddings, so raw options cannot reach them.

interactions_api.notes: This row names the Google Interactions API, which is not an API of this provider.

json_mode.notes: JSON object mode goes through with_provider_options as text.format on Responses or response_format on Chat Completions. with_schema is the named API for schemas.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with params openai/gpt-5-nano supports response_format param
verification.notes: json_object through provider options.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row names Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which is not an API of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: Chat#compact posts to responses/compact and keeps the returned envelope. It replaces only the context of later requests. Local messages and instructions stay. Pending tool calls block it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat compacts and continues a conversation with openai
verification.notes: Compaction followed by another turn.

music_generation.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document music generation..

nonchat_batches.notes: The Batch API also accepts moderations, image endpoints and legacy completions. RubyLLM registers Responses, Chat Completions and embedding batches only, and raises for other payloads.

omni_video_generation.notes: This row names a Google Omni video endpoint, which is not an API of this provider.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The API serves OpenAI's own models through its own wire formats. OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock belong to that provider's coverage.

prefix_completion.notes: The audited docs document no assistant prefill or prefix continuation. Predicted Outputs speed up a known output and do not constrain the response to a prefix.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: A raw programmatic_tool_calling Hash and allowed_callers through tool provider_options reach the API, and program items stay raw on ServerToolCall. A program that calls a local function cannot resume, because ToolCall drops the caller field that function_call_output must return.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching maps key, mode and ttl to prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_options, including the 12-hour Responses lifetime. Those lifetime options apply to GPT-5.6 and later. Earlier models take prompt_cache_retention, which needs with_provider_options because the retention: keyword renders as ttl.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document provider-managed model fallback on request..

realtime.notes: OpenAI documents the Realtime API and GPT-Live for live conversations and live transcription. These are outside RubyLLM's coverage. Conversation state stays in the application.

response_caching.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document a whole-response cache.. Prompt caching is recorded separately.

responses.notes: Responses is the default OpenAI chat protocol. Audio, realtime and search model IDs route to Chat Completions, and the protocol option selects either one.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality openai/gpt-5-nano can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Request posted to responses.

responses_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch targets /v1/responses by default, with a dedicated serializer and result parser.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with openai/gpt-5-nano answers staged chats and appends the answers to their conversations
verification.notes: Batch on /v1/responses.

search_api.notes: The audited docs document no standalone web search endpoint. Vector store search is recorded under Vector store management.

server_apply_patch.notes: A raw apply_patch Hash is forwarded and proposed patches stay readable on ServerToolCall, but RubyLLM cannot send apply_patch_call_output, so the model never sees the result.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: The image_generation alias adds the hosted tool to Responses. Tool options merge in as keywords, and the result stays as base64 on ServerToolCall rather than a typed Image.

server_tool_search.notes: with_tools(defer: true) and deferred tool classes send defer_loading and add the tool_search tool. Namespaced and searched calls dispatch back to Ruby tools and stay loaded on later turns. OpenAI offers it on gpt-5.4 and later.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat deferred tools with openai/gpt-5.4 loads a deferred tool through tool search and calls it
verification.notes: tool_search items and namespaced call.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat deferred tools with openai/gpt-5.4 keeps using a loaded tool on the next turn
verification.notes: Loaded tool on a later turn.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat deferred tools with openai/gpt-5.4 loads a deferred tool while streaming
verification.notes: Streamed tool search.

server_x_search.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document an X search tool..

shell_computer_tools.notes: Hosted shell goes through a raw shell Hash, with its calls and outputs kept on ServerToolCall and replayed. Local shell mode cannot run, because RubyLLM has no way to send shell_call_output. The computer tool has the same limit; see Computer use.

sound_effects.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document sound effect generation..

streaming_speech.notes: A block on speak yields SpeechChunk bytes as they arrive and returns the complete Speech. The endpoint's models shut down on January 6, 2027.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech streams speech from openai
verification.notes: Chunked audio.

task_budgets.notes: The docs describe no token budget for a whole task. max_tool_calls limits built-in tool calls in a response and return_token_budget limits returned web search content. Both are narrower tool settings that provider_options and tool options can reach.

text_intelligence.notes: The audited docs document no text analysis API returning intents, topics or sentiment. Decisions answers questions you write and is recorded under Classification.

vector_store_management.notes: The vector_stores endpoints create, list, update, delete and search stores and their files. RubyLLM has no integration. Hosted file_search can use a prepared store.

video_batches.notes: OpenAI shut down the Videos API and Sora 2 models on September 24, 2026 and names no replacement. Batch video generation is not available. The remaining guide and reference pages are kept for history.

video_editing.notes: OpenAI shut down the Videos API and Sora 2 models on September 24, 2026 and names no replacement. Video editing is not available. The remaining guide and reference pages are kept for history.

video_extension.notes: OpenAI shut down the Videos API and Sora 2 models on September 24, 2026 and names no replacement. Video extension is not available. The remaining guide and reference pages are kept for history.

voice_cloning.notes: OpenAI documents custom voices from a consent recording and reference sample, and prompt-generated voices for GPT-Live. RubyLLM has no voice or consent API. A voice created elsewhere can be used in speech through provider_options.

voice_conversion.notes: The audited docs index, API reference index and changelog do not document voice conversion..

web_fetch_api.notes: The audited docs document no standalone web fetch endpoint. Page opening exists only as a web_search action.

websockets.notes: Responses WebSocket mode runs over a persistent connection to /v1/responses and works with store: false. RubyLLM uses HTTP for Responses. Its WebSocket transport serves other providers' transcription.

gaps.notes: Background Responses jobs: provider_options can start a job, but RubyLLM has no retrieve, poll or cancel path for its result.

Browser use, Computer use, Apply patch tool: Raw tool definitions are forwarded and their calls stay readable on ServerToolCall. RubyLLM cannot send computer_call_output or apply_patch_call_output, so the client loop stops. Ruby function tools work for the code-execution pattern.
Programmatic tool calling: The hosted tool goes through a raw Hash. A program that calls a local function cannot resume, because ToolCall drops the caller field.
Shell and computer tools: Hosted shell goes through a raw Hash. Local shell mode has no way to send shell_call_output.

File listing and deletion, File search store management, Vector store management: RubyLLM has no list or delete for files and no vector store API. Hosted file_search can use a store prepared elsewhere.
Image batches, Other batch operations: The Batch API also accepts image, moderation and legacy completion endpoints. RubyLLM registers Responses, Chat Completions and embedding batches only.
Voice cloning: RubyLLM has no voice or consent API. A voice created elsewhere can be used in speech through provider_options.
Responses over WebSocket: RubyLLM uses HTTP for Responses and has no WebSocket mode, which OpenAI recommends for Ultrafast.
Fast inference, JSON object mode, Guardrail configuration, Context editing, Agent skills: These work through provider_options or a raw tool Hash without a named RubyLLM setting.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.notes: The audit covers the direct Claude API: Messages, Message Batches, Token Counting, Models, Files and Skills, with Managed Agents recorded as hosted sessions. RubyLLM sends API version 2023-06-01. Built-in coverage is conditional on supported models, and organization and billing administration are outside scope.

chat.notes: chat, ask and agents reach POST /v1/messages on the Messages API. Model restrictions apply.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Basic Messages API exchange with token usage.

streaming.notes: ask with a block streams server-sent events, including text, thinking, tool input, citation and compaction deltas.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streamed chunks assemble into the final message.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders output_config.format as json_schema. Anthropic rejects structured outputs combined with citations.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#with_schema with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: Request carries output_config and the reply parses to a Hash.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as base64, URL or Files API file_id sources.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 can understand local images
verification.notes: Local image sent as an attachment.

pdf_input.notes: PDF attachments render as document blocks from base64, a URL or a Files API file_id.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat pdf models anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 understands PDFs
verification.notes: PDF sent as a document block.

audio_input.notes: The Messages API content blocks have no audio input. Chat attachments cover images, PDFs and text. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for this type.

video_input.notes: The Messages API content blocks have no video input. Chat attachments cover images, PDFs and text. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for this type.

thinking.notes: Thinking text, signatures and redacted blocks parse into Thinking values, stream, and replay. Recent models omit the text unless display is summarized.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat thinking display with anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 returns readable thinking with display summarized
verification.notes: Adaptive thinking with xhigh effort returns summarized text and a signature.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking maps effort to output_config.effort, budget to budget_tokens, and display to thinking.display, and picks adaptive or budgeted mode from the registry. Sonnet 5.5 turns off with between_tools. Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 reject turning thinking off, and the API returns that error. Per-message effort changes are not exposed.

citations.notes: with_citations enables citations on text, PDF and Files API documents, and tool results can return search result blocks. Replies carry normalized Citation values, including while streaming.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 cites text documents in responses
verification.notes: Citation offsets map back to the response text.

tools.notes: Ruby tools render as custom tools with input_schema, and tool_use blocks run in the chat loop.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 can use tools
verification.notes: A tool call and its result complete a turn.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) maps to auto, any, none and tool. Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 reject any and tool with a 400 error, which RubyLLM surfaces.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Request forces the named tool.

parallel_tools.notes: Several tool_use blocks in one response all become tool calls.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 can use parallel tool calls
verification.notes: One response asks for two tools.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) sets disable_parallel_tool_use inside tool_choice.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 respects calls: :one for sequential execution
verification.notes: Request carries disable_parallel_tool_use.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) sends web_search_20260318 pinned to direct callers. Replies carry ServerToolCall values, citations, web_sources and search counts, and pause_turn continues automatically.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 searches, cites, and reports tool usage
verification.notes: Search results, citations, sources and search count.

server_web_fetch.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_fetch) or :url_context sends web_fetch_20260318 pinned to direct callers. Organization admins can turn web fetch off, and the API then returns a 400 error. No recording covers this alias.

server_code_execution.notes: with_provider_tools(:code_execution) sends code_execution_20260521, and result blocks return as ServerToolCall values. Generated file IDs stay in the raw result; fetch them with RubyLLM.download. This is the hosted tool, separate from with_code_execution, which runs in your own sandbox.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat code execution with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 runs code server-side and returns the result blocks
verification.notes: Request carries code_execution_20260521.

server_file_search.notes: The server tool list has no hosted file search. Search result blocks hold results your application supplies, and tool search finds tools, not documents.

server_mcp.notes: The mcp alias configures mcp_servers and a matching mcp_toolset with the mcp-client-2025-11-20 beta. Tool selection uses allowed_tools or default_config and configs. Anthropic runs tools without approval, so RubyLLM accepts only require_approval: never. Replies replay as returned. The newer mcp-client-2026-09-15 additions need raw headers.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat remote MCP execution anthropic executes a read-only tool and replays its history
verification.notes: Read-only Microsoft Learn MCP search, typed remote results and a follow-up replay.

prompt_caching.notes: with_caching sends top-level cache_control for automatic caching, and usage reports cache reads and writes by lifetime. Token minimums and prefix rules still apply.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat prompt cache round-trip anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 writes then reads the prompt cache
verification.notes: A second request reads what the first wrote.

cache_boundaries.notes: cache_until_here and with_instructions(cache_until_here: true) put cache_control on the last block of a message, with a per-boundary lifetime.

explicit_cache.notes: Prompt caching uses cache_control on requests. The API inventory has no cache resource to create, update or delete.

compaction.notes: with_compaction renders a compact_20260112 edit with at, instructions and pause_after, sends the compact-2026-01-12 beta, keeps compaction blocks in history, and sums usage.iterations so the summarization pass is billed. The API requires a threshold of at least 50,000 tokens.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat anthropic claude-sonnet-4-6 compacts a long conversation and bills the summarization pass
verification.notes: Response starts with a compaction block and tokens include every iteration.

token_counting.notes: count_tokens calls /v1/messages/count_tokens with messages, system, tools, tool choice and thinking. A schema or effort setting is not counted, because output_config is left out of the counted payload.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#count_tokens with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 counts the next request as configured
verification.notes: Instructions and tools raise the count.

image_generation.notes: The Claude API inventory has no image generation operation. Files that code execution produces do not count.

image_editing.notes: The Claude API inventory has no image editing operation. Files that code execution produces do not count.

video_generation.notes: The Claude API inventory has no video generation operation. Files that code execution produces do not count.

speech.notes: The Claude API inventory has no speech generation operation. RubyLLM registers no speech protocol here.

transcription.notes: The Claude API inventory has no transcription operation. RubyLLM registers no transcription protocol here.

streaming_transcription.notes: The Claude API inventory has no streaming transcription operation. RubyLLM registers no transcription protocol here.

diarization.notes: The Claude API inventory has no speaker identification operation. RubyLLM registers no transcription protocol here.

moderation.notes: The Claude API inventory has no moderation operation. The content moderation guide uses ordinary Messages prompts, and classifier refusals are not a moderation endpoint.

ocr.notes: The Claude API inventory has no OCR operation. Asking Claude to read an image or PDF is chat, not an OCR API.

embeddings.notes: Anthropic says it does not offer its own embedding model and points to Voyage AI, a separate service. RubyLLM raises an error.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: Anthropic says it does not offer its own embedding model and points to Voyage AI, a separate service.

reranking.notes: The Claude API inventory has no reranking operation. The embeddings guide points to Voyage AI, a separate service.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload posts to /v1/files with expires_in, and file_id attachments reach chat for images, PDFs and text. Requests send files-api-2025-04-14 and get its response shape, which omits expires_at.

verification.example: RubyLLM::UploadedFile live uploads anthropic uploads a PDF through the Files API
verification.notes: Upload returns the file ID and byte size. The endpoint takes no model.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM.download and UploadedFile.find reach the file content and metadata endpoints. Anthropic allows downloading files that skills or code execution created, not files you uploaded. No recording covers a download.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch creates, finds and cancels Message Batches, and returns ordered typed results at half price. Requests in a batch run independently and can name different models, and every beta a request needs joins the batch request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 reloads a batch by id and collects messages without the chats
verification.notes: Batch created, reloaded by ID and its results collected.

embedding_batches.notes: Anthropic offers no embedding endpoint, and Message Batches carry Messages requests only.

advisor_tool.notes: A raw advisor_20260301 definition in with_provider_tools and the advisor-tool-2026-03-01 beta in with_headers reach the API. The server_tool_use and advisor_tool_result blocks replay as returned. RubyLLM has no alias for it.

agent_responses.notes: Provider-specific row: Perplexity Agent API.

agent_skills.notes: Pass skills in the Messages container parameter with with_provider_options, together with the code execution alias. RubyLLM has no call for the Skills API that uploads and versions custom skills. with_skills is a separate feature that loads local folders.

async_research.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Managed Agents sessions are hosted agent runs, not an asynchronous research operation.

background_responses.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Message Batches and background compaction are separate operations.

browser_use.notes: A raw browser_toolset_20260801 definition works with Ruby tools in the browser namespace: member identity, order and text or image results are kept. browser_state result blocks, which report tabs after navigation and tab management, cannot be returned.

classification.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

computer_use.notes: Declare computer_toolset_20260801 with with_provider_tools and implement each member as a Ruby tool in the computer namespace. RubyLLM keeps member identity, runs calls in order, answers skipped calls, and returns text and image results. Your application owns the desktop. Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.5 take only the older computer_20251124 tool, which needs a raw definition and its beta header and does not dispatch to namespaced tools.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat Anthropic computer toolset returns a screenshot to a computer member call
verification.notes: A screenshot member returns an image in a tool result with toolset_name.

context_editing.notes: Send context_management edits such as clear_tool_uses_20250919 with with_provider_options and the context-management-2025-06-27 beta with with_headers. These edits replace the list with_compaction renders, so put compact_20260112 in the same raw list to use both.

contextual_embeddings.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Anthropic offers no embedding endpoint.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

dubbing.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

fast_inference.notes: Send speed: fast with with_provider_options. Opus 5.5 needs no beta header. Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 are in research preview and need fast-mode-2026-02-01 through with_headers. Fast mode on Opus 4.8 ends on 2026-11-30. RubyLLM does not apply fast mode prices to Cost.

file_management.notes: The Files API lists and deletes files. RubyLLM implements upload, metadata lookup and download only, and provider options cannot reach these endpoints.

file_search_store_management.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

fill_in_middle.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. The Messages API has no suffix parameter.

fine_tuning.notes: The Claude API inventory has no fine-tuning operation.

google_maps.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

guardrail_configuration.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Classifier refusals have no request settings, and Enterprise inference hooks are organization administration.

hosted_conversations.notes: Message threads keep a conversation on the server for a short time, in beta, and Managed Agents sessions keep agent state. Chat history stays in the application.

image_batches.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

interactions_api.notes: Provider-specific row: Google Interactions API.

json_mode.notes: JSON schema structured output exists. The structured outputs page documents no separate JSON object mode.

mantle_protocols.notes: Provider-specific row: Amazon Bedrock Mantle.

manual_compaction.notes: On-demand compaction is in beta. Send compaction: { type: "summarize" } with with_provider_options and compact-2026-09-04 with with_headers, then replace the summarized messages with messages= and keep the header. The returned block replays as raw content. Chat#compact raises on this provider.

music_generation.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

nonchat_batches.notes: Message Batches carry Messages requests only.

omni_video_generation.notes: Provider-specific row: Google Gemini Omni.

partner_model_protocols.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. The direct API serves Claude models only.

prefix_completion.notes: Older Claude models accept a final assistant message as a prefill. Add one with add_message and call generate. RubyLLM has no dedicated prefill interface. Claude 4.6 and later return a 400 error.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: Add allowed_callers to a tool with its provider_options and enable the code execution alias. Tool calls and server blocks replay as returned. The API requires the returned container ID on the next request, which the chat loop does not send, so a before_request hook has to add it. No recording covers this flow.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(ttl:) and cache_until_here(ttl:) set 5 minute or 1 hour lifetimes, and one-hour writes are priced at twice the input rate. Cache diagnostics need the raw diagnostics option.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat prompt cache round-trip anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 writes a one-hour boundary and prices it as one
verification.notes: One-hour cache write billed at its own rate.

provider_server_fallback.notes: Server-side fallback is in beta on the Claude API. Send fallbacks: "default" with with_provider_options and server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 with with_headers. with_fallbacks is RubyLLM's own client retry, a separate feature.

realtime.notes: The Claude API inventory has no realtime session operation.

response_caching.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Prompt caching reuses a prefix and still generates a reply.

responses.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

responses_batches.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

search_api.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

server_apply_patch.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. The text editor tool is a client tool, recorded under shell and computer tools.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

server_tool_search.notes: with_tools(defer: true), Tool.defer and with_mcp(defer: true) mark tools defer_loading and add tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119. A raw regex search tool replaces the default. Search blocks replay, and history drops them when a request declares no search tool.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat deferred tools with anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 loads a deferred tool through tool search and calls it
verification.notes: Model searches, loads and calls a deferred tool.

server_x_search.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

shell_computer_tools.notes: The computer toolset works through Ruby tools in the computer namespace. The bash and text editor tools need a raw definition and have no member dispatch: a Ruby tool of the same name renders a second declaration, so a before_request hook has to drop one. Your application runs every action.

sound_effects.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

streaming_speech.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

task_budgets.notes: Send output_config.task_budget with with_provider_options and task-budgets-2026-03-13 with with_headers. It merges with the effort that with_thinking sets. The budget is advisory, and the chat loop does not track it.

text_intelligence.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

vector_store_management.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Managed Agents memory stores hold text documents and are not vector stores.

video_batches.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

video_editing.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

video_extension.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

voice_cloning.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

voice_conversion.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

web_fetch_api.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory. Web fetch is a Messages server tool, not a standalone endpoint.

websockets.notes: Not documented in the audited API inventory.

gaps.notes: File listing and deletion: The Files API lists and deletes files. RubyLLM has no call for either, and provider options cannot reach them.
Browser use: RubyLLM keeps browser member calls in order and returns text and images, but cannot return the browser_state blocks that report tabs after navigation and tab management.

Shell and computer tools: The computer toolset is built in. The bash and text editor tools need a raw definition, and a Ruby tool of the same name adds a second declaration unless a before_request hook drops one.
Computer use: Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.5 take only the older computer_20251124 tool, which needs a raw definition and does not dispatch to namespaced tools.
Manual context compaction: On-demand compaction needs raw options and a manual swap of the summarized messages. Chat#compact raises on this provider.

Advisor tool, Agent skills, Context editing, Fast inference, Programmatic tool calling, Provider-managed fallback, Task budgets: These need provider options, raw tool definitions or beta headers. RubyLLM has no named interface. The Skills API that uploads custom skills has no RubyLLM call, and Cost does not apply fast mode prices.
Prefix completion: Older Claude models accept a final assistant message. RubyLLM has no dedicated interface, and Claude 4.6 and later return a 400 error.
Tool choice: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 reject the any and tool choices with a 400 error.
Thinking controls: Per-message effort changes and the progress updates display beta have no named interface.
Token counting: The counted payload leaves out output_config, so a schema or effort setting is not counted, though the endpoint accepts it.

providers.name: Gemini
providers.notes: Scope: the Gemini Developer API, with generateContent as the default route and Interactions selected by protocol: :interactions, plus media, files, caches, batches and one-shot Live transcription. Live conversations, stored conversations and other Google Cloud products are outside this inventory.

chat.notes: generateContent is the default route; protocol: :interactions selects Interactions. Google calls generateContent a legacy API that stays supported for existing integrations and recommends Interactions for new work. Parameters vary by model: Gemini 3 and later drop sampling parameters.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Asserts a real answer from generateContent.

streaming.notes: Streams through streamGenerateContent on the default route and through server-sent Interactions events on protocol: :interactions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses gemini/gemini-2.5-flash supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Request uses streamGenerateContent with alt=sse.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends responseJsonSchema on generateContent and response_format on Interactions. Batches send the same schema as responseSchema.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#with_schema with gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: Asserts JSON matching the schema.

vision.notes: Images go as chat attachments, inline or by Files API reference, on both routes.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can understand local images
verification.notes: Asserts the reply describes the image.

pdf_input.notes: PDFs go as chat attachments on both routes. Google documents up to 1000 pages.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat pdf models gemini/gemini-2.5-flash understands PDFs
verification.notes: Asserts the reply reads the PDF.

audio_input.notes: Audio goes as a chat attachment on both routes.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat audio models gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can understand audio
verification.notes: Asserts the reply describes the audio.

video_input.notes: Video goes as a chat attachment on both routes, with a processing mode for agentic navigation on the models that support it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat video models gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can understand local videos
verification.notes: Asserts the reply describes the video.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat agentic video gemini/gemini-3.5-flash-lite navigates a video and answers a follow-up
verification.notes: Covers navigation steps and the replayed follow-up.

thinking.notes: Returns thought summaries and signatures from both routes and replays signatures in later requests.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Asserts thinking text in the response.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking maps effort to thinkingLevel and a budget to thinkingBudget on generateContent. Google replaces budgets with levels on Gemini 3.6 and later; a bare with_thinking sends a level on models whose registry entry lists efforts, and -1 only on toggle models such as gemini-2.5-flash. An explicit budget: is still sent as thinkingBudget. Interactions takes effort and summary display only, and RubyLLM raises for a budget or thinking off there.

citations.notes: Maps grounding metadata and Interactions annotations to Citation values. Citations come from a grounding tool such as with_provider_tools(:web_search); with_citations alone does not add a tool.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with gemini/gemini-2.5-flash returns grounding citations when search is enabled
verification.notes: Asserts Citation values from grounding metadata.

tools.notes: Function tools work on both routes, including per-tool thought signatures and media in tool results on Gemini 3 and later. Tool results can carry inline media or a Files API reference next to the response.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can use tools
verification.notes: Round trip of a function call and its result.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) maps auto, none, required and a specific tool to functionCallingConfig on generateContent and tool_choice on Interactions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control gemini/gemini-2.5-flash respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Request carries allowedFunctionNames.

parallel_tools.notes: Receives several function calls in one response and returns results in call order, because functionResponse parts pair by position.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: Response carries more than one functionCall.

parallel_tool_control.notes: Neither the function calling guide nor the generateContent and Interactions references document a switch that limits parallel calls.

server_web_search.notes: web_search and google_search aliases on both routes, with queries and pages on the server tool call and billed searches counted.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with gemini/gemini-3.5-flash grounds the answer and exposes the queries it ran
verification.notes: Response carries webSearchQueries and grounding chunks.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Interactions streams a Google Search answer with suggestions it does not keep for replay
verification.notes: Covers the Interactions route.

server_web_fetch.notes: web_fetch and url_context aliases on both routes. Google limits which URL types and models work.

server_code_execution.notes: code_execution alias on both routes. Returns execution parts as server tool calls and replays them in later turns.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat code execution with gemini/gemini-3.5-flash runs code server-side and replays the turn
verification.notes: Response carries executableCode and codeExecutionResult parts.

server_file_search.notes: file_search alias on both routes uses an existing store and parses grounding. Creating and filling stores is the separate store management row; RubyLLM.upload targets ordinary Files.

server_mcp.notes: with_provider_tools(mcp: {name:, url:}) on protocol: :interactions connects a Streamable HTTP server. Google documents remote MCP for Interactions. Calls, results and signed steps replay statelessly. Remote tools run without an approval step. The generateContent schema also lists mcpServers; RubyLLM has no alias for it there.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Interactions executes a remote MCP tool and replays its signed results through stateless chat
verification.notes: Fresh Microsoft Learn MCP execution returned actual call/result steps, then a second user turn used those results. MCP output signatures remain in raw history but are omitted from input as required by the input schema; thought signatures are retained.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Interactions streams remote MCP results and preserves the complete signed history
verification.notes: Fresh SSE execution reconstructed call, result, thought and model-output steps; text chunks equal final assistant text and actual prompt/tool/thought usage is normalized.

prompt_caching.notes: Implicit caching applies automatically on Gemini 2.5 and later on both routes, and RubyLLM reports cached tokens. An ineligible prompt stays uncached; thresholds vary by model.

cache_boundaries.notes: Gemini has no cache breakpoint in a request. RubyLLM accepts cache_until_here and only logs a note, because caching is implicit or goes through cache resources.

explicit_cache.notes: RubyLLM.cache creates, finds, updates and deletes cachedContents, and with_caching(id:) attaches one on generateContent. Google does not offer explicit caching on Interactions or on Gemini 4 Argon and later; RubyLLM raises for a cache id on Interactions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::CachedContent explicit caching round-trip gemini/gemini-2.5-flash creates, uses, extends, and deletes a cache
verification.notes: Full lifecycle against cachedContents.

compaction.notes: Gemini documents context window compression only for Live sessions. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application. with_compaction is dropped on generateContent.

token_counting.notes: chat.count_tokens calls countTokens with rendered contents, instructions and tools on generateContent. Interactions has no RubyLLM token counting method.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#count_tokens with gemini/gemini-3.5-flash counts the next request as configured
verification.notes: Asserts a positive count from countTokens.

image_generation.notes: paint uses generateContent for Gemini image models, with multiple results, aspect ratio and resolution. Google shut down Imagen, so the predict path has no model. Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 does not match the image model test and goes to predict.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image basic functionality gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image can paint images
verification.notes: Request goes to generateContent and returns an image.

image_editing.notes: paint accepts reference images through with: on Gemini image models. The guide edits by prompt and has no mask field; RubyLLM raises for mask:. Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 has the same routing limit as image generation.

video_generation.notes: Google shut down Veo in the Gemini API on 2026-10-22 and points to Gemini Omni Flash, which runs through Interactions. RubyLLM.animate still posts to predictLongRunning, which reaches no current model. A chat on protocol: :interactions with an Omni model forwards response_format and returns the video as an attachment, with no Video result or job. No recording covers this route, so whether it works remains unverified.

speech.notes: speak uses generateContent with a voice name and returns Speech. Multi-speaker and output format settings go through provider_options. Gemini 3.8 TTS returns WAV by default, yet RubyLLM labels the result as pcm. A stored voice ID belongs in voiceConfig.voice, while voice: writes prebuiltVoiceConfig. Earlier TTS models may shut down from 2026-11-17.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech basic functionality gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts can speak
verification.notes: Request goes to generateContent and returns audio.

transcription.notes: transcribe uses generateContent audio understanding on general models and returns a typed transcript. The dedicated model is its own row.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality gemini/gemini-2.5-flash can transcribe audio
verification.notes: Asserts text from generateContent.

streaming_transcription.notes: transcribe with gemini-3.5-transcribe-live streams BidiGenerateContent partial and final text into TranscriptionChunk and returns a Transcription. It takes mono 16-bit PCM WAV with manual activity boundaries, and rejects diarization and word timestamps, which Google does not offer on Live. One-shot transcription is kept; live conversations are outside scope.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription streams partial and final transcription through gemini Live

moderation.notes: The audited inventory has no moderation endpoint. Safety settings on a generation request are the guardrail row.

ocr.notes: The audited inventory has no OCR or document parsing endpoint. Reading a PDF with a chat model is PDF input.

embeddings.notes: embed uses batchEmbedContents with dimensions, task_type and title.

reranking.notes: The audited inventory has no reranking endpoint. Asking a chat model to rank text is chat.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload uses the resumable Files API and waits for processing, then chat attachments reference the file. Registering Cloud Storage files through files:register is not implemented.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM.download follows a file's downloadUri. Google does not let you download user-uploaded files, only files models generate, and RubyLLM raises when a file has no URI.

chat_batches.notes: Batch.submit sends inline generateContent requests for one model, with polling, cancellation and ordered results. Google recommends the JSONL input file for larger jobs, since inline requests stop at 20 MB; RubyLLM does not submit input files.

verification.notes: Live submit, find and cancel.

advisor_tool.notes: The audited inventory documents no advisor tool.

agent_responses.notes: This row is the Perplexity Agent API, which is a different service.

agent_skills.notes: Gemini managed agents mount SKILL.md files into a remote environment. RubyLLM has no agent or environment resources on Gemini, and chat requests name a model, not an agent.

async_research.notes: Deep Research is a preview agent that runs in the background through Interactions. RubyLLM.research raises on this provider because it declares no research protocol. Vertex AI has its own.

background_responses.notes: This row concerns the Responses protocol, which Gemini does not serve. Interactions has its own background execution, covered by the research row.

browser_use.notes: The Computer Use tool targets browser environments and is generally available. A raw tool Hash reaches both routes through with_provider_tools. Your application runs the actions and sends back screenshots.

classification.notes: The audited inventory has no classification endpoint. Prompting a chat model is chat.

computer_use.notes: Computer Use is generally available on both APIs. RubyLLM has no alias for it. A raw tool Hash, such as computerUse on generateContent or type computer_use on Interactions, is forwarded, and your application runs the returned actions.

context_editing.notes: Live contextWindowCompression can drop old turns through a sliding window. Gemini documents this only for Live sessions, which are outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The audited inventory has no contextualized embedding operation. task_type and title are ordinary embedding fields.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: transcribe with gemini-3.5-transcribe goes through Interactions with transcription_config and returns text, usage, word offsets and detected speakers. Google rejects custom vocabulary combined with diarization or word timestamps.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription transcribes audio with speaker labels and word timestamps through gemini
verification.notes: Fresh provider execution and offline replay passed. Typed transcript, numeric word offsets and actual detected speaker labels; the two-speaker fixture returned distinct labels.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription distinguishes two speakers through gemini dedicated transcription
verification.notes: Fresh provider execution and offline replay passed. Typed transcript, numeric word offsets and actual detected speaker labels; the two-speaker fixture returned distinct labels.

dubbing.notes: The audited inventory has no dubbing endpoint. Live translate is a realtime session.

fast_inference.notes: Priority inference is selected with service_tier in the request body. with_provider_options(service_tier: "priority") forwards it. Flex uses the same field.

file_management.notes: Google documents listing and deleting Files. RubyLLM has upload, find and download only.

file_search_store_management.notes: Google documents File Search store and document lifecycles and import. RubyLLM can only name an existing store on the file_search tool.

fill_in_middle.notes: The audited inventory has no completion endpoint with a suffix. The OpenAI compatibility layer lists chat completions, images, embeddings and batches.

fine_tuning.notes: Google states no Gemini API model supports fine-tuning and has no plans to add it. Tuning on Google Cloud is a separate product.

google_maps.notes: google_maps alias on both routes. Options such as a location go in the alias hash. Availability depends on the model.

guardrail_configuration.notes: safetySettings pass through with_provider_options on generateContent. RubyLLM has no shared API for thresholds, and it maps blocks to content_filter.

hosted_conversations.notes: Interactions can store requests and continue them with previous_interaction_id. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; chat sends store: false and replays application-owned history.

image_batches.notes: Google runs image generation through Batch. A staged chat with raw image response modalities is forwarded and its attachments are parsed. There is no batched paint.

interactions_api.notes: protocol: :interactions handles text and media input, local tools, JSON Schema output, streaming, citations, thinking and usage. It sends store: false and replays results from application-owned history. Stored continuation is outside scope. Omni, Lyria and agents have no dedicated RubyLLM operation on it.

verification.notes: Fresh Microsoft Learn MCP execution returned actual call/result steps, then a second user turn used those results. MCP output signatures remain in raw history but are omitted from input as required by the input schema; thought signatures are retained.

json_mode.notes: generationConfig.responseMimeType of application/json without a schema passes through with_provider_options.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row is Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which is a different service.

manual_compaction.notes: Live offers automatic window compression only, with no separate compact operation.

music_generation.notes: The music guide generates Lyria audio through Interactions. A chat on protocol: :interactions with a Lyria model returns the audio as an attachment. RubyLLM has no music operation, and Lyria RealTime needs a Live session. No recording covers it.

nonchat_batches.notes: TTS models list Batch API support. A staged chat with raw AUDIO response modalities is forwarded and its attachments are parsed. There is no batched speak.

omni_video_generation.notes: Omni generates video through Interactions. A chat on protocol: :interactions with an Omni model forwards response_format and returns the video as an attachment. RubyLLM always sends an empty system_instruction and Google lists system instructions as unsupported on Omni, and no recording covers this route, so whether it works remains unverified. There is no typed result or animate route.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The audited inventory serves Google models only.

prefix_completion.notes: Migration guides list prefilled model turns as removed on Gemini 3.6 and later, with a 400 error, which hints that older models accept them. No page documents prefill as a feature of any current model, and no recording covers it.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The audited inventory and tool guides do not document code that calls tools programmatically.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(id:) attaches a cache resource on generateContent, and RubyLLM.cache sets its TTL. Implicit caching takes no options. This does not apply to Interactions or Gemini 4 Argon.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The audited inventory documents no provider-managed model fallback. Google reroutes retired model names, which is a deprecation policy.

realtime.notes: The Live API documents realtime voice and video sessions. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

response_caching.notes: The audited inventory documents no cache of whole responses.

responses.notes: Gemini serves no Responses endpoint. The OpenAI compatibility layer lists chat completions, images, embeddings and batches; Interactions and Live are separate APIs.

responses_batches.notes: Gemini serves no Responses endpoint, so it has no Responses batches.

search_api.notes: The audited inventory has no standalone search endpoint. Grounding is a tool on generation requests.

server_apply_patch.notes: The audited tools list has no apply patch tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: The audited tools list has no image generation tool. Image generation is a model operation.

server_tool_search.notes: The audited tools list has no hosted tool search. RubyLLM gives Gemini chats its own client-side tool search.

server_x_search.notes: The audited tools list has no X search tool.

shell_computer_tools.notes: Computer Use supports browser, mobile and desktop actions through a raw tool definition, and your application executes them. Antigravity agents have a hosted shell, which RubyLLM does not reach.

sound_effects.notes: The audited inventory has no sound effects endpoint. Lyria generates music.

streaming_speech.notes: Gemini streams TTS audio as raw PCM through Interactions. RubyLLM.speak makes one generateContent request, and a block raises because this protocol has no speech streaming.

task_budgets.notes: The audited inventory documents no task budget.

text_intelligence.notes: The audited inventory has no text analysis endpoint.

vector_store_management.notes: The audited inventory has no general vector store API. File Search stores have their own row.

video_batches.notes: The Batch API documents generateContent and embedding jobs, and the Omni guide documents no batch route.

video_editing.notes: Omni edits videos through Interactions, by stored turns or from an uploaded video. A chat on protocol: :interactions can send an uploaded video as an attachment and returns the result as an attachment. Stored turns are outside scope, Google does not offer uploaded video editing in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, and no recording covers this, so whether the route works remains unverified.

video_extension.notes: Google shut down Veo in the Gemini API on 2026-10-22 and points to Gemini Omni Flash, which runs through Interactions. animate(extend:) still sends a Veo URI to predictLongRunning. Omni extends through Interactions from stored turns or an uploaded video, up to 30 seconds total. A chat on protocol: :interactions can send the uploaded video as an attachment; no recording covers this, so whether the route works remains unverified.

voice_cloning.notes: Voice replication creates a voice from a source recording and a consent recording through POST /v1beta/voices, or a stateless voice key. RubyLLM has no voice lifecycle, and speak can only use a voice prepared elsewhere through provider_options.

voice_conversion.notes: The audited inventory has no speech-to-speech conversion. Voice remixing edits a stored voice from a text instruction.

web_fetch_api.notes: The audited inventory has no standalone fetch endpoint. URL context is a tool on generation requests.

websockets.notes: This row is Responses over WebSocket. Gemini serves no Responses endpoint, and its WebSockets belong to Live.

gaps.notes: Video generation, Omni video generation, Video editing, Video extension: RubyLLM.animate posts to predictLongRunning, which no current Gemini API model serves since Google shut down Veo on 2026-10-22. Omni runs through Interactions, where a chat on protocol: :interactions could reach it, but no recording covers that route.

Image generation, Image editing: paint sends gemini-nano-banana-2.1 to the shut down Imagen predict endpoint, because the model test looks for -image in the id. Other Gemini image models work. Masks are not supported.

Speech generation: speak labels the WAV that Gemini 3.8 TTS returns by default as pcm, rejects other format values, and writes voice: to prebuiltVoiceConfig, so stored voice IDs need provider_options.
Agent skills: Gemini managed agents mount skills into remote environments. RubyLLM has no agent or environment resources on this provider.
Asynchronous research: Deep Research runs as a background Interactions agent. This provider declares no research protocol, so RubyLLM.research raises here.
Browser use, Computer use, Shell and computer tools: Computer Use takes a raw tool definition, and your application executes the actions. RubyLLM has no alias for it.
File listing and deletion: Google documents listing and deleting Files. RubyLLM has upload, find and download only.
File search store management: RubyLLM names an existing store on the file_search tool, but does not create or delete stores or import documents.
Chat batches, Embedding batches: Batches submit inline requests only, which Google limits to 20 MB. JSONL input files are not implemented.
Fast inference, Guardrail configuration, JSON object mode: service_tier, safetySettings and responseMimeType without a schema need raw provider options.
Image batches, Other batch operations: Image and TTS batches work as staged chats with raw response modalities. There is no batched paint or speak.
Music generation: Lyria runs through a chat on Interactions with audio attachments. RubyLLM has no music operation or Lyria RealTime session.
Streaming speech generation: Gemini streams TTS through Interactions. speak has no streaming implementation here.
Voice cloning: Voice replication needs POST /v1beta/voices with consent audio. RubyLLM has no voice lifecycle.
Prefix completion: Migration guides say prefilled model turns stop working on Gemini 3.6 and later, and no page documents the feature for older models, so availability remains unverified.

Anthropic-managed Claude on claude.googleapis.com, Cloud Vision, Document AI and Model Armor are separate services; Discovery Engine ranking and Cloud Text-to-Speech are included because RubyLLM routes to them.

ocr.notes: Google offers Mistral OCR (25.05) as a partner model, in us-central1 and europe-west4. RubyLLM.ocr cannot reach it: the Vertex Mistral protocol includes chat, embeddings and media but not the OCR module, although the registry lists mistral-ocr-2505. DeepSeek-OCR had a scheduled retirement date of October 21, 2026, which has passed. Chat-prompted OCR on Gemini is not counted. Cloud Vision and Document AI are separate services.
