background_responses.notes: The Grok Responses page shows background: false in a sample response and documents no background mode. That field alone does not establish the feature. Checked the Grok Responses page and the Grok 4.7 model page. Interactions background execution is a separate row.

browser_use.notes: Google-managed Claude documents the browser use tool, and Gemini computer use documents browser environments. with_provider_tools accepts a raw declaration. The application executes the actions through tools registered with Tool.namespace.

classification.notes: The audited inventory documents no classification endpoint. Prompting a model to classify is not counted.

computer_use.notes: Gemini computer use is generally available, and Google-managed Claude documents the computer use tool. with_provider_tools accepts a raw declaration. The application executes the actions through tools registered with Tool.namespace.

context_editing.notes: Google-managed Claude documents context editing in beta. Clearing edits go through with_provider_options(context_management:) and with_headers for the beta header. with_compaction covers only the compaction edit.

contextual_embeddings.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. Embedding task types are not contextual embeddings.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe selects the dedicated protocol for gemini-3.5-transcribe-preview, sends audioTranscriptionConfig and returns word offsets and speaker labels. It requires the global location. Google names the current model gemini-3.5-transcribe, which RubyLLM does not route to this protocol.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription transcribes audio with speaker labels and word timestamps through vertexai
verification.notes: audioTranscriptionConfig returns speaker labels and word offsets.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription distinguishes two speakers through vertexai dedicated transcription
verification.notes: Two distinct speaker labels.

dubbing.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory.

fast_inference.notes: Priority PayGo and Flex PayGo use the X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Shared-Request-Type header, available through with_headers. Claude fast mode is offered only on Anthropic-managed Claude.

file_management.notes: Cloud Storage lists and deletes objects. The public RubyLLM file API uploads, finds and downloads. The internal list_uris helper serves batch output only.

file_search_store_management.notes: RAG Engine exposes corpus and file lifecycle. RubyLLM has no client for these resources. A raw retrieval tool can use an existing corpus.

fill_in_middle.notes: Codestral 2 on Vertex AI documents fill-in-the-middle completion with a prompt and an optional suffix. The Vertex Mistral protocol sends only chat messages.

fine_tuning.notes: Google offers supervised and reinforcement tuning jobs. RubyLLM has no tuning client.

google_maps.notes: The google_maps alias sends the googleMaps grounding tool on Gemini models.

guardrail_configuration.notes: safetySettings and modelArmorConfig on generateContent, and Llama Guard settings on Llama routes, go through with_provider_options. Separate Cloud security services are outside this row.

hosted_conversations.notes: Vertex AI Interactions stores conversation state and continues it with previous_interaction_id. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

image_batches.notes: Gemini image models support batch inference. RubyLLM.batch can stage a chat request with raw image response modalities and parse the attachments. There is no batched paint API.

interactions_api.notes: The Research protocol reaches the Vertex Interactions endpoint for single-turn hosted agents. Chat cannot select Interactions on Vertex AI, although Google documents it for Gemini 3 and later models. Function tools, continuation and other agents are unreachable.

json_mode.notes: Gemini generationConfig takes application/json without a schema, passed through with_provider_options. Chat Completions routes take response_format the same way.

mantle_protocols.notes: Provider-specific row for Amazon Bedrock Mantle.

manual_compaction.notes: Claude documents on-demand compaction on Google-managed Claude. Chat#compact needs a protocol with a compaction route, and only the Responses protocol has one.

music_generation.notes: Lyria 3 runs through Interactions and Lyria 2 through predict. RubyLLM has no music operation, and neither route is reachable.

nonchat_batches.notes: Batch inference documents Gemini generation and embedding models, including image output. The TTS model page lists no batch option, and Veo and Omni pages mark batch inference not supported. Image and embedding batches have their own rows.

omni_video_generation.notes: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates video through Interactions and is generally available. RubyLLM implements Veo prediction jobs and has no Interactions route for it.

partner_model_protocols.notes: protocol_for selects Claude rawPredict, Mistral rawPredict, or Chat Completions for publisher-prefixed MaaS models such as Grok, Llama, Qwen, GLM and DeepSeek. The Grok Responses route and Mistral OCR are separate rows.

verification.notes: Routing for each publisher family.
verification.example: routes publisher-prefixed MaaS models to the Chat Completions protocol

prefix_completion.notes: Claude models before 4.6 accept a final assistant prefill: add the assistant message, then complete. Claude 4.6 and later reject it. The partner and open model pages document no prefix option.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: Google-managed Claude does not offer programmatic tool calling, and no Gemini equivalent is documented.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching sets Claude TTL and automatic caching, and CachedContent attaches a Gemini cache resource.

provider_server_fallback.notes: Claude server-side fallback is in beta only on the Claude API and Anthropic-managed Claude. No Gemini equivalent is documented.

realtime.notes: Vertex AI documents realtime conversations through the Live API. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

response_caching.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. Context caching stores prompt prefixes, not responses.

responses.notes: Google offers Grok through the Responses API at endpoints/openapi/responses, without stored state. RubyLLM Vertex AI registers no Responses protocol and routes Grok to Chat Completions.

responses_batches.notes: The Grok Responses page documents no batches, and the Grok 4.7 model page marks batch predictions not supported.

search_api.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. Web grounding is a tool on generation requests, and Vertex AI Search is a separate product.

server_apply_patch.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. Image models generate images directly, and the Interactions tool list has no image generation tool.

server_tool_search.notes: with_tools(defer: true) marks tools defer_loading and adds the tool search tool on Claude routes. Claude documents the tool search tool on Google-managed Claude. Gemini routes send deferred tools as ordinary tools.

verification.notes: Claude on Vertex AI renders defer_loading. No recording covers this route.
verification.example: does not gate deferral on the model catalog

server_x_search.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. The Grok pages on Vertex AI document no X search tool.

shell_computer_tools.notes: Google-managed Claude documents the bash, text editor and computer tools, and Gemini documents computer use. Raw declarations go through with_provider_tools and the application executes them. This does not imply a hosted shell.

sound_effects.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. Lyria generates music.

streaming_speech.notes: Gemini TTS streams audio through streamGenerateContent. RubyLLM.speak with a block raises on Vertex AI, because neither the Gemini nor the Cloud Text-to-Speech protocol implements streaming speech.

task_budgets.notes: Claude documents task budgets in beta on Google-managed Claude. The output_config setting and beta header go through with_provider_options and with_headers. RubyLLM has no named option.

text_intelligence.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory.

vector_store_management.notes: RAG Engine exposes corpus and file lifecycle. RubyLLM has no client for these resources. A raw retrieval tool can use an existing corpus.

video_batches.notes: The Veo and Omni model pages mark batch inference not supported. Long-running single jobs are not batches.

video_editing.notes: Google documents video editing on Gemini Omni through Interactions. RubyLLM implements Veo prediction jobs and has no Interactions route for it.

video_extension.notes: animate(extend:) sends a gs:// video or inline bytes to Veo predictLongRunning. Veo is absent from the bundled registry, so use a documented model with assume_model_exists: true. Inline bytes have unit coverage only. Omni extension through Interactions is not reachable.

verification.example: extends a Cloud Storage video through a Vertex prediction job
verification.notes: gs:// sample extended in us-central1.

voice_cloning.notes: Gemini TTS voice replication is in Preview. A replicated voice identifier goes in speechConfig through provider_options on speak. RubyLLM has no replication lifecycle, and the Chirp3-HD protocol rejects voice clone fields.

voice_conversion.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory.

web_fetch_api.notes: Not documented in the audited inventory. URL context is a tool on generation requests.

websockets.notes: The Grok Responses page documents no WebSocket transport. Live API WebSockets are the realtime row.

gaps.notes: Remote MCP tools: Only hosted Deep Research connects a remote MCP server. Chat has no route, and the recorded research response omits MCP call and result steps.
Interactions API: Only single-turn hosted research reaches the endpoint. Chat cannot select Interactions, so model conversations, function tools and other agents are unreachable.
Omni video generation, Video editing: Gemini Omni runs through Interactions, which RubyLLM does not route for video.
OCR / document parsing: Mistral OCR on Vertex AI is unreachable, because the Vertex Mistral protocol omits the OCR module.
Fill-in-the-middle completion: Codestral 2 documents prompt and suffix completion. The Vertex Mistral protocol sends only chat messages.
Manual context compaction: Claude documents on-demand compaction on Google-managed Claude. Chat#compact supports only the Responses protocol.
Responses API: Grok Responses on Vertex AI has no route. Grok runs through Chat Completions.
Music generation: Lyria runs through Interactions and predict. RubyLLM has no music operation.
Streaming speech generation: Gemini TTS streams through streamGenerateContent. speak with a block raises on Vertex AI.
Agent skills: Managed Agents attach skills. RubyLLM has no agent or skill resources on Vertex AI.
File listing and deletion: Cloud Storage offers both. The public file API uploads, finds and downloads.
File search store management, Vector store management: RubyLLM has no RAG Engine corpus client.
Fine-tuning: RubyLLM has no tuning job client.
Token counting: chat.count_tokens raises on Claude routes, although Google documents a count-tokens endpoint for them.

Dedicated transcription API, Streaming transcription: RubyLLM routes only the preview model ids to these protocols, while Google names gemini-3.5-transcribe and gemini-3.5-transcribe-live as the models.
Web search tool: The Claude alias sends web_search_20260318, while Google-managed Claude documents only the basic tool.
Image input, PDF input: URL attachments on Claude routes render as URL sources, which Google-managed Claude does not support.

Computer use, Browser use, Shell and computer tools, Context editing, Task budgets, Fast inference, JSON object mode, Guardrail configuration, Image batches, Prefix completion, Voice cloning: These work only through raw options.

providers.name: Amazon Bedrock
providers.notes: Covers Bedrock foundation-model inference on bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle, plus documented inference resources and controls. Features may require an explicit protocol, model, region or IAM permission. AWS Data Automation, AgentCore, managed agents and general AWS services are outside scope.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat reaches every route the provider declares. Claude uses the Messages API through InvokeModel, or the Mantle Messages API for bare anthropic. ids. Nova, Llama and other versioned models use Converse. Mantle catalog models use Mantle Responses or Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Converse route, response parsed into a Message.

streaming.notes: ConverseStream, InvokeModelWithResponseStream and Mantle SSE all stream through the block form of ask. The InvokeModel route decodes AWS event streams.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Recorded against converse-stream.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders output_config.format on Claude routes, outputConfig.textFormat on Converse and response_format or text.format on Mantle. GPT models on Converse also need additionalModelRequestFields.text.format.strict, which needs raw options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with schema with bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: InvokeModel route.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as Converse image blocks or Claude image blocks. Remote images on the InvokeModel route are sent as bytes, because Bedrock does not fetch URLs.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models bedrock/claude-sonnet-4-5 can understand local images
verification.notes: InvokeModel route.

pdf_input.notes: PDF attachments work on Converse document blocks and on Claude document blocks. Claude on Bedrock takes PDFs inline or through Converse, not through a Files API.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat pdf models bedrock/claude-sonnet-4-5 understands PDFs
verification.notes: InvokeModel route.

audio_input.notes: Audio attachments render as Converse audio blocks, or as input_audio on Mantle Chat Completions for Voxtral. Claude routes do not take audio.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat audio models bedrock/mistral.voxtral-mini-3b-2507 can understand audio
verification.notes: Mantle Chat Completions with input_audio WAV. The model card does not describe this request shape.

video_input.notes: Video attachments render as Converse video blocks for models that accept them, such as Nova 2 Lite.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat video models bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 can understand local videos
verification.notes: MP4 sent in a Converse video block.

thinking.notes: Message#thinking returns Claude thinking blocks, Converse reasoningContent, and Responses reasoning items, with signatures kept for replay.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Budgeted thinking on InvokeModel.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat Bedrock Nova 2 reasoning returns reasoning content blocks
verification.notes: Converse reasoningContent.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking maps effort and budget to thinking and output_config on Claude, reasoningConfig on Nova, and the matching Converse fields on other families. Each model accepts its own subset, and Nova rejects a token budget.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 preserves thinking signatures between turns when provided
verification.notes: Thinking settings and replay on InvokeModel.

citations.notes: with_citations enables document citations. RubyLLM parses Converse citationsContent and Claude citation blocks into Citation values, including search results returned by tools.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 cites PDF documents with page numbers
verification.notes: Response carries page_location citations.

tools.notes: Application tools work on Converse toolConfig, Claude tools, and Mantle function tools.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 can use tools
verification.notes: Converse tool round trip.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Bedrock::Mantle responses chat calls tools through the Responses surface
verification.notes: Mantle Responses tool round trip.

tool_choice.notes: choice maps to auto, required and a named tool on every route. Converse has no none value, so RubyLLM raises for choice: :none there. Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject forced tool use.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Sends toolChoice.tool on Converse.

parallel_tools.notes: Several tool calls in one response are parsed and answered in a single user turn on Converse, Claude and Mantle routes.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: Converse response with several toolUse blocks.

parallel_tool_control.notes: calls: :one sends disable_parallel_tool_use on Claude routes and parallel_tool_calls on Mantle routes. Converse documents no such field, and render_tool_config leaves the setting out on that route.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) sends the nova_grounding system tool on Converse for Nova 2 models and returns ServerToolCall and Citation values. AWS Web Search for GPT-5.4 and later runs on Mantle Responses under /openai/v1, in US Regions and GovCloud, while RubyLLM posts to /v1/responses unless bedrock_mantle_api_base adds the prefix.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with bedrock/amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 grounds the answer with web citations
verification.notes: nova_grounding call with citationsContent in the response.

server_web_fetch.notes: Fetch runs inside AWS Web Search on GPT-5.4 and later through Mantle Responses. Reaching it takes protocol: :mantle_responses and bedrock_mantle_api_base with the /openai prefix, because these models are documented under /openai/v1 and RubyLLM posts to /v1/responses by default. Nova grounding has no separate fetch operation. No recording covers this route.

server_code_execution.notes: Nova 2 documents a nova_code_interpreter system tool on Converse, in IAD, PDX and NRT. It has no RubyLLM alias, but with_provider_tools({ systemTool: { name: "nova_code_interpreter" } }) adds it to toolConfig.tools. Claude on Bedrock does not support code execution. AWS mentions a code interpreter for Mantle Responses without documenting the tool, and no recording covers it.

server_file_search.notes: Knowledge Bases answer through RetrieveAndGenerate, which creates a provider-managed session for the conversation. RubyLLM does not integrate that lifecycle. Inference tools on Converse and Mantle document no file search tool.

server_mcp.notes: with_provider_tools(mcp: { connector_id: ... }) reaches Mantle Responses for Lambda function and AgentCore Gateway ARNs, and completed results replay statelessly. AWS examples set require_approval: never and do not use a public server_url. Claude on Bedrock does not support the MCP connector.

verification.notes: No connector ARN was configured, so discovery and execution have no recording.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Bedrock::Mantle request shape renders ARN-backed MCP connectors and replays their completed results

prompt_caching.notes: with_caching places automatic cache points on Converse for Claude and Nova, and cache_control on Claude routes. Only eligible models and prompts cache, and models also apply implicit caching on their own.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat prompt cache round-trip bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 writes then reads the prompt cache
verification.notes: Second call reads 7358 cached tokens on InvokeModel.

cache_boundaries.notes: cache_until_here renders a Converse cachePoint or Claude cache_control with an optional TTL. Bedrock takes at most four points in one request, and Nova takes none in tools.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat Bedrock cache points caches a Claude turn that ends with Word and Excel documents
verification.notes: Cache point placed after the last block that accepts one.

explicit_cache.notes: Bedrock documents cache checkpoints in the prompt, with no separately created, found or deleted cache resource. Checkpoints count under cache boundaries.

compaction.notes: with_compaction sends the compact_20260112 context_management edit on the Claude InvokeModel and Mantle routes, with its beta in anthropic_beta on InvokeModel. AWS lists Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 for this mechanism, and the Converse API supports neither compaction mechanism. No recording covers Bedrock.

token_counting.notes: count_tokens uses CountTokens on bedrock-runtime for Converse and InvokeModel bodies, addressed to the foundation model, and /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens on Mantle. Some Claude models support only the Mantle operation.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat deferred tools with bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5 counts tokens with deferred tools declared
verification.notes: InvokeModel body wrapped for count-tokens.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint supports Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, Stable Image Core and Stable Image Ultra through InvokeModel. Size selects an aspect ratio, and each request returns one image. Nova Canvas reached end of life on September 30, 2026. Core and Ultra share the documented contract but have no recording.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::InvokeModel::StabilityImages generates an image with Bedrock Stable Diffusion
verification.notes: Returned bytes decode to an image.

image_editing.notes: RubyLLM.paint with a source image supports Stable Diffusion 3.5 image-to-image and Stable Image Inpaint with an explicit mask or the source alpha channel. Other Stability edit services, such as outpainting, upscaling, background removal and search and replace, raise an unsupported model error.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::InvokeModel::StabilityImages inpaints a local image through a Bedrock inference profile
verification.notes: Source and mask through the inference profile.

video_generation.notes: RubyLLM.animate and animate_later use StartAsyncInvoke for Luma Ray 2 with one or two keyframe images. They require bedrock_video_s3_uri, and the completed MP4 downloads from the returned S3 prefix. Nova Reel reached end of life on September 30, 2026, and RubyLLM has no adapter for it. No completed generation has a recording.

verification.notes: No job was submitted and no S3 object was written.

verification.example: signs one submission, polls its ARN, and downloads the single MP4 under the returned output prefix
verification.notes: Covers the documented request and result lifecycle.

speech.notes: Speech output on Bedrock uses Nova 2 Sonic and Nova 2.5 Sonic through InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, a voice conversation endpoint rather than standalone text to speech. RubyLLM does not implement realtime conversations.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe sends mistral.voxtral-small-24b-2507 audio as input_audio on Mantle Chat Completions and returns a typed Transcription with token usage. AWS describes the model as speech to text without documenting a transcription endpoint or this request shape. Timestamps, speaker labels and non-text formats raise, and other models do not route here.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Bedrock::Mantle::Voxtral transcribes speech through Bedrock Voxtral with typed usage
verification.notes: Successful transcript through Mantle Chat Completions.

streaming_transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe with a block sends the complete file to Mantle Voxtral and yields transcript deltas, then one final transcript. This streams output from an uploaded file, not live microphone input. A stream without a terminal stop raises.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Bedrock::Mantle::Voxtral streams a complete multi-utterance WAV transcript through Bedrock Voxtral with typed usage
verification.notes: Successful streamed transcript with usage.

diarization.notes: Foundation-model APIs document no speaker labels. Bedrock Data Automation and Amazon Transcribe are separate services.

moderation.notes: RubyLLM.moderate(provider: :bedrock) calls ApplyGuardrail on the configured guardrail ID and version, for text and PNG or JPEG attachments. flagged? reflects GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED. Scores, tokens and cost stay nil. It creates no guardrail and does not use the detect-only InvokeGuardrailChecks operation. No recording covers it, because it needs an existing guardrail.

verification.example: applies an explicitly selected existing guardrail and reports its actual verdict
verification.notes: No guardrail ID and version were configured, so the live example has no cassette.
Covers text and image verdicts, policy records and usage without a model.

ocr.notes: The inventory documents no OCR operation on foundation models. Bedrock Data Automation and Textract are separate services.

embeddings.notes: RubyLLM.embed routes Titan Text, Titan Multimodal, Cohere Embed and Nova Multimodal Embeddings models through InvokeModel, for text. Other embedding models on the platform, such as TwelveLabs Marengo, raise an unsupported model error.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 can handle a single text
verification.notes: Titan Text through InvokeModel.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding Bedrock embedding dialects bedrock/us.cohere.embed-v4:0 embeds a single text
verification.notes: Cohere dialect through InvokeModel.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: Titan Multimodal, Nova Multimodal and Cohere Embed v4 accept images, and Nova also accepts video, but embed(with:) raises on every Bedrock embedding protocol. Image fields reach the model only as provider_options merged into the InvokeModel body. On Nova, RubyLLM always renders text and AWS requires exactly one input, so an image must override it, and that path is unverified.

reranking.notes: RubyLLM.rerank calls agent-runtime /rerank with Amazon Rerank or Cohere Rerank model ARNs, follows nextToken pages, and returns original indices with scores. Usage and cost stay unknown because the API does not return them. Cohere Rerank has no separate recording.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Bedrock::Rerank reranks actual documents with Amazon Rerank and leaves unreported usage unknown
verification.notes: Top document index and positive score. Usage stays nil.
Covers pagination, repeated cursors, index bounds and JSON sources.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload stores the file in S3 under bedrock_batch_s3_uri or an explicit s3:// uri, and needs the aws-sdk-s3 gem. Converse attaches S3 references for Nova models, and Claude routes send content inline. This is S3 storage, not a Bedrock files endpoint.

file_download.notes: Downloads and metadata lookups read s3:// objects through the same file API, using any credentials the bucket admits.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch submits Model Invocation Jobs with S3 input and output. Claude requests use the InvokeModel format, which carries tools. Other models use the Converse format, where RubyLLM rejects tools and structured output. Bedrock also needs bedrock_batch_role_arn. The OpenAI Batch API on bedrock-runtime is not integrated. No recording covers these jobs.

embedding_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch accepts text embeddings for Titan Text Embeddings V2 and Titan Multimodal Embeddings G1 through InvokeModel jobs, with submission, refresh, cancellation and typed Embedding results restored to their request order. An S3 prefix and a batch role are required, and other embedding models raise. No completed job has a recording.

verification.notes: Covers the batch lifecycle with stubs, including shuffled records, errors and missing usage.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::InvokeModel::EmbeddingBatches submits, reloads and cancels an embedding batch using explicitly configured S3 resources
verification.notes: No S3 prefix or batch role was configured, so no job was submitted.

advisor_tool.notes: The Claude advisor tool page does not list Amazon Bedrock, and Claude in Amazon Bedrock lists it as not supported.

agent_responses.notes: Provider-specific row for the Perplexity Agent API.

agent_skills.notes: Claude in Amazon Bedrock lists Agent Skills as not supported. AgentCore and managed agents are separate products.

async_research.notes: The inventory documents no asynchronous research operation.

background_responses.notes: Mantle Responses documents background execution, and bedrock-runtime rejects it. Raw provider options can send background on Mantle, but RubyLLM has no retrieval, polling or cancellation lifecycle. Normal chat requests send store: false and replay local history.

browser_use.notes: Claude documents browser_toolset_20260801 on Bedrock through InvokeModel for Fable 5, Opus 4.8 and later models. with_provider_tools takes the raw declaration, and tools with namespace "browser" run the members locally. browser_state result blocks are not represented, so tab-management workflows are not covered.

classification.notes: The inventory documents no classification operation.

computer_use.notes: Bedrock documents computer_toolset_20260801 on newer Claude models and Anthropic-defined computer tools on others. with_provider_tools takes the raw declaration, and tools with namespace "computer" run the members locally with text and image results. Your application owns the environment. No recording covers Bedrock.

context_editing.notes: Claude documents context editing on Bedrock and its InvokeModel route. It needs context_management through provider_options and the beta through with_headers, which the InvokeModel route moves into anthropic_beta.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no contextual embeddings operation.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: Voxtral is served through model inference, and the inventory lists no transcription endpoint. Data Automation and Amazon Transcribe are separate services.

dubbing.notes: The inventory documents no dubbing operation.

fast_inference.notes: Converse performanceConfig.latency optimized is a preview feature for Nova Pro, Llama 3.1 and Claude 3.5 Haiku, sent through provider_options. Priority service tier is also a raw option. InvokeModel takes these settings through its own request fields, which with_headers can set. Claude fast mode does not list Bedrock.

file_management.notes: S3 offers object listing and deletion. The public file API uploads, finds and downloads, and its internal listing serves batch output only.

file_search_store_management.notes: Knowledge Bases expose managed retrieval storage and lifecycle operations. RubyLLM has no Knowledge Base client.

fill_in_middle.notes: The inventory documents no fill-in-the-middle operation.

fine_tuning.notes: Bedrock offers model customization jobs and OpenAI-compatible fine-tuning. RubyLLM does not manage either.

google_maps.notes: Provider-specific row for Google Maps grounding.

guardrail_configuration.notes: Converse takes guardrailConfig through provider_options. InvokeModel takes guardrail request fields that with_headers can set. RubyLLM has no shared setting and maps guardrail_intervened to :content_filter.

hosted_conversations.notes: Responses stores conversations for 30 days by default and continues them with previous_response_id. RubyLLM sends store: false and keeps conversation state in the application.

image_batches.notes: The batch model table lists no image generation model.

interactions_api.notes: Provider-specific row for the Google Interactions API.

json_mode.notes: Bedrock documents JSON Schema output, with no schema-free JSON object mode.

mantle_protocols.notes: RubyLLM signs for bedrock-mantle and routes bare anthropic. ids to Messages, listed Gemma and GPT OSS models to Responses, and other Mantle catalog models to Chat Completions. It posts to /v1 paths. GPT-5.4 and later are documented under /openai/v1, so they need bedrock_mantle_api_base with that prefix.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Bedrock::Mantle signed requests reaches the mantle endpoint with bedrock-mantle credentials
verification.notes: Lists v1/models with a bedrock-mantle signature.

manual_compaction.notes: Bedrock documents the compact-2026-09-04 top-level compaction parameter on InvokeModel for models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, and not on Converse. Chat#compact has no render_compaction_payload on Bedrock protocols. The request and the adoption of the returned block need provider_options, with_headers and a before_request hook.

music_generation.notes: The inventory and model catalog document no music generation.

nonchat_batches.notes: The batch model table covers chat and embedding models, which have their own rows.

omni_video_generation.notes: Provider-specific row for Google Gemini Omni.

partner_model_protocols.notes: RubyLLM selects Converse, Claude Messages on InvokeModel and Mantle, Responses, Chat Completions, and the Titan, Cohere, Nova, Stability and Luma InvokeModel formats for each model. Coverage is for these named formats, and other InvokeModel-only models fall back to Converse or raise.

prefix_completion.notes: Bedrock documents prefilling with a final assistant message on the Claude Messages format. RubyLLM has no prefix setter, so it takes an assistant message added before generating. Model support varies.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The Claude page does not list Amazon Bedrock, and Claude in Amazon Bedrock lists it as not supported.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching takes a TTL, and cache_until_here takes a per-message TTL, on Converse and Claude routes. TTLs depend on the model.

provider_server_fallback.notes: Claude in Amazon Bedrock lists the fallbacks parameter as not supported. Inference requests document no other server-side model fallback.

realtime.notes: Nova 2 Sonic and Nova 2.5 Sonic use InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream for realtime voice conversations. RubyLLM does not implement realtime conversations.

response_caching.notes: The inventory documents prompt caching but no response cache.

responses.notes: Mantle Responses runs by default for listed Gemma and GPT OSS models and with protocol: :mantle_responses elsewhere. The recommended bedrock-runtime /openai/v1 Responses path is not integrated, and GPT-5.4 and later need bedrock_mantle_api_base with the /openai prefix.

verification.notes: Successful v1/responses call.

responses_batches.notes: The OpenAI Batch API on Bedrock requires endpoint v1/chat/completions, so it documents no Responses batch.

search_api.notes: The inventory documents no standalone web search operation. Knowledge Base Retrieve queries your own stores, and Web Search is a tool on inference requests.

server_apply_patch.notes: Bedrock tool documentation does not list an apply patch tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: Bedrock tool documentation does not list an image generation tool.

server_tool_search.notes: with_tools(defer: true) marks deferred tools and adds the BM25 search tool on the Claude InvokeModel route, with the tool-search beta in anthropic_beta. Claude documents this for InvokeModel and not for Converse.

verification.notes: InvokeModel response with tool_search_tool_result blocks.

verification.notes: Streamed through invoke-with-response-stream.

server_x_search.notes: Provider-specific row for X search. Bedrock tool documentation does not list it.

shell_computer_tools.notes: Claude on Bedrock documents client-executed bash, text editor, memory and computer tools. They need raw tool definitions through with_provider_tools and an application executor. A computer or browser toolset member can use a namespaced local tool.

sound_effects.notes: The inventory and model catalog document no sound effects generation.

streaming_speech.notes: Speech output on Bedrock uses Nova 2 Sonic and Nova 2.5 Sonic through InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, a voice conversation endpoint rather than standalone text to speech. RubyLLM does not implement realtime conversations.

task_budgets.notes: The Claude task budgets page lists other cloud platforms and not Amazon Bedrock. The AWS Claude pages name task_budget only as a parameter that a compaction request or a per-turn system message cannot use, without saying whether regular requests accept it. Availability on Bedrock remains unconfirmed.

text_intelligence.notes: The inventory documents no text analysis operation.

vector_store_management.notes: Knowledge Bases manage vector stores through their lifecycle operations. RubyLLM has no Knowledge Base client.

video_batches.notes: The batch model table lists no video generation model.

video_editing.notes: Luma Ray 2 documents generation from text and keyframes, with no video editing input.

video_extension.notes: Luma Ray 2 documents generation from text and keyframes, with no extension of an existing video.

voice_cloning.notes: The inventory and model catalog document no voice cloning.

voice_conversion.notes: The inventory and model catalog document no voice conversion.

web_fetch_api.notes: The inventory documents no standalone web fetch operation. Fetch runs inside the Web Search tool.

websockets.notes: The Responses documentation describes HTTP and SSE requests and no WebSocket transport. Bidirectional streaming on Bedrock is a separate Sonic operation.

gaps.notes: Web fetch tool, Web search tool: AWS Web Search and its Fetch operation run on GPT-5.4 and later, which are documented under /openai/v1 on Mantle. RubyLLM posts to /v1/responses and selects Chat Completions for these models, so they need protocol: :mantle_responses and bedrock_mantle_api_base with the /openai prefix. Web search on Nova 2 is unaffected.

Bedrock Mantle protocols, Responses API: GPT-5.4 and later need bedrock_mantle_api_base with the /openai prefix. The recommended bedrock-runtime /openai/v1 Responses and Chat Completions paths are not integrated.
Background Responses jobs: Mantle Responses documents background execution. Raw provider options can express the request field, but RubyLLM has no retrieval, polling or cancellation lifecycle.
Code execution tool: The Nova 2 nova_code_interpreter system tool needs a raw tool definition, because the Converse alias table has only web_search.
Multimodal embeddings: Titan Multimodal, Nova Multimodal and Cohere Embed v4 images need provider_options, because embed(with:) raises on Bedrock embedding protocols.

Image editing: Only Stable Diffusion 3.5 image-to-image and Stable Image Inpaint are integrated. Outpainting, upscaling, background removal, search and replace, and the other Stability edit services are not.
Moderation: RubyLLM needs an existing guardrail and does not use the detect-only InvokeGuardrailChecks operation.

Chat batches: The Converse batch format rejects tools, as Bedrock does, and RubyLLM also rejects structured output there, which Bedrock accepts. The OpenAI Batch API on bedrock-runtime is not integrated.

Context compaction, Manual context compaction: with_compaction sends only the compact-2026-01-12 mechanism, listed for Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6. The compact-2026-09-04 parameter needs raw options, because Chat#compact has no Bedrock implementation.

Computer use, Browser use, Shell and computer tools, Context editing: These Claude features need provider-specific tool or context declarations and application-managed execution or state. Browser toolsets do not represent browser_state results.
Fast inference: Converse performanceConfig.latency and service tiers need raw options.
File listing and deletion: S3 offers object listing and deletion. The public file API only uploads, finds and downloads.
File search store management, Vector store management: Knowledge Bases expose managed retrieval storage and lifecycle operations. RubyLLM has no Knowledge Base client.
Fine-tuning: Bedrock offers model customization and OpenAI-compatible fine-tuning jobs. RubyLLM does not manage them.
Guardrail configuration: guardrailConfig and the InvokeModel guardrail fields need raw options, without a shared setting.
Prefix completion: A final assistant message can prefill on the Claude Messages format, without a shared prefix setter.
Task budgets: The Claude page does not list Amazon Bedrock, and AWS pages do not confirm that regular requests accept task_budget.

providers.name: Azure OpenAI / Foundry
providers.notes: Covers Azure OpenAI v1 and the OpenAI-compatible routes in the Foundry REST reference, plus partner models documented on Foundry, including Cohere embeddings and reranking and Claude Messages. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products. Most media operations have Azure-specific endpoint handling with HTTP regression coverage but no live recording, and they require compatible deployments.

chat.notes: chat uses Chat Completions or Responses on the deployment. Chat Completions is the default route; deployments named after gpt-5.4 or later, or gpt-6 and later, route to Responses. An explicit protocol: or azure_protocol overrides the routing.

token_counting.notes: Claude on Foundry documents POST /v1/messages/count_tokens. RubyLLM Azure has no Messages route, and Azure::Responses does not include the input-token module. The Azure OpenAI inventories document no count endpoint.

image_generation.notes: paint sends Azure image requests and parses URL and base64 images. Resource and /openai/v1 bases use the v1 endpoints with api-version preview. Deployment bases keep their path, defaulting to 2025-04-01-preview. Requires a compatible deployment. No Azure live recording covers it. Reference images raise; the /videos route is not used. The retirement schedule shows 2026-10-15 for sora-2 version 2025-12-08 while the video guide and region tables still list it. moderation.notes: The Foundry REST reference lists POST /openai/v1/moderations with OpenAI model names, but the Azure model catalogs list no moderation model, so availability is unconfirmed. RubyLLM inherits a relative moderations path that resolves correctly only on an /openai/v1 base, with no Azure spec. Azure AI Content Safety is a separate product.

ocr.notes: Foundry sells Mistral document models (mistral-document-ai-2512, mistral-ocr-4-0) as image-to-text, and Cohere documents Parse on Foundry. RubyLLM Azure has no OCR route: Azure::Cohere leaves ocr_url abstract and no Mistral protocol is declared. Azure Document Intelligence is a separate product.

chat_batches.notes: Chat Completions batches have a create, poll, results and cancel lifecycle under /openai/v1/batches, always through the Chat Completions protocol. They need a Global or Data Zone Batch deployment. No Azure live recording covers them.

embedding_batches.notes: Azure docs conflict. The Foundry batch reference and v1 enum list /v1/embeddings, the v1 prose names only chat completions, and the batch guide and Global Batch availability table list no embedding model. The batch FAQ on embeddings answers a different question. RubyLLM has no Azure embedding batch adapter.

advisor_tool.notes: No dedicated advisor tool operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. The Foundry Claude pages do not list one. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

agent_responses.notes: This row names the Perplexity Agent API, which is not an API of this provider.

agent_skills.notes: Azure documents versioned skills mounted on the hosted shell environment. A raw shell tool definition can reference them through with_provider_tools. RubyLLM has no API for Azure skill upload or versions; Chat#with_skills is a separate local feature.

async_research.notes: Azure documents deep research with o3-deep-research in background mode. Raw fields can start a job, but RubyLLM has no retrieval, polling or cancellation on Azure and sends store false by default.

background_responses.notes: Azure documents background Responses with polling and cancellation. Raw fields pass through, but RubyLLM has no retrieval, polling or cancellation lifecycle and sends store false by default.

browser_use.notes: Azure documents browser automation through the computer tool and Playwright, driven by your own code. A raw tool definition can be sent, but RubyLLM does not implement the action and screenshot loop. Limited access applies to gpt-5.4.

classification.notes: judge uses the Azure Decisions API at /openai/v1/decisions. Choice, predicate and score questions classify text and images into typed answers. gpt-6-luna is the only supported model.

computer_use.notes: Azure documents the computer tool, with limited access for gpt-5.4 and computer-use-preview in the catalog. A raw tool definition can be sent, but RubyLLM does not implement the client action and output loop.

context_editing.notes: Claude on Foundry documents context editing through the Messages API beta header. RubyLLM Azure has no Messages route, so raw options cannot reach it.

contextual_embeddings.notes: No dedicated contextual embeddings operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: The audio/transcriptions route is the same integration as Transcription, including streamed and detailed results. No Azure live recording covers it.

dubbing.notes: No dedicated dubbing operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

fast_inference.notes: Azure documents priority processing and Flex processing, selected on eligible deployments or per request with service_tier. with_provider_options can send service_tier; RubyLLM has no dedicated setting.

file_management.notes: Azure documents file listing and deletion. RubyLLM Files supports upload, metadata and download only.

file_search_store_management.notes: Azure vector stores are the file search stores, with a full create, index and search lifecycle. RubyLLM can only use a prepared store with file_search.

fill_in_middle.notes: The Foundry completions reference documents suffix only for gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, which the Azure catalogs and retirement schedule do not list, and Codestral is listed without a documented fill-in-the-middle route. Whether any deployment accepts it is unconfirmed. RubyLLM has no completions route.

fine_tuning.notes: Azure documents fine-tuning jobs. RubyLLM has no job lifecycle; calling a fine-tuned deployment works as chat. Training APIs are a scope boundary.

google_maps.notes: This row names Google Maps grounding, which is not an API of this provider.

guardrail_configuration.notes: Azure documents selecting a custom guardrail per request with the x-policy-id header, which with_headers can send. Creating guardrails happens in the portal or the management API, which RubyLLM does not cover.

hosted_conversations.notes: Azure documents stored responses, previous_response_id chaining and a Conversations API. Claude on Foundry documents message threads. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

image_batches.notes: The Foundry batch reference enum lists image endpoints, but the batch guide and Global Batch availability table list no image model. A schema enum alone does not confirm it. RubyLLM has no image batch adapter.

interactions_api.notes: This row names the Google Interactions API, which is not an API of this provider.

json_mode.notes: response_format json_object goes through with_provider_options. Structured schemas have their own public API.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row names Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which is not an API of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: Chat#compact calls Responses /compact and keeps the full history locally, resetting only later wire context. Pending tool calls block compaction.

music_generation.notes: No dedicated music generation operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

nonchat_batches.notes: The Foundry batch reference enum lists completions, moderations, images and videos, but the batch guide documents only Responses and Chat Completions input. A schema enum alone does not confirm them. RubyLLM has no adapter for them.

omni_video_generation.notes: This row names the Google Omni video endpoint, which is not an API of this provider.

realtime.notes: Azure documents the GPT Realtime API and GPT-Live. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

response_caching.notes: No dedicated response caching operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

shell_computer_tools.notes: Azure documents hosted and local shell. A raw hosted shell definition can be sent and its items are kept as server tool calls. Local shell needs a client execution loop RubyLLM does not implement.

sound_effects.notes: No dedicated sound effects operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.
