task_budgets.notes: Claude on Foundry lists task_budget token budgets in beta on recent models. RubyLLM Azure has no Messages route, so raw options cannot reach it.

text_intelligence.notes: No dedicated text analysis operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

vector_store_management.notes: Azure documents vector stores, their files, batches and search. RubyLLM has no API for them.

video_batches.notes: The Foundry batch reference enum lists /v1/videos, but the batch guide and Global Batch availability table list no video model. A schema enum alone does not confirm it. RubyLLM has no video batch adapter.

video_editing.notes: The Foundry REST reference documents video remix and edits on /openai/v1/videos. RubyLLM Azure uses only the jobs route, which has no remix or edit operation.

video_extension.notes: The Foundry REST reference documents POST /openai/v1/videos/extensions. RubyLLM Azure has no extension route.

voice_cloning.notes: No dedicated voice cloning operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

voice_conversion.notes: No dedicated voice conversion operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

web_fetch_api.notes: No dedicated standalone web fetch operation is documented in the Azure OpenAI v1 or Foundry REST inventories. Azure Speech, Content Safety, Document Intelligence, AI Search and Foundry Agent Service are separate products.

websockets.notes: Azure documents Responses over WebSocket, continued with previous_response_id and store false. RubyLLM has no WebSocket transport for Responses.

gaps.notes: Partner model protocols: RubyLLM Azure covers Cohere embeddings and reranking. The Claude Messages API on Foundry has no Azure route.
Token counting, Context editing, Task budgets: Foundry documents these for Claude through the Messages API, which RubyLLM Azure does not reach.
OCR / document parsing: Foundry offers Mistral document models and Cohere Parse. RubyLLM Azure has no OCR route.
Video editing, Video extension: The Foundry REST reference documents remix, edits and extensions on /openai/v1/videos. RubyLLM Azure uses only the jobs route.

Programmatic tool calling, Browser use, Computer use, Apply patch tool, Shell and computer tools: Raw tool definitions can be sent, but RubyLLM does not implement their client execution and output loops.
Asynchronous research, Background Responses jobs: Raw fields can start a job, but RubyLLM has no retrieval, polling or cancellation lifecycle and sends store false by default.
File listing and deletion, File search store management, Vector store management: Azure documents these lifecycles. RubyLLM Files supports upload, metadata and download only.
Fine-tuning: RubyLLM has no job lifecycle. Training APIs are a scope boundary.
Responses batches: Azure documents /v1/responses batch input, but RubyLLM registers no Responses batch dialect for Azure.
Responses over WebSocket: Azure documents this mode. RubyLLM has no WebSocket transport for Responses.
Agent skills, Fast inference, Guardrail configuration, Provider-managed fallback, JSON object mode: These need raw options or headers, with no dedicated RubyLLM setting.

Embedding batches, Image batches, Video batches, Other batch operations: Azure references list these endpoints, while the batch guide and availability tables do not confirm them. Provider availability needs confirmation.

Moderation: The Foundry REST reference lists a moderations operation, but no moderation model appears in the Azure catalogs. RubyLLM inherits an untested path that resolves only on an /openai/v1 base.
Fill-in-the-middle completion, Prefix completion: The completions reference does not establish these for a model in the Azure catalogs.

providers.name: xAI
providers.notes: Covers the public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs at api.x.ai and management-api.x.ai, documented at docs.x.ai under the SpaceXSI name. Consumer Grok, Grok Build and Grok Bot are separate products.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat uses the Responses API by default. protocol: :chat_completions selects Chat Completions, which xAI files under legacy. Multi-agent models work only on Responses.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Answers on the Responses endpoint. The spec names a retired slug that the registry aliases to grok-4.3.

streaming.notes: A block on ask streams server-sent events on Responses or Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Server-sent events on the Responses endpoint.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends text.format with json_schema on Responses and response_format on Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat #with_schema with xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: The request carries text.format with type json_schema.

vision.notes: Image attachments go as input_image on Responses and image_url on Chat Completions. xAI lists JPEG and PNG, up to 20 MiB each.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning can understand local images
verification.notes: A local image goes as an input_image data URI.

pdf_input.notes: On Responses, a PDF URL goes as input_file with file_url, an uploaded file with file_id, and a local PDF inline with file_data. Attached files turn the request into an agentic document search. The Chat Completions dialect rejects document attachments. Only the file_url path has a recording.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat document URL models xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning reads PDFs the provider fetches from their URL
verification.notes: The request carries input_file with file_url. RubyLLM does not download the PDF.

audio_input.notes: xAI takes conversational audio through its Speech to Speech realtime API. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application. The Responses and Chat Completions references document text, image and file parts only. An InputAudio schema in the OpenAPI file is not referenced by any request.

video_input.notes: The Responses and Chat Completions inputs document text, image and file parts, not video. X Search can inspect videos it finds through a tool option; that is a server-search capability.

thinking.notes: Reasoning summaries and encrypted reasoning from Responses become Message#thinking and replay on later turns. RubyLLM asks for reasoning.encrypted_content on every request. grok-4.7 always returns it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking xai/grok-3-mini returns thinking when available
verification.notes: The response carries a reasoning summary. The spec names a retired slug that the registry aliases to grok-4.3.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking(effort:) sends reasoning.effort. xAI documents low, medium and high on grok-4.5, grok-4.6 and grok-4.7, and xhigh from grok-4.6. Reasoning cannot be disabled on those models.

citations.notes: URL annotations and collections:// source references become citations, including those that arrive only in the completed stream event.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with xai/grok-4.3 searches, cites, and counts the sources it used
verification.notes: The response carries url_citation annotations that become citations.

tools.notes: Function tools work on Responses and Chat Completions. Multi-agent models reject client-side function tools.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning can use tools
verification.notes: A function_call item runs locally and its result goes back in the next request.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) sends tool_choice, including a specific function.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: The model calls the tool the request names.

parallel_tools.notes: One response can carry several function calls, and RubyLLM runs them all.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: One response carries several function_call items.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) sends parallel_tool_calls false.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning respects calls one for sequential execution
verification.notes: The response echoes parallel_tool_calls false.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) sends the web_search tool. Domain filters and image options pass as alias options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with xai/grok-4.3 searches, cites, and counts the sources it used
verification.notes: Search calls, cited pages and web_search_requests usage are all present.

server_web_fetch.notes: xAI has no separate fetch tool: browsing pages is part of web_search, which RubyLLM registers. There is no web_fetch alias.

server_code_execution.notes: with_provider_tools(:code_interpreter) sends the code_interpreter type xAI documents for Responses. The :code_execution alias sends type code_execution, which is the xAI SDK name and is not in the documented Responses tool types. No recording covers either alias.

server_file_search.notes: The file_search and collections_search aliases send file_search with options such as the collection ids. RubyLLM cannot create the collections; prepare them through xAI.

server_mcp.notes: The mcp alias takes a portable name and url plus options such as allowed_tools. xAI runs the remote tools and returns server tool calls. xAI does not support require_approval or connector_id.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat remote MCP execution xai executes a read-only tool and replays its history
verification.notes: xAI runs a read-only MCP tool, and the follow-up request replays the typed results.

prompt_caching.notes: xAI caches matching prefixes automatically, and cached counts land in cache_read. with_caching(key:) sends prompt_cache_key, which xAI treats as x-grok-conv-id. The header itself needs with_headers.

cache_boundaries.notes: xAI documents automatic prefix caching and routing keys, with no caller-selected boundaries. The deprecated Messages endpoint marks cache_control as unsupported.

explicit_cache.notes: xAI documents automatic prefix caching and routing keys, not separately created cache resources.

compaction.notes: Chat#compact calls POST /v1/responses/compact and continues from the returned compaction item. It needs the Responses protocol. with_compaction has no xAI wire option: the reference says context_management is parsed but not yet executed, so RubyLLM drops it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat compacts and continues a conversation with xai
verification.notes: Chat#compact calls responses/compact, and the next request continues from the compaction item.

token_counting.notes: RubyLLM.tokenize calls POST /v1/tokenize-text for plain text. xAI documents no endpoint that counts a full request, so Chat#count_tokens is not available. Token ids are not billed usage.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Tokenization tokenizes text with xai through the public API
verification.notes: Token ids come back from tokenize-text and the count matches them.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint calls images/generations and parses several images. xAI documents aspect_ratio, resolution and quality, which pass through provider_options. The size keyword is sent as size, a field the Images reference does not list.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image basic functionality xai/grok-imagine-image can paint images
verification.notes: The request omits size, and the response returns an image URL.

image_editing.notes: with: selects images/edits and sends JSON references for URLs and local images. xAI takes up to five images and documents no mask, so RubyLLM rejects one. Uploaded files are sent in the url field; xAI documents them under file_id.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image edit functionality with xAI reference images xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0 supports image edits with reference images
verification.notes: A local image goes as a data URI in the images array on images/edits.

video_generation.notes: RubyLLM.animate does text-to-video and image-to-video with job polling and Video results. Reference-to-video fields such as reference_images and reference_audios, and keyframes, pass through provider_options; with: takes one reference.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Video basic functionality xai/grok-imagine-video can animate videos
verification.notes: The job is created, polled until done, and the MP4 is downloaded.

speech.notes: RubyLLM.speak calls POST /v1/tts with voice_id, language auto and output_format. It returns a Speech with save and to_blob.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech basic functionality xai/grok-tts can speak
verification.notes: POST /v1/tts returns audio bytes.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe calls POST /v1/stt with a multipart file. grok-stt maps to the API name grok-voice-transcribe-2.0. Options such as format and keyterm pass through provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality xai/grok-stt can transcribe audio
verification.notes: The multipart request names grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 and returns the transcript.

streaming_transcription.notes: A block on transcribe opens the stt WebSocket and streams WAV PCM or G.711 audio, mono or multichannel. Raw Opus and other containers are not converted.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::XAI::StreamingTranscription streams transcription through the public API with typed chunks and word timing
verification.notes: Partial events, word timing and a final transcript come over the stt WebSocket.

diarization.notes: speaker_names: on transcribe sends diarize, and each word carries a numeric speaker index. xAI has no named speakers, so speaker_references and named_speakers are rejected.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality xai/grok-stt labels words with speakers when speaker names are given
verification.notes: The request sets diarize, and each word carries a speaker index.

moderation.notes: The inventory has no moderation endpoint. The guidelines request field changes how Grok writes its answer and returns no verdict; see Guardrail configuration.

ocr.notes: The inventory has no OCR or document parsing endpoint. Chat with Files searches documents through a chat request, which is not an OCR API.

embeddings.notes: The OpenAPI file lists POST /v1/embeddings and GET /v1/embedding-models with text input. The REST reference, model catalog and pricing page do not list them or any embedding model, and a Collections example names only grok-embedding-small for indexing. Availability to an API key could not be confirmed without a call. RubyLLM.embed reaches the inherited endpoint, with no spec or recording for xAI.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The documented embedding input takes strings and token arrays only, not images.

reranking.notes: The inventory has no reranking endpoint.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload calls POST /v1/files with purpose and expires_in. xAI needs its fields before the file part, and RubyLLM sends them in that order. The uri option is rejected.

verification.example: RubyLLM::UploadedFile live uploads xai uploads a PDF through the Files API
verification.notes: POST /v1/files returns the file id and byte size.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM.download returns a DownloadedFile with save and to_blob, and UploadedFile.find reads metadata. No recording covers xAI downloads.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch runs the xAI lifecycle: create, add requests, poll, collect results, cancel. Not every model accepts batches.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning answers staged chats and appends the answers to their conversations
verification.notes: Creates a batch, adds requests, polls, and collects results in order.

embedding_batches.notes: The Batch API accepts chat, Responses, image and video requests, and does not list embeddings.

advisor_tool.notes: No dedicated advisor tool operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

agent_responses.notes: This row specifically names Perplexity Agent API; it is not an API of this provider.

agent_skills.notes: The OpenAPI file lists /v1/skills endpoints to upload, list, read and delete hosted skills, and a shell tool environment takes a skills list. These operations have no descriptions, and the guides and REST reference do not say how a request uses a hosted skill. Whether this is a public feature remains unconfirmed. RubyLLM has no integration.

async_research.notes: xAI documents multi-agent research as a synchronous or streamed Responses model. Deferred completions and batches are general queues, and background is marked unsupported, so no asynchronous research operation is documented.

background_responses.notes: The Responses reference labels background unsupported. Deferred Chat Completions is a different API and does not establish Responses background support.

browser_use.notes: No dedicated browser use operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

classification.notes: No dedicated classification operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

computer_use.notes: The inventory has no computer use tool. Grok Bot computers are a separate product. The separate local shell tool type is covered under Shell and computer tools.

context_editing.notes: No dedicated context editing operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

contextual_embeddings.notes: Collections can prepend metadata fields to each embedding chunk with inject_into_chunk, through the Management API. RubyLLM does not manage collections.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe uses the dedicated stt endpoint. This row overlaps Transcription.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality xai/grok-stt can transcribe audio
verification.notes: The multipart request names grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 and returns the transcript.

dubbing.notes: No dedicated dubbing operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

fast_inference.notes: Priority processing uses service_tier on Chat Completions and Responses. with_provider_options(service_tier: "priority") forwards it. There is no dedicated priority API, and the served tier stays in the raw response.

file_management.notes: xAI documents file listing, deletion, renaming and public URLs. RubyLLM has upload, metadata and download only.

file_search_store_management.notes: xAI Collections are the file search stores, with creation, document and deletion APIs behind a Management API key. RubyLLM can query an existing collection through the hosted tool, and cannot manage one.

fill_in_middle.notes: The legacy completions endpoint marks suffix as unsupported, and xAI documents no other fill-in-the-middle operation.

fine_tuning.notes: The current inference and management inventory documents no fine-tuning job endpoint. This means no documented hosted offering, not that private enterprise arrangements are impossible.

google_maps.notes: This row specifically names Google Maps grounding; it is not an API of this provider.

guardrail_configuration.notes: A guidelines array on Responses or Chat Completions sets per-request behavior for the nsfw, violence and profanity categories. with_provider_options(guidelines: [...]) forwards it. RubyLLM has no dedicated option. xAI rejects guidelines on multi-agent models and deferred completions.

hosted_conversations.notes: xAI stores responses for 30 days and continues them through previous_response_id, with read and delete endpoints. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application, and RubyLLM sends store false.

image_batches.notes: The Batch API takes image generation and editing requests. RubyLLM.batch takes chats and embedding requests only.

interactions_api.notes: This row specifically names Google Interactions API; it is not an API of this provider.

json_mode.notes: JSON object mode needs a raw option: text.format on Responses or response_format on Chat Completions, through with_provider_options. with_schema is the public method for schemas. The xAI guides describe schemas, and the OpenAPI file lists json_object.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with params xai/grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning supports response_format param
verification.notes: Raw text.format with type json_object goes through with_provider_options and returns JSON.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row specifically names Amazon Bedrock Mantle; it is not an API of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: Chat#compact calls POST /v1/responses/compact. The returned item replaces the wire context for later requests, while the local transcript keeps every message. Pending tool calls block compaction.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat compacts and continues a conversation with xai
verification.notes: Chat#compact calls responses/compact, and the next request continues from the compaction item.

music_generation.notes: No dedicated music generation operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

nonchat_batches.notes: The Batch API also takes image generation, image editing, video generation, video editing and video extension requests. RubyLLM.batch takes chats and embedding requests only. This row overlaps Image batches and Video batches.

omni_video_generation.notes: This row specifically names Google Omni video endpoint; it is not an API of this provider.

partner_model_protocols.notes: No dedicated partner model protocols operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

prefix_completion.notes: The legacy completions endpoint continues a raw prompt on non-reasoning models, with no documented prefix parameter. The Responses and Chat Completions references do not say whether a final assistant message is continued. RubyLLM has no completions operation.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: No dedicated programmatic tool calling operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(key:) sends prompt_cache_key on Responses and Chat Completions. xAI uses it for routing, and it does not set cache boundaries. The x-grok-conv-id header itself needs with_headers.

provider_server_fallback.notes: No dedicated provider-managed fallback operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

realtime.notes: xAI documents realtime voice conversations over WebSocket. This is outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

response_caching.notes: No dedicated response caching operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

responses.notes: The xAI Responses dialect is the default protocol. RubyLLM sends store false and replays local history.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat responses protocol dialects with xai/grok-4.3 chats on the Responses endpoint by default
verification.notes: Two turns on the responses path, replaying local history with store false.

responses_batches.notes: Chats on Responses go into a batch under the responses key. Results come back as chat completions, which RubyLLM parses in submission order.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::XAI::ChatCompletions::Batches collects completed structured Responses and Chat Completions results in submission order
verification.notes: A two-row batch mixes Responses and Chat Completions requests. Both results arrive in order.

search_api.notes: The inventory has no standalone web search API. The one search endpoint, POST /v1/documents/search, searches your collections and is covered under Vector store management.

server_apply_patch.notes: No dedicated apply patch tool operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: with_provider_tools(:image_generation) sends the image_generation tool. No recording covers it.

server_tool_search.notes: The OpenAPI file lists a tool_search tool type and matching output items for deferred tool definitions, while the guides and tools overview do not mention it. RubyLLM adds this tool on Responses when a chat defers tools, with no xAI recording. Whether xAI serves it publicly remains unconfirmed.

server_x_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:x_search) sends the x_search tool, with handle, date and media options as alias options. Usage counts x_search_requests. No recording covers it.

shell_computer_tools.notes: The OpenAPI file lists a local shell tool type with shell call and output items, while the guides and tools overview do not mention it. Whether xAI serves it publicly remains unconfirmed. No computer tool is documented. RubyLLM has no integration.

sound_effects.notes: No dedicated sound effects operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

streaming_speech.notes: A block on speak streams bytes from POST /v1/tts and returns the complete Speech. Timestamp JSON mode is rejected when streaming. The bidirectional wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts endpoint, which streams text in, is not integrated.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::XAI::Speech streams speech and retains the complete audio through the public API
verification.notes: Typed chunks join into the same bytes as the complete Speech.

task_budgets.notes: max_turns limits the assistant and tool-call turns of one agentic request. with_provider_options(max_turns: 3) forwards it. It limits turns, not tokens, and RubyLLM has no dedicated option.

text_intelligence.notes: No dedicated text analysis API operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

vector_store_management.notes: Collections provide the managed vector index, with creation, indexing and POST /v1/documents/search. RubyLLM can query an existing collection through the hosted tool, and cannot manage or search one directly.

video_batches.notes: The Batch API takes video generation, editing and extension requests. RubyLLM.batch takes chats and embedding requests only.

video_editing.notes: A video attachment on with: selects videos/edits. Local files, URLs and uploaded files work, using url or file_id.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::XAI::Videos video editing and extension completes a video edit through the public API
verification.notes: The job completes and the MP4 downloads.

video_extension.notes: extend: selects videos/extensions and takes a Video, URL, path or uploaded file. Duration is the added part, through provider_options. with: and extend: are mutually exclusive.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::XAI::Videos video editing and extension completes a video extension through the public API
verification.notes: The job completes and the MP4 downloads.

voice_cloning.notes: xAI creates custom voices from a recording in the console, or through POST /v1/custom-voices on Enterprise plans, and only in the United States outside Illinois. RubyLLM has no create, list or delete API. speak accepts a voice id prepared elsewhere.

voice_conversion.notes: No dedicated voice conversion operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

web_fetch_api.notes: No dedicated standalone web fetch API operation is documented in the audited API inventory. This is a documentation-scope conclusion, not a claim that the provider or its other products cannot perform related tasks. Scope: The public xAI inference, Files and Collections APIs; excludes Grok consumer app, Grok Build CLI and management APIs. Enterprise-gated inference features remain included with their access restrictions.

websockets.notes: xAI documents Responses over WebSocket on /v1/responses. RubyLLM uses WebSockets for streaming transcription only, and has no Responses transport over them.

gaps.notes: Contextual embeddings: Collections can inject metadata into embedding chunks through the Management API. RubyLLM does not manage collections.

File listing and deletion, File search store management, Vector store management: xAI exposes file and Collections management and indexing APIs. RubyLLM implements upload, metadata and download, and querying an existing collection through a hosted tool, not collection creation or indexing or file listing or deletion.
Image batches, Video batches, Other batch operations: The Batch API takes image and video requests. RubyLLM.batch takes chats and embedding requests only.

Voice cloning: xAI creates custom voices from a recording, in the console or through an Enterprise-gated API, in the United States outside Illinois. RubyLLM has no custom voice API; speak can use a voice id prepared elsewhere.
Responses over WebSocket: xAI documents Responses over a long-lived WebSocket. RubyLLM has no Responses WebSocket transport.
Fast inference, Guardrail configuration, JSON object mode, Task budgets: service_tier, guidelines, text.format with json_object, and max_turns work only as raw request options.
Code execution tool: The :code_execution alias sends type code_execution, which is not in the documented Responses tool types. Use :code_interpreter, which sends the documented type.
Image editing: Uploaded files are sent in the url field, while xAI documents file_id for them. URLs and local images work.
Video generation: Reference-to-video fields and keyframes need provider_options; with: takes one reference.
Streaming speech generation: The bidirectional text-to-speech WebSocket and timestamps while streaming are not integrated.

providers.name: DeepSeek
providers.notes: Scope: the public hosted DeepSeek API at api.deepseek.com. RubyLLM speaks Chat Completions by default, Responses through protocol: :responses, and the Files API. DeepSeek also documents an Anthropic-compatible format at /anthropic, which RubyLLM does not use. Local model hosting, open-weight releases, consumer applications, DeepSeek Harness and third-party deployments are outside scope.

chat.notes: Chat Completions is the default protocol, and protocol: :responses selects the Responses API. Both serve deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Recorded against /chat/completions; asserts the answer, role and token usage. DeepSeek reports deepseek-flash as the serving model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat responses protocol dialects with deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash chats with reasoning text on the opt-in Responses protocol
verification.notes: Recorded against /responses over two turns.

streaming.notes: Both protocols stream. Chat Completions uses chunk deltas and Responses uses semantic events, including reasoning_text deltas.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streamed Chat Completions request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat responses protocol dialects with deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash streams reasoning deltas
verification.notes: Streamed Responses request with reasoning chunks.

structured_output.notes: Select protocol: :responses to use with_schema, which sends a json_schema text format. The default Chat Completions protocol accepts only text and json_object formats, so with_schema raises ArgumentError there. No API recording covers a schema request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses sends JSON Schema through the Responses text format
verification.notes: Checks the rendered text.format.

vision.notes: Both protocols send inline and URL images to deepseek-flash; deepseek-v4-pro has no vision. Uploaded file references work only with protocol: :responses, because the Chat Completions dialect raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for them although DeepSeek documents a file content block there.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models deepseek/deepseek-flash can understand local images
verification.notes: Sends an image_url part on Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses renders uploaded images as input_image references
verification.notes: Checks the input_image file_id part on Responses.

pdf_input.notes: DeepSeek documents no document input: Responses says file inputs are not supported, and the Anthropic format marks document blocks not supported. The Files API stores images only.

audio_input.notes: The models reference lists only text and image input modalities, and the chat references define no audio content part.

video_input.notes: The models reference lists only text and image input modalities, and the chat references define no video content part.

thinking.notes: RubyLLM parses reasoning_content on Chat Completions and reasoning_text parts on Responses, in full responses and streams, and replays them on later turns. Reasoning token counts reach the thinking bucket.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat DeepSeek thinking control returns reasoning content for effort high
verification.notes: Asserts thinking text on Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses continues a streamed reasoning conversation after a tool result
verification.notes: Asserts streamed reasoning and its replay with the tool result on Responses.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking translates effort on both protocols, and effort: :none turns thinking off. On Chat Completions it also sends the thinking toggle. DeepSeek has no token budget, so budget: raises ArgumentError. On Responses, with_thinking(false) sends no reasoning field, so the service default of thinking on applies; use effort: :none.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat DeepSeek thinking control disables thinking for effort none
verification.notes: Sends thinking disabled and asserts no reasoning in the response.

citations.notes: The Responses schema gives output_text only type and text, and no page describes citation output. Its example response shows an empty annotations array. No recording shows a web search on deepseek-v4-pro, so whether that array carries citations remains unverified. The Anthropic format ignores citations on input text blocks.

tools.notes: Function tools work on both protocols. In thinking mode RubyLLM replays reasoning with the tool history, as DeepSeek requires. DeepSeek also documents a beta strict mode on its /beta base URL; RubyLLM has no named option for it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash can use tools
verification.notes: Runs the tool loop on Chat Completions.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses continues a streamed reasoning conversation after a tool result
verification.notes: Runs the tool loop on Responses.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) sends none, auto, required or a named tool on both protocols. On Chat Completions, required and named choices return a 400 in thinking mode, so turn thinking off for them.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Sends a named choice with thinking disabled.

parallel_tools.notes: RubyLLM runs several tool calls from one response on both protocols. The Responses API always enables parallel calls.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: The first recorded response carries three tool calls.

parallel_tool_control.notes: DeepSeek offers no working control. Responses ignores parallel_tool_calls, the Anthropic format ignores disable_parallel_tool_use, and the Chat Completions reference has no such parameter.

server_web_search.notes: DeepSeek runs web_search on the server with deepseek-v4-pro on Responses, and ignores it with deepseek-flash. RubyLLM has no alias: :web_search raises UnsupportedServerToolError. Pass with_provider_tools({ type: "web_search" }) with protocol: :responses; web_search_call items are kept and replayed. The documented usage.server_tool_use counts are not parsed.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses server tools passes raw tool definitions through unchanged
verification.notes: Checks that the raw web_search definition reaches the payload. No API recording covers a search.

server_web_fetch.notes: DeepSeek has no separate fetch tool. Its web_search tool on deepseek-v4-pro also opens pages and finds text in them, counted as tool_fetch, so the same raw definition reaches it. RubyLLM keeps those web_search_call items, and does not parse the tool_fetch count.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses server tools passes raw tool definitions through unchanged
verification.notes: Checks that the raw web_search definition reaches the payload. No API recording covers a search.

server_code_execution.notes: The Responses API lists code_interpreter among built-in tools it ignores, and the reference allows only function, custom and web_search tool types.

server_file_search.notes: The Responses API lists file_search among built-in tools it ignores, and the reference allows only function, custom and web_search tool types.

server_mcp.notes: The Responses API ignores mcp tools, and the Anthropic format ignores mcp_servers and does not support MCP tool blocks.

prompt_caching.notes: Context caching is automatic with no request option. RubyLLM reads cache hits from prompt_cache_hit_tokens or cached_tokens on Chat Completions and from cached_tokens on Responses, and bills them as cache reads.

cache_boundaries.notes: Caching works on prefixes the service detects. The Anthropic format ignores cache_control, and the other formats document no marker.

explicit_cache.notes: The inventory has no cache resource endpoint. Caching is automatic, and cached prefixes clear on their own.

compaction.notes: Responses does not support context_management or truncation, and a request over the context window returns a 400. No other route documents a provider control that reduces context.

token_counting.notes: DeepSeek documents a downloadable local tokenizer and an image token calculator, and no hosted counting endpoint in its inventory. RubyLLM raises for count_tokens. Post-request usage is separate.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat #count_tokens with a provider without token counting raises a clear error
verification.notes: Checks the error on the default protocol.

image_generation.notes: The API inventory has no image generation endpoint, and models list text as their only output. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

image_editing.notes: The API inventory has no image editing endpoint, and models list text as their only output. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

video_generation.notes: The API inventory has no video generation endpoint, and models list text as their only output.

speech.notes: The API inventory has no speech endpoint, and models list text as their only output. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

transcription.notes: The API inventory has no transcription endpoint. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

streaming_transcription.notes: The API inventory has no transcription endpoint, streaming or otherwise.

diarization.notes: The API inventory has no transcription endpoint, so it offers no speaker identification.

moderation.notes: The API inventory has no moderation endpoint. A moderation key in an example response and user_id content safety handling are not a moderation operation. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

ocr.notes: The API inventory has no OCR endpoint. Reading text from a screenshot through chat is image input.

embeddings.notes: The API inventory has no embeddings endpoint. The Chat Completions protocol carries this operation, so a RubyLLM call reaches an endpoint DeepSeek does not list.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The API inventory has no embeddings endpoint.

reranking.notes: The API inventory has no reranking endpoint. The rerank_score field on Search results is a search ranking value.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload and UploadedFile.find support DeepSeek image files and expires_in, with purpose defaulting to user_data, the only documented value. RubyLLM leaves file types and sizes to DeepSeek, which accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP up to 64 MiB.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::DeepSeek::Files uploads and retrieves an image with an expiry
verification.notes: Uploads, finds and checks the expiry of an image. The request names no model.

file_download.notes: The Files API documents upload, list, retrieve metadata and delete, and no content download. RubyLLM raises an explicit error for download and marks files as not downloadable.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::DeepSeek::Files reports that stored images cannot be downloaded
verification.notes: Checks the error and the downloadable flag.

chat_batches.notes: The API inventory has no batch endpoint. Off-peak pricing is a lower rate on normal requests, not a batch API. RubyLLM raises for batches on this provider.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch .submit rejects providers without batch support
verification.notes: Checks the error.

embedding_batches.notes: The API inventory has no batch endpoint. Off-peak pricing is a lower rate on normal requests, not a batch API. RubyLLM raises for batches on this provider.

advisor_tool.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document advisor tool. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

agent_responses.notes: This row names the Perplexity Agent API, which is not an API of this provider.

agent_skills.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document agent skills. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

async_research.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document asynchronous research. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

background_responses.notes: The Responses API is stateless and does not support background.

classification.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document classification. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

dubbing.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document dubbing. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

fast_inference.notes: The Responses API does not support service_tier, and no reference page documents a faster tier. Peak and off-peak rates change price, not speed.

file_search_store_management.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document file search store management. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

fill_in_middle.notes: DeepSeek documents FIM completion in beta at /completions on its /beta base URL, with prompt and suffix, in non-thinking mode. RubyLLM has no completions operation for it.

fine_tuning.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document fine-tuning. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

google_maps.notes: This row names Google Maps grounding, which is not an API of this provider.

guardrail_configuration.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document guardrail configuration. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

hosted_conversations.notes: The Responses API is stateless and does not support conversation, store or previous_response_id.

image_batches.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document image batches. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

interactions_api.notes: This row names the Google Interactions API, which is not an API of this provider.

json_mode.notes: JSON mode uses raw options: with_provider_options(response_format: { type: "json_object" }) on Chat Completions, or text: { format: { type: "json_object" } } on Responses. with_schema on Responses is the dedicated JSON Schema API, counted separately.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with params deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash supports response_format param
verification.notes: Sends response_format json_object on Chat Completions and parses the JSON answer.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row names Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which is not an API of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: The inventory has no compaction endpoint, and Responses does not support context_management. RubyLLM raises for chat.compact on this provider.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat does not enable manual compaction for other Responses dialects
verification.notes: Checks the error.

music_generation.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document music generation. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

nonchat_batches.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document other batch operations. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

omni_video_generation.notes: This row names the Google Omni video endpoint, which is not an API of this provider.

partner_model_protocols.notes: DeepSeek serves only its own models and hosts no partner models. Its OpenAI and Anthropic formats are ways to reach those same models.

prefix_completion.notes: DeepSeek documents Chat Prefix Completion in beta. It needs the /beta base URL through deepseek_api_base and a final assistant message with prefix: true. RubyLLM has no prefix option, so pass the whole message list through with_provider_options(messages: [...]), which replaces the rendered transcript. No API recording covers it.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document programmatic tool calling. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: The Responses API does not support prompt_cache_key or prompt_cache_retention, and caching is managed automatically. The user_id parameter isolates caches between end users, and RubyLLM sends it through with_end_user.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document provider-managed fallback. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

realtime.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document realtime sessions. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

response_caching.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document response caching. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

responses.notes: The provider registers a DeepSeek Responses dialect. Select it with protocol: :responses, as Chat Completions is the default. It handles reasoning_text, images, schemas and function tools. The API is stateless, and RubyLLM sends the local transcript.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses sends the phase of a streamed answer back on the next turn
verification.notes: Two streamed turns on /responses.

responses_batches.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document responses batches. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

search_api.notes: DeepSeek documents a standalone Search API at POST /v1/tools/search, billed per successful request. RubyLLM has no operation for it, and it sits outside the chat payload, so raw options cannot reach it.

server_apply_patch.notes: The :apply_patch alias with protocol: :responses sends the custom tool definition, the only custom tool DeepSeek accepts. RubyLLM records the returned custom_tool_call as a ServerToolCall instead of running a local tool, and has no way to send custom_tool_call_output back, so the loop is left to the application.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::DeepSeek::Responses server tools keeps the patch tool alias
verification.notes: Checks the rendered tool definition.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: The Responses reference allows only function, custom and web_search tool types and ignores other built-in tools. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

server_tool_search.notes: The Responses reference lists a tool_search_call output item and the guide calls it client-side tool discovery, but no page documents how to enable it: the tools array allows only function, custom and web_search types, and defer_loading is undocumented. No recording shows one.

server_x_search.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document x search tool. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

shell_computer_tools.notes: The Responses reference allows only function, custom and web_search tool types, and ignores computer_use and other built-in tools.

sound_effects.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document sound effects. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

streaming_speech.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document streaming speech generation. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

task_budgets.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document task budgets. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

text_intelligence.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document text analysis api. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

vector_store_management.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document vector store management. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

video_batches.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document video batches. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

video_editing.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document video editing. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

video_extension.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document video extension. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

voice_cloning.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document voice cloning. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

voice_conversion.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document voice conversion. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

web_fetch_api.notes: DeepSeek documents a standalone Fetch API at POST /v1/tools/fetch that returns a page as Markdown, billed per successful request. RubyLLM has no operation for it, and it sits outside the chat payload, so raw options cannot reach it.

websockets.notes: The DeepSeek API reference does not document responses over websocket. The inventory covers Chat Completions, Responses, the Anthropic-format Messages, FIM completion, Files, Search, Fetch, models and balance.

gaps.notes: File listing and deletion: DeepSeek documents file listing and deletion, and RubyLLM has no list or delete operation.
Fill-in-the-middle completion: DeepSeek documents a beta FIM Completion API on its /beta base URL, and RubyLLM has no completions operation.
Standalone search API, Standalone web fetch API: DeepSeek documents POST /v1/tools/search and POST /v1/tools/fetch, and RubyLLM wraps neither.
Apply patch tool: The alias sends the custom apply_patch definition, but custom_tool_call output is recorded as a ServerToolCall, with no local tool loop and no custom_tool_call_output.

Web search tool, Web fetch tool: DeepSeek runs web_search on deepseek-v4-pro through Responses. RubyLLM has no alias, so it needs a raw tool definition, and usage.server_tool_use counts are not parsed into usage or cost.
JSON object mode: JSON mode uses raw response_format on Chat Completions or raw text.format on Responses.
Prefix completion: Chat Prefix Completion needs the /beta base URL and a raw message list with prefix: true. RubyLLM has no prefix option.
Image input: Uploaded file references work only on Responses. Chat Completions raises UnsupportedAttachmentError, although DeepSeek documents a file content block there.
Thinking controls: On Responses, with_thinking(false) sends no reasoning field and thinking stays on by default. Use effort: :none.
Citations, Tool search: DeepSeek shows only an empty annotations array and a tool_search_call output type, with no description of how to use either, so availability remains unverified.

providers.name: Cohere
providers.notes: Audited: the public Cohere inference and dataset APIs, with Chat v2 as the RubyLLM route and v1 endpoints where Cohere still documents them. North, Model Vault, the OpenAI-compatible Compatibility API and third-party or private deployments are outside this scope.

chat.notes: RubyLLM sends conversations to /v2/chat from the local transcript. Sampling options without a shared name, such as p, k, seed and priority, go through with_provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality cohere/command-a-03-2025 can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Answers and reports token usage.

streaming.notes: Parses the v2 event stream for text, thinking, tool calls, citations and final usage. A stream that ends with finish_reason ERROR raises a ServerError.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses cohere/command-a-03-2025 supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streams chunks through the public chat API.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders response_format type json_object with a bare json_schema. Cohere documents this on Command R, Command R+ and newer models. Chat batches reject response_format before upload.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat#with_schema with cohere/command-a-03-2025 accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: Returns parsed JSON that matches the schema.

vision.notes: Chat sends image_url blocks on Cohere vision models, such as Command A Vision and Command A+. A remote URL without a known image extension is inlined as a data URI, because Cohere resolves remote images by extension.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models cohere/command-a-plus-05-2026 can understand local images
verification.notes: Describes a local image.

pdf_input.notes: Chat v2 user content documents text and image_url blocks only, so RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for a PDF. The Parse API reference states PDF and file URL inputs are not yet supported. Mixed PDF page input on Embed models is an embedding input, not a chat attachment.

audio_input.notes: Chat v2 message content documents text and images, with no audio block. Audio goes through the separate transcription endpoint.

video_input.notes: Chat v2 message content documents text and images, with no video block.

thinking.notes: Returns thinking content blocks on reasoning models, such as Command A Reasoning, in full and streaming responses. On a tool-calling turn without thinking blocks, tool_plan is exposed as thinking and stays out of later requests.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking cohere/command-a-reasoning-08-2025 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Returns thinking text from a reasoning model.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking renders thinking type enabled or disabled, with token_budget from budget:. The wire format has no effort field, so only the toggle and the budget reach Cohere.

citations.notes: with_citations sends text attachments as top-level documents and parses typed citations, including citations of tool results returned as search results and streamed citation events. citation_options goes through with_provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with cohere/command-a-plus-05-2026 cites text documents in responses
verification.notes: Returns citations of an attached text document.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with cohere/command-a-plus-05-2026 streams citations
verification.notes: Returns citations from a stream.

tools.notes: Sends client function tools and replays their results. strict_tools has no shared name and goes through with_provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling cohere/command-a-03-2025 can use tools
verification.notes: Runs a local tool and answers from its result.

tool_choice.notes: Supports the choices Cohere exposes: auto by omission, REQUIRED and NONE. Cohere cannot force a named tool, so RubyLLM raises ArgumentError for one. Documented for Command R7B and newer models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control cohere/command-a-03-2025 respects choice: :none
verification.notes: Sends NONE and gets a direct answer.

parallel_tools.notes: Parses and runs every tool call in one assistant response, in full and streaming modes.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling cohere/command-a-03-2025 can use parallel tool calls
verification.notes: The recorded response carries two tool calls.

parallel_tool_control.notes: Chat v2 documents no option that limits parallel calls, and the Compatibility API lists parallel_tool_calls as unsupported. The calls: option on with_tool_options limits calls in RubyLLM and sends nothing to Cohere.

server_web_search.notes: Chat v2 tools are client-defined functions. The web-search connector belongs to the v1 connectors parameter, which Cohere deprecated effective 2025-09-15 and does not carry into v2. Its migration guide replaces it with a client tool.

server_web_fetch.notes: Chat v2 tools are client-defined functions. No hosted fetch tool is documented.

server_code_execution.notes: Chat v2 tools are client-defined functions. No hosted code execution tool is documented.

server_file_search.notes: Chat v2 tools are client-defined functions. Documents are supplied by the caller, and the managed connectors were deprecated effective 2025-09-15.

server_mcp.notes: Chat v2 tools are client-defined functions. No remote MCP tool type is documented. Cohere's documentation MCP server and North's connectors are not inference tools.

prompt_caching.notes: Cohere caches on its own, with nothing to request. Chat v2 reports hits as usage.cached_tokens and recorded responses show nonzero values, but the docs do not describe the cache or its pricing. A bare with_caching is accepted and options raise ArgumentError. RubyLLM counts billed_units, so cache_read stays nil: cached_tokens includes a preamble Cohere does not bill. The field stays readable through raw.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality cohere/command-a-03-2025 returns raw responses
verification.notes: The recorded response reports cached_tokens of 448. The example does not assert it.

verification.notes: Usage stays on billed units when cached_tokens is present.

cache_boundaries.notes: Chat v2 documents no such request option or endpoint; cached_tokens is only a response field. Cache markers cannot be sent.

explicit_cache.notes: Chat v2 documents no such request option or endpoint; cached_tokens is only a response field. No cache resource API is listed.

compaction.notes: Chat v2, the API RubyLLM speaks, does not support prompt_truncation. Only the older v1 Chat offers it.

token_counting.notes: RubyLLM.tokenize calls /v1/tokenize for exact plain-text token IDs. Chat#count_tokens is not implemented for Cohere, which documents no whole-request counter. Tokenizing records no generation usage.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Tokenization tokenizes text with cohere through the public API
verification.notes: Returns integer token IDs for command-a-03-2025.

image_generation.notes: No image generation operation is documented in the Cohere API inventory. Parse, Embed, Transcribe and Command vision input are separate operations.

image_editing.notes: No image editing operation is documented in the Cohere API inventory. Parse, Embed, Transcribe and Command vision input are separate operations.

video_generation.notes: No video generation operation is documented in the Cohere API inventory. Parse, Embed, Transcribe and Command vision input are separate operations.

speech.notes: No speech generation operation is documented in the Cohere API inventory. Parse, Embed, Transcribe and Command vision input are separate operations.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe posts to /v2/audio/transcriptions with language and temperature. Cohere requires language, so RubyLLM sends en when none is given. The endpoint returns text only and takes flac, mp3, mpeg, mpga, ogg and wav files. format, prompt, speaker names and timestamps raise before the request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality cohere/cohere-transcribe-03-2026 can transcribe audio
verification.notes: Transcribes an audio file.

streaming_transcription.notes: The transcription endpoint documents no streaming, and the Compatibility API lists stream as unsupported for transcriptions.

diarization.notes: The model pages state Cohere Transcribe has neither timestamps nor speaker diarization.

moderation.notes: The API reference lists no moderation endpoint. An old release note announces a Moderate beta, with no reference page today. safety_mode changes chat behavior and is a separate row.

ocr.notes: RubyLLM.ocr calls /v2/parse with one image URL or inline image. Default output is Markdown, and provider_options output_format: blocks also works. Pages normalize to OCR::Page and keep the original page hash, image and table metadata, and billed pages. The API reference accepts images only and says PDF and file URL inputs are not yet supported, although the model page lists PDF and PPT, so PDFs raise before the request. pages may be omitted or [0]; other selections raise.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::OCR parses an image through the public OCR API with markdown output
verification.notes: Markdown output with images and billed pages.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::OCR parses an image through the public OCR API with blocks output
verification.notes: Blocks output normalized to the same page object.

embeddings.notes: RubyLLM.embed calls /v2/embed for Embed v3, v4 and v5 models and returns float vectors. task_type sets input_type, which defaults to search_document. dimensions sets output_dimension on Embed v4 and newer. int8, uint8 and binary types are not parsed.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality cohere/embed-v4.0 can handle a single text
verification.notes: Returns a float vector.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality cohere/embed-v4.0 can handle a single text with custom dimensions
verification.notes: Honors the requested dimensions.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: Embed v4 and v5 take mixed text and images through the shared embedding API using inputs. Embed v3 takes one image without text using images, which RubyLLM selects for embed-english-v3.0 and embed-multilingual-v3.0; the light v3 models take the inputs path. Azure-hosted Cohere deployments reuse the same serialization. The recorded v3 request returned a 1024-dimensional vector and billed one image.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Embeddings embeds an image with native Cohere Embed v3
verification.notes: Embeds one image with embed-english-v3.0.

reranking.notes: RubyLLM.rerank calls /v2/rerank, resolves ranked text from the documents sent and reports search units. relevant_spans (Context Focus on Rerank 5) and max_tokens_per_doc go through provider_options; returned spans are readable only through raw.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Rerank reranking with cohere/rerank-v3.5 orders documents by relevance and resolves them from the request
verification.notes: Orders two documents and maps indexes back to them.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload creates Cohere datasets. purpose selects the dataset type, provider_options sets name and other query options, and the validation status is exposed. Datasets feed batches and expire after 30 days; they are not chat attachments.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Datasets uploads validates retrieves and downloads a Cohere dataset
verification.notes: Uploads, validates, finds and downloads one embed-input dataset.

file_download.notes: Original uploaded bytes download unchanged by default. Generated Avro dataset parts decode in provider part order to JSONL through the optional avro gem. Signed URLs are fetched without API credentials.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Datasets uploads validates retrieves and downloads a Cohere dataset
verification.notes: Uploads, validates, finds and downloads one embed-input dataset.

chat_batches.notes: Create, find, cancel and results use /v2/batches with batch-chat-v2-input datasets. Results keep IDs, tool calls, model and per-request usage, and failed rows become failed slots. Structured output, forced tool choice and retrieval documents raise before upload. Cancel posts to /v2/batches/{id}/cancel while the reference documents {id}:cancel, and that route has no recording.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Batches collects completed Cohere chat responses with returned IDs and token usage
verification.notes: Runs a two-request batch to completion.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Batches collects typed messages and individual failures with provider usage and returned tool calls
verification.notes: Covers failed rows and tool calls against stubbed data.

embedding_batches.notes: Uses /v2/batches with batch-embed-v2-input datasets, recorded on embed-v4.0, separately from the older Embed Jobs API that is limited to v3 models and has no RubyLLM route. Scalar and array shapes survive Batch.find and out-of-order output. dimensions is sent as output_dimension and left to Cohere to validate. Cancel shares the undocumented route noted for chat batches.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Batches collects completed Cohere embedding batches with scalar and array results
verification.notes: Runs scalar and array embedding requests to completion.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::Cohere::Batches leaves embedding dimensions to Cohere
verification.notes: output_dimension passes through the batch body.

gaps.notes: File listing and deletion: Cohere lists and deletes datasets. RubyLLM has no dataset listing or deletion; these resources feed batches, not conversations.
JSON object mode, Guardrail configuration: response_format type json_object without a schema and safety_mode need with_provider_options.

Chat batches, Embedding batches: cancel posts to /v2/batches/{id}/cancel, while the reference documents /v2/batches/{id}:cancel. The route has no recording. The older Embed Jobs API for v3 models has no RubyLLM route.
