providers.name: Mistral
providers.notes: Covers Mistral inference, hosted tools, files, batches and audio on api.mistral.ai. RubyLLM uses Chat Completions with multi-completion hosted tools by default and an explicit stateless Conversations protocol. Stored conversations, the Agents SDK harness, Vibe, and agent, library and skill resources stay separate.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat uses /v1/chat/completions by default. protocol: :conversations selects stateless Conversations for hosted tools. Model support varies; the API rejects what a model cannot do.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality mistral/mistral-small-latest can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Basic request and response on Chat Completions.

streaming.notes: Chat Completions and Conversations both stream over server-sent events. Requests with hosted tools on Chat Completions use the multi-completion stream.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses mistral/mistral-small-latest supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streamed text deltas on Chat Completions.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders response_format with json_schema on Chat Completions, and inside completion_args on Conversations. Model support varies; the API rejects what a model cannot do.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with schema with mistral/mistral-small-latest accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: The recorded request carries response_format with json_schema.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as image_url content parts, by URL or data URI, on vision-capable models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models mistral/pixtral-12b can understand local images
verification.notes: Local image sent as a data URI.

pdf_input.notes: PDF and document attachments render as document_url parts, by URL or data URI, on models with document support. Uploaded file IDs cannot be attached: the Mistral renderer has no file part. A DOCX recording covers the document_url path; no recording covers a PDF in chat.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat document models mistral/mistral-small-latest understands DOCX documents
verification.notes: Covers document_url with a DOCX file, the same content part a PDF uses.

audio_input.notes: Audio attachments render as input_audio parts on Voxtral chat models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat audio models mistral/voxtral-small-latest can understand audio
verification.notes: Local audio sent to a Voxtral chat model.

video_input.notes: The chat content schema documents text, images, documents, references, files, thinking and audio, with no video part. The vision guide and current model cards list no video input. Extracted image frames and Vibe application behavior are separate.

thinking.notes: Thinking chunks parse into Message#thinking on sync and streamed responses, and replay as thinking content blocks across turns.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat Mistral hybrid reasoning separates thinking from final content
verification.notes: The recorded response carries a thinking chunk parsed apart from the answer.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking(effort:) sends reasoning_effort, inside completion_args on Conversations. Accepted values differ by model family. A thinking budget raises ArgumentError because Mistral has no budget control.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat Mistral hybrid reasoning separates thinking from final content
verification.notes: The recorded request sends reasoning_effort high.

citations.notes: Hosted tool results work: tool_reference chunks on Conversations and multi-completion Chat Completions become Citation values, including streamed results. The documented reference chunks with reference_ids, returned when your own tool supplies sources, are dropped: their text survives and no Citation is built, though Message#raw keeps them.

verification.example: searches the web with citations and replays hosted results in a stateless conversation
verification.notes: Hosted web search returned citations, and the follow-up replayed the results without stored state.

tools.notes: Function tools render on Chat Completions and Conversations. Function results are replayed from the local transcript.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling mistral/mistral-small-latest can use tools
verification.notes: Tool call and result round trip.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) maps :required to any, or to the single named tool when only one is present. Conversations accepts :auto, :none and :required, and raises on a named tool.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control mistral/mistral-small-latest respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: The recorded request names the function in tool_choice.

parallel_tools.notes: Several tool calls in one response parse into separate ToolCall values.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling mistral/mistral-small-latest can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: The recorded response returns more than one tool call.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) sends parallel_tool_calls false on Chat Completions. Conversations has no such control and raises ArgumentError.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control mistral/mistral-small-latest respects calls: :one for sequential execution
verification.notes: The recorded request sends parallel_tool_calls false.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) on the explicit :conversations protocol. Completed hosted calls stay ServerToolCall values with raw results and usage, and follow-ups replay them statelessly. The web_search_premium variant has no alias. Mistral says the Agents SDK replaces the Agents and Conversations API and calls Agents API v1 about to be deprecated, with no date.

verification.example: searches the web with citations and replays hosted results in a stateless conversation
verification.notes: Hosted web search returned citations, and the follow-up replayed the results without stored state.

server_web_fetch.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_fetch) enables the Conversations web_search tool, whose open_url step fetches a page. The web search guide names open_url under domain filtering, without a dedicated section.

verification.example: fetches a public page through the web fetch alias
verification.notes: The recorded response shows the open_url step fetching the requested page.

server_code_execution.notes: with_provider_tools(:code_execution) maps to code_interpreter on Conversations, including streamed results, execution records, usage and stateless continuation.

verification.example: streams hosted Python execution with complete tool history and usage
verification.notes: Hosted Python ran in a streamed request with its history and usage retained.

server_file_search.notes: with_provider_tools(file_search: {library_ids: [...]}) maps to document_library on Conversations. It uses existing indexed libraries; creating and managing them is a separate row.

verification.example: searches an uploaded document through the file search alias
verification.notes: The spec prepares a library, then the alias searches it through document_library.

server_mcp.notes: The mcp alias maps connector_id to connector tools on Chat Completions and on stateless Conversations. Connectors are registered MCP servers in public preview. Completed results replay from local history. Confirmations need stored conversations and raise. No recording covers remote execution.

verification.notes: A fresh request to create a private read-only Microsoft Learn MCP connector returned HTTP 403: this API key lacks personal_and_shared scope. No connector created, permissions changed, or existing business tools invoked. Remote connector execution is not live-verified.
Stateless hosted tool rendering and result replay are covered. Storage and confirmation options are rejected before requests.

prompt_caching.notes: Mistral caches shared prefixes automatically and with_caching(key:) sends prompt_cache_key on Chat Completions. cached_tokens become cache_read. Conversations has neither the key nor cached token counts, so caching applies to Chat Completions only.

cache_boundaries.notes: The OpenAPI file gives Responses API content parts a prompt_cache_breakpoint field with mode explicit. The prompt caching guide and Responses guide describe only prompt_cache_key, and Chat Completions has no such field, so a working feature is not established. RubyLLM sends no boundary to Mistral.

explicit_cache.notes: No cache resource endpoint appears in the OpenAPI inventory. Caching is automatic with an optional key.

compaction.notes: No inference endpoint exposes a compaction control. The Responses schema fixes truncation to disabled. Compaction inside Managed Agents belongs to the Agents SDK harness, a separate product.

token_counting.notes: POST /v1/responses/input_tokens counts a request before generation, in public preview. The Mistral protocols implement no count_tokens payload, so RubyLLM count_tokens raises, and raw options cannot reach the endpoint.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint calls the Conversations image_generation tool with a chat model and returns an Image with downloaded bytes and usage. One image per request; size and count raise.

verification.example: generates and downloads an image through paint
verification.notes: RubyLLM.paint generated an image and downloaded its bytes.

image_editing.notes: The inventory and the image generation tool guide document generation from a prompt only. with: and mask: raise in RubyLLM.

video_generation.notes: The inventory documents no video generation operation.

speech.notes: RubyLLM.speak posts to /v1/audio/speech, maps voice: to voice_id, and decodes the base64 audio. Saved voice IDs work as voice:. expressiveness, phoneme_hints and conversation_history go through provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech basic functionality mistral/voxtral-mini-tts-latest can speak
verification.notes: The recorded request sends voice_id.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe uploads the file to /v1/audio/transcriptions. prompt: maps to context_bias, timestamps: :segment to timestamp_granularities, and format: is rejected. Word timestamps are not offered.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality mistral/voxtral-mini-latest can transcribe audio
verification.notes: File upload and transcript text.

streaming_transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe with a block handles the SSE events transcription.text.delta, transcription.segment and transcription.done for an uploaded file, keeping text, speaker segments, duration and usage. Live audio over the realtime WebSocket endpoint has no integration.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality streams Mistral transcriptions with speaker segments and usage
verification.notes: The recording shows segment and done events.

diarization.notes: speaker_names: [] turns on diarize with segment timestamps, and segments carry speaker_id. Non-empty names and speaker_references: are rejected, although Mistral documents speaker_references for naming speakers from clips.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality mistral/voxtral-mini-latest labels segments with speakers when speaker names are given
verification.notes: Recorded segments carry speaker_id.

moderation.notes: RubyLLM.moderate posts to /v1/moderations and derives flagged from the returned category booleans. The /v1/chat/moderations endpoint for conversations is not used. No recording covers this route.

ocr.notes: RubyLLM.ocr returns typed pages and accepts pages:. Annotations, table_format, include_blocks and confidence scores go through provider_options. Uploaded file IDs cannot be passed as the document.

verification.example: RubyLLM::OCR basic functionality mistral/mistral-ocr-latest extracts markdown from a PDF
verification.notes: Local PDF processed through /v1/ocr.

embeddings.notes: RubyLLM.embed posts to /v1/embeddings and dimensions: maps to output_dimension where the model allows it. output_dtype and encoding_format go through provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality mistral/mistral-embed can handle a single text
verification.notes: Single text embedding.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The embeddings endpoint accepts text as a string or array of strings. No image, audio or video input is documented.

reranking.notes: The inventory documents no rerank operation.

file_upload.notes: RubyLLM.upload posts to /v1/files with purpose: and expires_in:, rounded up to whole hours as expiry. visibility goes through provider_options. uri: is rejected.

verification.example: RubyLLM::UploadedFile live uploads mistral uploads a PDF through the Files API
verification.notes: PDF uploaded with purpose ocr.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM.download fetches bytes from /files/:id/content, including files generated by hosted tools.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch submits inline requests to /v1/batch/jobs for /v1/chat/completions and reads results with inline=true. A job takes one model and cannot mix chat and embedding requests.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Batch with mistral/mistral-small-latest answers staged chats and appends the answers to their conversations
verification.notes: Job submitted, polled to completion and results read inline.

embedding_batches.notes: RubyLLM.batch sends embed_later requests to /v1/embeddings through the same job API and parses typed Embedding results. custom_id preserves scalar or array shape after reloading, and errors keep their slots. The recording covers submit, find and cancel; result parsing has unit specs.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Mistral::ChatCompletions::Batches submits, reloads, and cancels an embedding batch
verification.notes: Submit, reload and cancel were recorded; the job did not complete.

advisor_tool.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated advisor tool operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

agent_responses.notes: This row names the Perplexity Agent API, which is not an API of this provider.

agent_skills.notes: Mistral stores versioned skills through the beta /v2/skills API. RubyLLM registers no skill resource protocol, and no inference request takes a skill.

async_research.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated asynchronous research operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

background_responses.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated background job operation. The Responses schema fixes background to false and responses are not stored. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

browser_use.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated browser use operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

classification.notes: POST /v1/classifications and /v1/chat/classifications run classifier models, and no RubyLLM operation calls them. RubyLLM.moderate covers only the moderation endpoint.

computer_use.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated computer use operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

context_editing.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated context editing operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated contextual embeddings operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: The dedicated /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint is used through the Mistral transcription dialect. This row overlaps Transcription.

dubbing.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated dubbing operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

fast_inference.notes: Priority Tier is selected with service_tier on completion requests, forwarded through with_provider_options. It is limited access: it needs an agreement and custom rate limits from Mistral. The served tier stays in the raw usage.

file_management.notes: Mistral exposes file listing and deletion. RubyLLM Files implements upload, metadata lookup and download only.

file_search_store_management.notes: Mistral Libraries provide managed indexing and retrieval. RubyLLM has no library creation or management API; its Files integration is separate.

fill_in_middle.notes: POST /v1/fim/completions takes prompt and suffix for code models. RubyLLM has no operation for it, and raw options cannot change the chat endpoint.

fine_tuning.notes: Mistral labels fine-tuning deprecated and not actively supported, with no removal date. Its guides keep job and pricing details, while the OpenAPI file lists only model update and archive routes and the deprecated reference link in the API index returned 404. Public documentation does not establish whether a new job can still be created. RubyLLM has no fine-tuning lifecycle.

google_maps.notes: This row names Google Maps grounding, which is not an API of this provider.

guardrail_configuration.notes: Mistral documents a guardrails request field on Chat Completions and Conversations. with_provider_options forwards it on both, and results stay in the raw response. Agent-level guardrails belong to stored agents.

hosted_conversations.notes: Mistral documents stored conversations through /v1/conversations with append, history and restart routes, and tool confirmations depend on them. RubyLLM sends store: false and keeps conversation state in the application.

image_batches.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated image batch operation. The batch endpoint list names no image operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

interactions_api.notes: This row names the Google Interactions API, which is not an API of this provider.

json_mode.notes: Mistral documents response_format json_object. with_provider_options forwards it and returns the text as usual; with_schema is the dedicated structured path.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with params mistral/mistral-small-latest supports response_format param
verification.notes: The recorded request carries response_format json_object.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row names Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which is not an API of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: The inventory documents no compaction endpoint.

music_generation.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated music generation operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

nonchat_batches.notes: The batch endpoint list also covers FIM, moderation, OCR, classification, Conversations and transcription. RubyLLM batches only chat and embeddings.

omni_video_generation.notes: This row names a Google video endpoint, which is not an API of this provider.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated partner model protocol operation. Partner models such as Z.ai GLM are served through the same Mistral endpoints. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

prefix_completion.notes: Mistral documents prefix: true on a final assistant message. RubyLLM has no per-message option, so with_provider_options(messages: [...]) must replace the whole message list with raw values.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The Responses schema has allowed_callers on tools and a program caller on function calls. The Responses guide and API description say only client-executed function tools are supported, and no guide describes program callers, so availability is not established. RubyLLM has no Responses route for Mistral.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(key:) maps to prompt_cache_key on Chat Completions; other options raise. The Conversations route drops the setting because its schema has no key.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated provider-managed fallback operation. Priority Tier falling back to Standard Tier is capacity routing, not model fallback. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

realtime.notes: Mistral documents realtime voice agents, realtime transcription and realtime speech over WebSocket sessions. RubyLLM has no Mistral realtime transport, and realtime conversations are outside 2.0 coverage.

response_caching.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated response caching operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

responses.notes: POST /v1/responses is in public preview: stateless, with text, images, files, structured output, streaming, client-executed functions and reasoning. Mistral registers no :responses protocol in RubyLLM, so protocol: :responses is unavailable and raw options cannot reach the endpoint.

responses_batches.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated Responses batch operation. The batch endpoint list excludes /v1/responses. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

search_api.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated standalone web search operation. The Search Index search route queries an index you created and belongs with vector store management. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

server_apply_patch.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated apply patch tool operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: with_provider_tools(:image_generation) works on default Chat Completions and on Conversations. Multi-completion and streamed responses keep every native message and generated attachment, without dispatching completed hosted calls as local tools.

verification.example: streams and downloads a hosted image through the default chat API
verification.notes: The hosted image tool streamed on Chat Completions and the image was downloaded.

verification.example: generates and downloads an image through paint
verification.notes: RubyLLM.paint generated an image and downloaded its bytes.

server_tool_search.notes: The Responses schema has defer_loading on tools and namespace tools, but no tool search tool, and the guide describes only client-executed functions with namespaces. Availability of deferred tool discovery is not established. RubyLLM has no Responses route for Mistral.

server_x_search.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated X search tool operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

shell_computer_tools.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated shell or computer tool operation. Sandboxes in Managed Agents belong to the Agents SDK harness. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

sound_effects.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated sound effects operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

streaming_speech.notes: RubyLLM.speak with a block sends stream: true and decodes speech.audio.delta events into SpeechChunk values. speech.audio.done is required and its usage is kept. You send the complete text once; text streamed in over the realtime WebSocket endpoint has no integration.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech streams speech from mistral
verification.notes: Streamed audio deltas and final usage.

task_budgets.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated task budget operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

text_intelligence.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated text analysis operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

vector_store_management.notes: Mistral Libraries, the RAG search-index API and the Search Index API support indexing and retrieval. RubyLLM can pass an existing library to a hosted tool, but has no index creation or management API.

video_batches.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated video batch operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

video_editing.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated video editing operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

video_extension.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated video extension operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

voice_cloning.notes: ref_audio clones a voice for one request and RubyLLM.speak forwards it through provider_options. Mistral also has saved voices at /v1/audio/voices; a saved voice ID works as voice:, but creating and managing voices has no RubyLLM lifecycle.

voice_conversion.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated voice conversion operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

web_fetch_api.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated standalone web fetch operation. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

websockets.notes: The API inventory documents no dedicated Responses over WebSocket operation. The Responses API uses HTTP with server-sent events. WebSocket sessions cover realtime audio, recorded under Realtime sessions. Scope: Mistral inference, Conversations, connector, library and skill APIs. Vibe, the Agents SDK harness and client-side Search Toolkit helpers are separate.

gaps.notes: Agent skills: Mistral stores versioned skills through the beta /v2/skills API. RubyLLM registers no skill resource protocol.
Citations: Hosted tool references become Citation values, but the reference chunks with reference_ids documented for chat are not mapped.
Classification: The classification endpoints have no RubyLLM operation.
File listing and deletion: Mistral exposes both, while RubyLLM Files implements upload, metadata lookup and download only.

File search store management, Vector store management: Mistral Libraries and Search Index APIs support indexing and retrieval. RubyLLM can pass an existing library into a hosted tool, but has no creation or management API.
Fill-in-the-middle completion: The /v1/fim/completions endpoint has no RubyLLM operation.
Other batch operations: Mistral also batches FIM, moderation, OCR, classification, Conversations and transcription.
Responses API, Token counting: The public preview /v1/responses and /v1/responses/input_tokens endpoints have no registered RubyLLM protocol.

Fast inference, Guardrail configuration, JSON object mode, Prefix completion: Mistral documents service_tier, guardrails, json_object and assistant prefix. They work only through with_provider_options; prefix must replace the whole message list. Priority Tier is limited access.
Voice cloning: ref_audio works through provider_options. Creating and managing saved voices has no RubyLLM lifecycle.
PDF input, OCR / document parsing: Uploaded file IDs cannot be attached; use a URL or local file.
Speaker identification: speaker_references: and non-empty speaker_names: are rejected, although Mistral documents reference clips for naming speakers.
Streaming transcription, Streaming speech generation: SSE streaming works. The realtime WebSocket endpoints for live audio and text input have no integration.
Prompt caching, Prompt cache options: These apply to Chat Completions. On Conversations, with_caching has no effect and cached tokens are not reported.

Web search tool, Code execution tool, File search tool, Remote MCP tools: Mistral says the Agents SDK replaces the Agents and Conversations API and calls Agents API v1 about to be deprecated, with no date. RubyLLM uses Conversations for the hosted tools that Chat Completions does not offer.
Cache boundaries, Programmatic tool calling, Tool search: The Responses schema has related fields, but the guides do not describe these features.
Fine-tuning: Mistral labels it deprecated with no removal date, and public documentation does not establish whether a new job can still be created. RubyLLM has no fine-tuning lifecycle.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.notes: The audit covers Chat Completions, Responses, Messages, Decisions, Extractions, media, Files, Batch, routing and documented server tools, for the models OpenRouter routes from other providers. RubyLLM defaults to Chat Completions and selects Responses on request; it has no Messages route. Workspace administration is sampled, not exhaustively audited.

chat.notes: Default route is Chat Completions; protocol: :responses selects Responses. Applies to the models OpenRouter routes.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Completion over /chat/completions.

streaming.notes: Server-sent events on Chat Completions and Responses, with reasoning details, usage and reported cost on chunks.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Stream over /chat/completions.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends response_format json_schema on supporting models. RubyLLM removes the strict key from the schema body.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with_schema with openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: JSON schema request and parsed output.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as image_url parts. Local files and remote URLs both work. Availability depends on the upstream model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 can understand local images
verification.notes: Local image over /chat/completions.

pdf_input.notes: PDFs render as file parts on Chat Completions and input_file on Responses. A PDF above the inline threshold can upload as a provider file. Upstream support or the file-parser plugin decides how it is read.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat pdf models openrouter/gemini-2.5-flash understands PDFs
verification.notes: Local PDF over /chat/completions.

audio_input.notes: Audio attachments render as base64 input_audio parts. The audio guide shows Responses and the Chat Completions schema carries the same part. Audio URLs are not accepted. No OpenRouter recording exercises this path.

video_input.notes: Video attachments render as video_url parts, from a URL or a base64 data URL, on supporting models. Which URLs work depends on the upstream provider. Generation is a separate operation. No OpenRouter recording exercises this path.

thinking.notes: Reasoning text, summaries, signatures and encrypted details are parsed, and reasoning_details replay unchanged across tool calls.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: Reasoning returned on /chat/completions.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking maps effort to reasoning.effort, budget to reasoning.max_tokens and the switch to reasoning.enabled.

citations.notes: URL annotations and root citations normalize to Citation objects. Web search through the server tool or a search model produces them.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat citations with openrouter/perplexity/sonar returns search result citations
verification.notes: Search result citations from a search model.

tools.notes: Function tools on Chat Completions and Responses, with streaming and multi-turn tool loops. Availability depends on the upstream model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 can use tools
verification.notes: Tool call and result over /chat/completions.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) maps to tool_choice. For choice: :none RubyLLM removes tools from the payload.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Forced tool call.

parallel_tools.notes: Several tool calls in one response are parsed and run. Whether a model emits several is up to the model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling openrouter/claude-haiku-4-5 can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: Several tool calls in one response.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) sends parallel_tool_calls false. Upstream support varies by model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control openrouter/upstage/solar-pro4 respects calls one for sequential execution
verification.notes: Sequential tool calls with parallel_tool_calls false.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) sends openrouter:web_search on Chat Completions and Responses. Results surface as citations and usage counters. Server tools are beta.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2 searches transparently, returning citations and usage counters
verification.notes: Citations and web_search_requests in usage.

server_web_fetch.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_fetch) or :url_context sends openrouter:web_fetch, and options such as allowed_domains pass through the alias. No OpenRouter recording exercises it. Server tools are beta.

server_code_execution.notes: with_provider_tools(:code_execution) on protocol: :responses runs the hosted shell, and output, exit status and billing are preserved. The docs say this tool returns 400 on Chat Completions, the default route, so select Responses. Server tools are beta.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::OpenRouter::Responses executes a hosted shell and returns its real output and billed usage
verification.notes: Runs python3 in the hosted shell through openrouter:shell. stdout 391, exit code 0 and billed usage are in the recording.

server_file_search.notes: The Responses schema lists a file_search tool with vector_store_ids, but no guide describes it, the server-tools catalog omits it, and the inventory has no vector store endpoint. GET /tools needs an API key and was not read. Whether it runs, and for which models, stays unverified.

server_mcp.notes: with_provider_tools(mcp:) on protocol: :responses invokes a remote server and records call IDs and arguments. The guides do not describe hosted MCP; the request schema and a recording do. In that recording the stream omits tool names, results and approval records, so RubyLLM requires require_approval: never and rejects approval modes before sending.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::OpenRouter::Responses records remote MCP arguments without inventing omitted tool names or results
verification.notes: Stream events carry arguments and an item ID, with no tool name or result.

prompt_caching.notes: Most upstream providers cache automatically, and cache read and write counts are parsed from usage. with_caching adds a top-level cache_control for the models that need it.

cache_boundaries.notes: cache_until_here adds a cache_control block on supporting upstream models. OpenAI explicit caching uses prompt_cache_breakpoint, which this marker does not send; provider_options cannot place it on a content block.

verification.example: sends OpenRouter the spelling its cache_control takes
verification.notes: Renders cache_control with the requested lifetime.

explicit_cache.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. Prompt caching is automatic or marked per request. No separately created cache resource exists.

compaction.notes: with_compaction adds the context-compression plugin, which removes or truncates middle messages when the prompt exceeds the context window. It does not summarize and has no threshold, so portable options are dropped with a debug log.

verification.example: maps to the context-compression plugin on OpenRouter
verification.notes: Adds the context-compression plugin to the payload.

token_counting.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. No token counting endpoint appears in the OpenAPI paths. Counts arrive in response usage.

image_generation.notes: paint uses /images and reads the reported cost. The endpoint accepts n up to 10, but RubyLLM rejects count: and reads the first image only. Streaming partial images is not exposed.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image basic functionality openrouter/google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image can paint images
verification.notes: Image returned by /images.

image_editing.notes: paint(with:) sends reference images as input_references. mask: raises because the API has no mask field; markup, its overlay for some models, needs provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Image edit functionality with openrouter reference images openrouter/google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image edits images passed via with
verification.notes: Reference image edit through /images.

video_generation.notes: animate submits to /videos, polls the job and downloads the content. Up to two with: images become first and last frames. Only unit specs cover this path.

verification.example: maps reference images to first and last frames
verification.notes: Covers payload, job status, cost and download with stubbed responses.

speech.notes: speak posts to /audio/speech and returns typed audio. Voices are model-specific, so no default voice is assumed.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech basic functionality openrouter/hexgrad/kokoro-82m can speak
verification.notes: Audio bytes from /audio/speech.

transcription.notes: transcribe posts base64 audio to /audio/transcriptions. Formats are json and verbose_json. prompt: raises because the API ignores it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe can transcribe audio
verification.notes: Transcribes the recorded fixture through /audio/transcriptions.

streaming_transcription.notes: The transcription reference documents one completed JSON response, with no stream flag or delta events. RubyLLM raises when given a block.

diarization.notes: speaker_names: [] sets the Azure and Deepgram diarization options under provider.options and asks for verbose_json. Numbered speaker labels are preserved. Named speakers and reference audio raise because the API has no field for them. Backend support varies.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::OpenRouter::Transcription transcribes a real recording with speaker labels and reported duration and cost
verification.notes: Speaker labels, duration and reported cost in a verbose_json transcript.

moderation.notes: The OpenAPI paths have no moderation endpoint. Guardrail policies, Armor and Alignment apply rules to requests and tool calls, not to arbitrary content on demand. Those configuration APIs are under Guardrail configuration.

ocr.notes: POST /api/alpha/extractions pulls typed fields from text, images and PDFs on a few extraction models, and it is alpha. RubyLLM has no integration and raw options cannot reach this route. No endpoint returns page text; OCR also runs inside the chat file-parser plugin, which counts as PDF input.

embeddings.notes: embed posts to /embeddings and returns vectors, usage and the reported cost.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding basic functionality openrouter/openai/text-embedding-3-small can handle a single text
verification.notes: Single text embedding.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: embed(with:) renders one content array with image_url, input_audio, input_video and input_file parts and returns one vector. Supported media depend on the model. Text arrays cannot be combined with attachments.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding multimodal embeddings openrouter/google/gemini-embedding-2 embeds an image alongside text
verification.notes: Text and image joined in one input.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Embedding multimodal embeddings openrouter/google/gemini-embedding-2 embeds ruby.mp4
verification.notes: Video input.

reranking.notes: rerank posts to /rerank and returns ordered results with the reported cost.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Rerank reranking with openrouter/voyageai/rerank-2.5-lite orders documents by relevance and reports the exact cost
verification.notes: Ordered documents and exact cost.

file_upload.notes: upload posts to the beta /files endpoint and find reads metadata. Files can be up to 100 MiB and belong to a workspace.

verification.example: normalizes file metadata
verification.notes: Parses the file response with stubbed HTTP.

file_download.notes: download reads /files/{id}/content. OpenRouter only serves files a model or sandbox created (downloadable: true); a file you uploaded returns 400. Container file endpoints are not integrated.

chat_batches.notes: RubyLLM submits inline requests with one model and one endpoint, then finds the batch and reads ordered results, per-request failures and the aggregate cost. It posts to /api/beta/batches, and the docs document /api/v1/batches. No batch has completed through a live recording. Public image and file URLs are documented, but RubyLLM raises on any media part. callback_url and provider.only are not exposed. Models need a batch variant. OpenRouter has no cancel operation.

advisor_tool.notes: Pass a raw { type: "openrouter:advisor", parameters: { model: ... } } hash to with_provider_tools. RubyLLM forwards it and has no alias or typed advisor result. Available on Chat Completions, Responses and Messages.

agent_responses.notes: This row names Perplexity's Agent API. It is not a capability of this provider.

agent_skills.notes: The Messages response schema carries a container object with a skills list. No guide documents uploading or attaching skills, and the request schema has no such field. The Agent SDK skills example runs on the client. Whether skills can be attached stays unverified.

async_research.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. Long-running research examples in the Agent SDK run on the client. /videos and /batches are the only asynchronous job APIs.

background_responses.notes: The Responses schema accepts background, but no guide describes it, and POST /responses is the only documented Responses route, so nothing retrieves or cancels a job. Whether the flag does anything stays unverified.

browser_use.notes: The Responses schema defines an openrouter:browser_use output item. The server-tools catalog does not list that tool and no guide describes it. GET /tools needs an API key and was not read.

classification.notes: judge sends choice, probability and score questions to /api/alpha/decisions and returns typed answers with probabilities on decision models such as Jev. The route is alpha. Custom Classifiers, the separate workspace feature that tags logged generations, are configured outside RubyLLM.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::OpenRouter::Judgments with the Decisions API judges all three question types through the compact DSL
verification.notes: A choice question returns one label with a probability for each.

computer_use.notes: The Responses schema lists a computer_use_preview tool, but the server-tools catalog omits it and no guide establishes a working upstream integration. Whether it runs stays unverified.

context_editing.notes: The Messages request schema has context_management with edits, in Anthropic's shape. No guide describes it or says which models honor it. RubyLLM has no Messages route on this provider, so it could not reach this field anyway.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. The embeddings endpoint takes input_type and has no document-context field.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: POST /audio/transcriptions is a dedicated JSON and multipart endpoint. RubyLLM uses the JSON form.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Transcription basic functionality openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe can transcribe audio
verification.notes: Transcribes the recorded fixture through /audio/transcriptions.

dubbing.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this.

fast_inference.notes: service_tier priority (alias fast) on a request is passed through with_provider_options, and RubyLLM has no speed API. The :nitro model variant also favors throughput. Support and billing vary by model.

file_management.notes: GET /files and DELETE /files/{id} exist. RubyLLM implements upload, metadata lookup and download only.

file_search_store_management.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. The OpenAPI paths have no vector or file-search store route.

fill_in_middle.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. The OpenAPI paths list no /completions route and no suffix parameter.

fine_tuning.notes: OpenRouter routes to public and private endpoints and has no training job API. Tuning at an upstream provider is outside this inventory.

google_maps.notes: This row names Google Maps grounding. The inventory and the web-search guide do not mention it.

guardrail_configuration.notes: /guardrails and its assignment routes create and assign policies for budgets, model access and content moderation. RubyLLM does not manage them. Request routing preferences do not replace this administrative API.

hosted_conversations.notes: The Responses guide says requests are stateless: store: true and a non-null previous_response_id return 400. Agent SDK conversation helpers run on the client.

image_batches.notes: The Batch API returns text and embeddings only and rejects image output. Image URLs are accepted as input to chat requests, which is the chat batches row.

interactions_api.notes: This row names Google's Interactions API. It is not a capability of this provider.

json_mode.notes: response_format { type: "json_object" } goes through with_provider_options on supporting models. with_schema is the separate JSON schema operation.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row names Bedrock Mantle protocols. It is not a capability of this provider.

manual_compaction.notes: The Responses schema defines a compaction_trigger input item and compaction output items, but no guide documents them or says which models honor them, and there is no compact route. RubyLLM has no integration for this item here.

music_generation.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. Seed Audio prompts describe speech, sound effects, ambience or a scene; the guide does not cover music.

nonchat_batches.notes: Batches cover Chat Completions, Responses, Messages and embeddings. No other operation can be batched.

omni_video_generation.notes: input_references takes image, audio and video assets; audio and video are honored by providers such as BytePlus Seedance generation 2 and newer. animate maps only first and last frames, so references go through provider_options.

verification.notes: provider_options reach the video payload.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. /messages is an Anthropic-shaped route over any model, not a publisher-specific protocol for partner models.

prefix_completion.notes: A final assistant message is continued on models that allow it; newer Claude models reject it. Chat#complete treats a trailing assistant message as answered and sends nothing, so the messages array has to go through with_provider_options.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: Responses function tools accept allowed_callers with a programmatic value, in the schema only. The one guide that names the field, Advisor, says it is ignored there. Whether any model honors it stays unverified.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching maps ttl to cache_control. Other options raise; prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_options go through with_provider_options.

verification.example: sends OpenRouter the spelling its cache_control takes
verification.notes: Renders cache_control with the requested lifetime.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The models list and provider preferences go through with_provider_options. Chat#with_fallbacks is RubyLLM's own client-side feature.

realtime.notes: The inventory documents HTTP and SSE only. Agent SDK streaming and microphone examples run on the client.

response_caching.notes: The X-OpenRouter-Cache header goes through with_headers. This whole-response cache is separate from prompt caching.

responses.notes: protocol: :responses selects the OpenRouter Responses dialect, while ordinary chats stay on Chat Completions. Hosted output, reasoning, citations, reported cost and usage are normalized. Judgments keep their Decisions route.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::OpenRouter::Responses executes a hosted shell and returns its real output and billed usage
verification.notes: Runs python3 in the hosted shell through openrouter:shell. stdout 391, exit code 0 and billed usage are in the recording.

responses_batches.notes: RubyLLM submits inline requests with one model and one endpoint, then finds the batch and reads ordered results, per-request failures and the aggregate cost. It posts to /api/beta/batches, and the docs document /api/v1/batches. No batch has completed through a live recording. A chat on protocol: :responses renders /v1/responses rows, and unit specs cover reading those results. Media parts raise, and callback_url and provider.only are not exposed.

verification.notes: Fresh actual API probes saved as observed model/status/error tuples, not a passing VCR batch test No batch ID returned, no resources created; Catalog and RubyLLM registry confirmed the explicit :batch variant before its one submission; Stopped submissions after the catalog contradiction; no brute-force model guessing Observed provider limitation: [{"model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "status": 400, "error": "Model 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5' does not have a :batch endpoint."}, {"model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small", "endpoint": "/v1/embeddings", "status": 400, "error": "Model 'openai/text-embedding-3-small' does not have a :batch endpoint."}, {"model": "openai/gpt-4.1-nano:batch", "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions", "status": 400, "error": "Model 'openai/gpt-4.1-nano:batch' does not have a :batch endpoint."}]
Documented request/result contract and protocol regression coverage; no completed live batch or patch execution claimed.

search_api.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. Search exists only as a server tool during generation.

server_apply_patch.notes: with_provider_tools(:apply_patch) on protocol: :responses declares the tool, and output items are kept. OpenRouter validates the diff but never applies it: the application must return apply_patch_call_output, and RubyLLM has no patch execution or result lifecycle. The docs say Chat Completions does not support this tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: with_provider_tools(:image_generation) sends openrouter:image_generation, with options passed through the alias. The image URL goes to the model, so results reach you through its message. No OpenRouter recording exercises it.

server_tool_search.notes: with_tools(defer: true) on protocol: :responses sends defer_loading with a bare tool_search tool. The docs and request schema only list openrouter:tool_search, RubyLLM has no alias for it, and no recording exercises this route. On Chat Completions, RubyLLM runs its own client-side tool_search instead of the server tool.

server_x_search.notes: with_provider_tools(web_search: { parameters: { x_search: {} } }) passes the documented opt-in through the alias. It applies only to native search on SpaceXAI models, and X results bill per item. No recording exercises it.

shell_computer_tools.notes: with_provider_tools(:shell) or :code_execution on protocol: :responses runs the hosted shell, and RubyLLM preserves action, output and exit status. openrouter:bash is Messages only, which RubyLLM does not route to, and no interactive desktop tool is documented.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Protocols::OpenRouter::Responses executes a hosted shell and returns its real output and billed usage
verification.notes: Runs python3 in the hosted shell through openrouter:shell. stdout 391, exit code 0 and billed usage are in the recording.

sound_effects.notes: speak with Seed Audio 1.0 and no voice treats the input as a prompt, which can describe sound effects or ambience. There is no dedicated operation, this applies to that model family only, and no recording exercises it.

streaming_speech.notes: A block on speak yields SpeechChunk bytes as /audio/speech returns its raw byte stream, then returns the complete Speech.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Speech streams speech from openrouter
verification.notes: Binary chunks join to the complete Speech.

task_budgets.notes: max_tool_calls and stop_server_tools_when bound the server-tool loop and go through with_provider_options. RubyLLM has no shared API for them.

text_intelligence.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. No route returns intents, topics or sentiment. Decisions questions count under Classification, and Extractions under OCR / document parsing.

vector_store_management.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. The OpenAPI paths have no vector store route.

video_batches.notes: The Batch API returns text and embeddings only. Video output is not batched.

video_editing.notes: Video input_references and previous_job_id ("edit or extend") go through provider_options on supporting models. animate has no editing argument, and exact transformations are model-specific.

video_extension.notes: previous_job_id on /videos names a completed job to edit or extend, on models that support continuation; only the reference describes it. It goes through provider_options, and animate has no extend argument.

voice_cloning.notes: input_references with audio clips clone a voice per request on supporting endpoints. They go through speak provider_options, with no shared voice-reference argument and no voice resource to manage.

voice_conversion.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this.

web_fetch_api.notes: The audited inference, server-tool, media, Files and Batch inventory documents no operation for this. Fetching exists only as a server tool during generation.

websockets.notes: The inventory documents HTTP and SSE. The Codex Desktop guide says to leave Responses WebSocket support off for OpenRouter.

gaps.notes: Chat batches, Embedding batches, Responses batches: RubyLLM posts to /api/beta/batches while the docs document /api/v1/batches, and no batch has completed through a live recording. Image and file URLs on chat and Responses batches raise. callback_url and provider.only are not exposed. OpenRouter has no cancel operation.
Remote MCP tools: The stream in the recording omits tool names, results and approval records, so RubyLLM keeps call IDs and arguments only and requires require_approval: never.
Apply patch tool: OpenRouter validates the diff and the application applies it. RubyLLM declares the tool but has no execution or apply_patch_call_output lifecycle.
Tool search: Deferred tools on Responses send a bare tool_search tool, while the docs and schema list openrouter:tool_search. RubyLLM has no alias for it and no recording covers the route.
OCR / document parsing: The alpha Extractions route returns typed fields from images and PDFs, and RubyLLM has no integration for it.
File listing and deletion: RubyLLM implements upload, metadata lookup and download, not GET /files or DELETE /files/{id}.
Guardrail configuration: RubyLLM does not create or assign workspace guardrail policies.
Advisor tool, Task budgets: These need a raw tool hash and request fields. RubyLLM has no alias or budget API for the server-tool loop.
Fast inference: service_tier goes through provider options, with no shared speed API.
JSON object mode: response_format json_object goes through provider options.
Omni video generation, Video editing, Video extension: input_references and previous_job_id go through provider options.
Prefix completion: Chat#complete sends nothing after a trailing assistant message, so the messages array goes through provider options.
Provider-managed fallback: The models list and routing preferences go through provider options.
Response caching: The cache header goes through with_headers.
Voice cloning: Reference clips go through speech provider options.
Image generation: The API accepts n up to 10. RubyLLM rejects count: and reads the first image only.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.notes: Covers the Agent API, which is the default chat route and runs statelessly, plus embeddings, generated files, the Orchestrator API (formerly Router, in private preview) and legacy Sonar, whose support ended on September 27, 2026 while synchronous requests keep working. Search, Decisions, Batch and Files are documented with no RubyLLM integration.

server_code_execution.notes: The Agent API documents the sandbox tool on stateless requests. It takes with_provider_tools({ type: "sandbox" }). The inherited code_execution alias renders code_interpreter, which is not in Perplexity's tool list.

server_file_search.notes: The Agent API tools overview and Tool schema list no file_search type. The inherited RubyLLM alias has nothing to reach. Documents go to the model as input_file, without a search tool.

server_mcp.notes: with_provider_tools(mcp: { url:, name: }) renders the documented mcp tool with server_url and server_label, and calls run without approval by default. Approvals are documented with previous_response_id and RubyLLM drops mcp_approval_request items on replay, so require_approval is unverified. Connectors take raw definitions. No recording covers MCP.

Orchestrator Messages cache_control is not reachable. Orchestrator, formerly Router, is in private preview and requires protocol: :router_chat_completions. RubyLLM posts to the /router/v1 base, which Perplexity keeps working alongside /orchestrator/v1. The configured account gets HTTP 403, so no successful Orchestrator inference is recorded.

compaction.notes: No request control is documented. The xhigh effort level compacts context inside its own run as a fixed setting outside the request schema. with_compaction is dropped with a debug log. Orchestrator Messages accepts context_management and ignores it.

token_counting.notes: The Orchestrator Messages specification has CountMessageTokensRequest and Response components describing POST /orchestrator/v1/messages/count_tokens, but its paths list only /orchestrator/v1/messages and the Orchestrator guide omits token counting. The Agent API and Chat Completions references have no such endpoint. Availability remains unverified, and RubyLLM has no route for it.

image_generation.notes: The image_search tool and Sonar image results retrieve existing images. The Agent, Orchestrator and Sonar references document no image generation or editing operation.

image_editing.notes: The image_search tool and Sonar image results retrieve existing images. The Agent, Orchestrator and Sonar references document no image generation or editing operation.

video_generation.notes: Sonar can return found videos, which is retrieval. The Agent, Orchestrator and Sonar references document no video generation operation.

speech.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

transcription.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

diarization.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

moderation.notes: The references document no moderation operation. Safety identifiers attribute policy violations to an end user and do not classify content.

ocr.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

embeddings.notes: RubyLLM.embed posts to /v1/embeddings and decodes base64 signed int8 vectors, with custom dimensions. Binary quantization is not decoded.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The Embeddings API takes text only: standard and contextualized embeddings have no image input.

reranking.notes: No rerank endpoint is documented. A cookbook ranks sentences through Decisions API probabilities, which is application code over another operation.

file_upload.notes: POST /v1/files takes JSONL batch input with purpose=batch only. RubyLLM.upload raises for Perplexity. Agent API documents do not use file ids.

file_download.notes: RubyLLM::UploadedFile.find and RubyLLM.download take a response_id/files/file_id identifier for files an Agent API run produced. Batch output through /v1/files/{file_id}/content is not reachable. No generation recording exists.

chat_batches.notes: POST /v1/batches runs Agent API requests from a JSONL file on a 24 hour window, for every organization except zero data retention ones. Perplexity declares no batch protocol, so RubyLLM.batch raises.

embedding_batches.notes: Perplexity Batch API accepts only /v1/responses lines, so it has no batch for this operation. Multiple inputs to embed run synchronously.

advisor_tool.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

agent_responses.notes: The default chat protocol, run statelessly: store:false, the whole conversation each turn, no previous_response_id. Covers effort levels, provider/model ids, streaming, function tools, JSON Schema output, the web_search tool and search_results citations. Replayed turns drop search_results and fetch_url_results, which Perplexity rejects as input. Cost uses the reported total, which includes tool fees. RubyLLM selects levels through the deprecated preset field, and its list omits ultra. Documents are rejected before sending. Stored responses and previous_response_id chaining stay outside RubyLLM coverage.

agent_skills.notes: The Agent API skills field takes built-in, inline and custom skills, and with_provider_options(skills:) forwards it. Selecting a skill enables the sandbox tool. RubyLLM does not manage /v1/skills resources.

async_research.notes: Perplexity ended asynchronous Sonar requests when Sonar support ended on September 27, 2026, and points them to Agent API background mode. with_provider_options(background: true) can submit a run, but RubyLLM has no polling, retrieval or cancellation, so the job cannot be completed.

background_responses.notes: POST /v1/agent takes background, with GET /v1/agent/{id} and cancel. The request field passes through with_provider_options, but RubyLLM has no polling, retrieval or cancellation lifecycle and sends store:false.

browser_use.notes: The Working with Files page and Agent API schema say browser tools are unavailable with documents, including when an effort level enables one, but the tools overview and Tool schema list no browser tool. Whether it is a usable request feature remains unverified.

classification.notes: POST /v1/decisions answers yes/no, choice and score questions with probabilities, for classifying and routing. It takes text, JSON or images. Perplexity registers no judgment protocol, so RubyLLM.judge cannot reach it.

computer_use.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

context_editing.notes: Orchestrator Messages accepts context_management, and its contract says it is ignored and context edits are not applied. The Agent API has no such control.

contextual_embeddings.notes: POST /v1/contextualizedembeddings takes nested document chunks and returns nested groups. RubyLLM.embed posts only to /v1/embeddings.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

file_management.notes: /v1/files lists, retrieves and deletes batch files, and GET /v1/agent/{id}/files lists a response's files. RubyLLM exposes no listing or deletion for Perplexity.

file_search_store_management.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

image_batches.notes: Perplexity Batch API accepts only /v1/responses lines, so it has no batch for this operation.

RubyLLM posts to the /router/v1 base, which Perplexity keeps working alongside /orchestrator/v1. The configured account gets HTTP 403, so no successful Orchestrator inference is recorded.

prefix_completion.notes: The Agent, Orchestrator, Search, Embeddings, Decisions, Batch, Files and legacy Sonar references document no operation for this. Perplexity Computer and arbitrary code running in a sandbox are not counted as separate inference endpoints.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(key:, ttl:, mode:) renders prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_options through protocol: :router_chat_completions. The Agent API accepts prompt_cache_key in its frozen configurations, and RubyLLM sends it there too. Orchestrator Messages cache_control is not reachable. Orchestrator, formerly Router, is in private preview and requires protocol: :router_chat_completions. RubyLLM posts to the /router/v1 base, which Perplexity keeps working alongside /orchestrator/v1. The configured account gets HTTP 403, so no successful Orchestrator inference is recorded.

providers.name: Deepgram
providers.notes: This covers speech generation, transcription, Text Intelligence and Deepgram LLMs on /v1/think, which is in Early Access. RubyLLM integrates Aura speech and Nova transcription, including streaming output. Voice Agent conversations are outside this release; their documented offerings remain listed separately. Account, project and billing administration are outside scope.

chat.notes: Deepgram LLMs on POST /v1/think are in Early Access for enrolled contract customers. The stateless endpoint follows the Chat Completions structure and takes the full history on each request. RubyLLM declares no chat operation for Deepgram. Voice Agent also offers conversations, which are outside RubyLLM 2.0 coverage.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders response_format with a JSON Schema, which Ollama applies on /v1/chat/completions. Ollama's structured outputs page says its cloud does not support the feature; this cell covers the local server.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as base64 data URIs in image_url parts. Ollama does not accept image URLs, so RubyLLM downloads a remote image and sends its bytes. The model must support vision.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models ollama/gemma4 can understand local images
verification.notes: Base64 image sent to a local vision model.

pdf_input.notes: The audited Ollama native and compatibility APIs document no PDF chat input, and the Anthropic compatibility page lists PDF document blocks as unsupported. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for PDF attachments.

audio_input.notes: Audio attachments render as input_audio parts with base64 data and a format. Released v0.40.15 parses that part on /v1/chat/completions. The compatibility page does not list it, and only audio-capable models accept it. No Ollama recording covers this path.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Ollama::Media.render_content encodes audio attachments in the released Ollama input_audio format
verification.notes: Covers the rendered request only.

video_input.notes: No dedicated video input operation is documented in the audited Ollama native and compatibility APIs.

thinking.notes: Ollama returns thinking in the reasoning field of /v1/chat/completions responses and deltas, and RubyLLM exposes it as thinking. Thinking-capable models only.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking ollama/qwen3 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: The response carries a reasoning field beside the answer.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking(effort:) renders reasoning_effort, which Ollama maps to model-defined names and compatibility aliases. Ollama has no token budgets, so budget: raises ArgumentError. Which values apply depends on the model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Ollama::Chat.render_payload raises for a thinking budget
verification.notes: Effort rendering and the budget error, without a live server.

citations.notes: The audited Ollama native and compatibility APIs document no citations, and the Anthropic compatibility page lists citations blocks as unsupported.

tools.notes: Function tools render in the Chat Completions format, on tool-capable models.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling ollama/qwen3 can use tools
verification.notes: Tool call and follow-up turn.

tool_choice.notes: The compatibility page marks tool_choice unsupported on /v1/chat/completions and on the Anthropic route, and the v0.40.15 request struct has no such field. RubyLLM serializes a choice through shared Chat Completions code, but Ollama does not act on it.

parallel_tools.notes: RubyLLM parses several tool calls from one response. Whether a model returns several depends on the model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling ollama/qwen3 can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: The recorded response holds three calls.

parallel_tool_control.notes: Ollama's OpenAI-compatible chat request has neither tool_choice nor parallel_tool_calls, in the docs or in the v0.40.15 request struct. No request control limits the number of calls.

server_web_search.notes: Ollama executes a built-in web_search tool on /v1/responses and the Anthropic route, for signed-in local servers. The cloud API does not offer it on /v1/responses. RubyLLM registers only Chat Completions for Ollama and has no web search alias, and raw tool definitions cannot reach that route.

speech.notes: RubyLLM.speak posts to /v1/audio/speech. Pass a voice the model lists, or default: without one RubyLLM sends alloy, which Ollama rejects with a 400. Ollama returns WAV unless asked for pcm, so pass format: 'wav' for a correctly labeled result. Other formats, speeds and instructions return a 400. The endpoint arrived in v0.40.8, and Phonon needs v0.40.9 or later. No Ollama recording covers this path.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe posts to /v1/audio/transcriptions with model, file, language, prompt, temperature and response_format. Ollama accepts WAV uploads, up to 512 MB and 2 hours, on models with audio input. It returns json, text or verbose_json with segments, and ignores timestamp_granularities. No Ollama recording covers this path. RubyLLM has no operation for the separate /v1/audio/translations route.

streaming_transcription.notes: A block on transcribe sends stream=true and reads the transcript.text.delta and transcript.text.done events Ollama documents. No Ollama recording covers this path.

diarization.notes: Ollama documents no speaker labels. verbose_json returns one segment per transcribed piece of audio, without a speaker.

The embed reference does not describe it. embed(with:) raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for Ollama; provider_options: { input: { ... } } replaces the input and forwards the object.
