providers.name: Meta
providers.notes: Covers the Meta Model API at api.meta.ai/v1 with Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, Muse Image, and Muse Voice Transcribe. RubyLLM declares its Responses format only. Muse Code, the open-weight models, and SAM segmentation are outside these rows.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat reaches Muse Wonder and Muse Spark through the Responses API, the format Meta recommends. Runs stateless with store false. Meta also serves Chat Completions and Messages, which RubyLLM does not declare for this provider.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: A recorded conversation through POST /v1/responses with store false.

streaming.notes: Server-sent events from POST /v1/responses, including function call arguments and usage on the final event.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Recorded server-sent events assembled into a message.

structured_output.notes: with_schema renders text.format with json_schema, which Meta constrains during decoding. Recursive schemas return HTTP 400, and tool search cannot be combined with a schema.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat #with_schema with meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: The request carries text.format with json_schema.

vision.notes: Images travel as input_image parts. The Meta dialect always sends them inline as data URIs, including remote images, because Meta refuses to fetch many remote images. Up to 50 images per request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor can understand local images
verification.notes: A local image sent as input_image.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta sends remote images inline, because Meta refuses to fetch many of them
verification.notes: Remote images travel as data URIs.

pdf_input.notes: PDFs travel as input_file parts: inline as file_data, or by file_url when the attachment is a URL. Meta reads text from the first 100 pages and images from the first 50.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat document URL models meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor reads PDFs the provider fetches from their URL
verification.notes: A PDF URL sent as input_file with file_url, fetched by Meta.

audio_input.notes: Meta takes input_audio parts (MP3 and WAV) on Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, and calls audio on Muse Spark 1.3 not fully supported. An audio attachment raises UnsupportedAttachmentError on the Responses protocol. with_provider_options(input: ...) forwards provider-shaped items, replacing the rendered input.

video_input.notes: Meta takes input_video parts by URL, data URL, or file ID, and input_file by file ID, for MP4. A video attachment raises UnsupportedAttachmentError on the Responses protocol. with_provider_options(input: ...) forwards provider-shaped items, replacing the rendered input.

thinking.notes: Responses return reasoning items whose encrypted content RubyLLM keeps as the thinking signature and replays across turns. Meta never returns raw reasoning as text. A readable summary comes back only when requested, with with_thinking display: :summarized, and may be empty.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor returns thinking when available
verification.notes: The response carries a reasoning item with encrypted content.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor preserves thinking signatures between turns when provided
verification.notes: The encrypted reasoning is replayed on the next turn.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking(effort:) renders reasoning.effort, from minimal to max. Meta rejects none, so reasoning cannot be turned off, and max is not available on muse-spark-1.3-contributor.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta chat sets the reasoning effort
verification.notes: with_thinking(effort: :max) renders reasoning.effort.

citations.notes: Web search answers carry url_citation annotations with offsets, which RubyLLM parses into Message citations.

tools.notes: RubyLLM tools render as flat function tools, with function_call and function_call_output items replayed statelessly. Generated arguments are not guaranteed to match the schema.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor can use tools
verification.notes: A function call and its result round trip.

tool_choice.notes: The tool_choice parameter accepts only auto, the default. Meta returns HTTP 400 for none, required, and named functions, so with_tool_options(choice:) reaches the API and Meta rejects it.

parallel_tools.notes: The model can return several function_call items in one response, and RubyLLM runs each one.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: Several function_call items in one response.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) renders parallel_tool_calls false. The flag applies only with function tools.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) renders the web_search tool and asks for its sources. Options such as user_location and search_context_size pass through the alias. Billed per 1,000 queries on top of tokens. Muse Image rejects this tool and searches by itself.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat web search with meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor searches, returns the sources, and replays them
verification.notes: A web_search tool, its sources, and a replayed second turn.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta chat grounds answers in web search, and refuses other provider tools
verification.notes: The web_search alias renders; code_execution raises.

server_web_fetch.notes: The Responses tool union lists function, computer, web search, and tool search. Opening a page is an internal step of web_search, not a separate tool.

server_code_execution.notes: Tool calling names web_search and tool_search as the built-in tools. Code execution means a function tool the application runs in its own sandbox. Muse Image runs code internally, which is not a tool for callers.

server_file_search.notes: The Responses tool union has no file search tool. Files reach the model only as inputs.

server_mcp.notes: The Responses tool union has no remote MCP tool. Meta describes namespace tools for names that come from MCP clients, which the application runs itself.

prompt_caching.notes: Prefix caching is automatic on every request. RubyLLM reads cached_tokens into the cache_read bucket, billed at the cached input rate.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta chat sends a cache key and retention without breakpoints
verification.notes: with_caching renders prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention, and no breakpoint.

cache_boundaries.notes: Meta documents no breakpoints: the prefix is matched from the start of the prompt. The dialect leaves message content unmarked.

explicit_cache.notes: The inventory lists no cache resources. Caching is automatic prefix reuse with an optional key.

compaction.notes: Meta does not trim requests in general, and truncation auto returns HTTP 400. On computer requests, truncation auto trims old screenshots where it is enabled for the account, so it has limited access. with_provider_options(truncation: "auto") forwards it. with_compaction sends nothing on this provider.

token_counting.notes: Chat#count_tokens posts to /v1/responses/input_tokens, which applies the model tokenizer, instructions, tools, and media.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta counts input tokens with the Responses endpoint
verification.notes: count_tokens posts to /v1/responses/input_tokens.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint with muse-image-1.0 posts to /v1/images/generations through operations the Responses protocol inherits, and reads the base64 image and output_format. No recording covers this path yet. The conversational Responses route is listed under the image generation tool.

image_editing.notes: RubyLLM.paint with with: posts multipart to /v1/images/edits. Meta returns HTTP 400 for mask. No recording covers this path yet.

video_generation.notes: The model lines and inventory list no video generation. Video is an input for Muse Spark and SAM.

speech.notes: Meta states that Muse Voice Transcribe does not synthesize speech, and the inventory lists no speech endpoint.

transcription.notes: Meta transcribes files with muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 at POST /v1/asr/transcribe, as multipart request and audio parts, WAV only. RubyLLM.transcribe on Meta posts the inherited OpenAI request to audio/transcriptions, a path Meta does not document. Raw options cannot change the path or part names.

streaming_transcription.notes: Meta streams transcripts over server-sent events from /v1/asr/transcribe and over the /v1/asr/realtime WebSocket. RubyLLM has no integration for either.

diarization.notes: Meta labels speakers with mode DIARIZATION on both transcription endpoints. RubyLLM has no transcription integration for Meta.

moderation.notes: The inventory lists no moderation endpoint. Moderation on image requests is a parameter Meta rejects on muse-image-1.0.

ocr.notes: The inventory lists no OCR or document parsing endpoint. PDF text extraction happens inside chat input and is covered under PDF input.

embeddings.notes: The inventory lists no embeddings endpoint.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The inventory lists no embeddings endpoint.

reranking.notes: The inventory lists no reranking endpoint.

file_upload.notes: Meta documents POST /v1/files, up to 1 GiB, with file IDs usable in Responses input. The Meta provider declares no files protocol, so RubyLLM raises that it does not support file uploads.

file_download.notes: Meta documents GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content. The Meta provider declares no files protocol, so RubyLLM raises that it does not support file uploads.

chat_batches.notes: The Files API accepts purpose batch for "Batch input files", but the API reference and documentation index list no batch endpoint, so what a batch can run is unverified. RubyLLM declares no batch operation for Meta.

embedding_batches.notes: The inventory lists no embeddings endpoint to batch.

advisor_tool.notes: The inventory documents no advisor tool.

agent_responses.notes: This row covers the Perplexity Agent API, which Meta does not serve.

agent_skills.notes: Skills belong to Muse Code, a separate coding agent product. The API inventory has no skills resource.

async_research.notes: The inventory documents no research job endpoint. Background responses are a separate row.

background_responses.notes: Meta documents background true with polling, stream retrieval, and cancel. with_provider_options(background: true, store: true) can start one, but RubyLLM reads the queued acknowledgement as a finished turn and has no retrieval, polling, or cancel lifecycle.

browser_use.notes: The Responses tool union has no browser tool. browser.search, browser.open, and browser.find are names reserved inside web_search.

classification.notes: The inventory lists no classification endpoint.

computer_use.notes: Meta documents a client-executed computer tool on Responses for Muse Wonder and Muse Spark. with_provider_tools({ type: "computer" }) forwards the raw tool, and computer_call items come back as ServerToolCall objects. RubyLLM has no way to dispatch them or send computer_call_output items with screenshots and safety acknowledgements.

context_editing.notes: The inventory documents no controls for editing context on requests. Screenshot truncation on computer requests is recorded under Context compaction, and old reasoning is the application's to drop.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The inventory lists no embeddings endpoint.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: POST /v1/asr/transcribe is a dedicated file transcription endpoint, with JSON, event stream, and plain text responses. RubyLLM.transcribe on Meta does not call it.

dubbing.notes: The inventory lists no dubbing endpoint.

fast_inference.notes: The schemas list service_tier values including flex and priority, and recordings echo default or auto. The guides and pricing page describe no tiers, so what those values do is unverified. with_provider_options(service_tier:) would forward the field.

file_management.notes: Meta documents listing, retrieving, and deleting files, plus file expiry. The Meta provider declares no files protocol, so RubyLLM raises that it does not support file uploads.

file_search_store_management.notes: The inventory lists no file search stores.

fill_in_middle.notes: The Chat Completions schemas and the inventory document no suffix parameter or completions endpoint.

fine_tuning.notes: The Files API rejects the fine-tune purpose and the inventory lists no fine-tuning jobs. Post-training is for the open-weight models on your own GPUs or a hosted service, outside this API.

google_maps.notes: The inventory lists no maps tool.

guardrail_configuration.notes: The inventory lists no guardrail resources. safety_identifier, which RubyLLM sends through with_end_user, attributes a request and configures nothing.

hosted_conversations.notes: Meta stores responses by default and continues them with previous_response_id. RubyLLM sends store false and replays the local transcript. Meta states conversation resources are not supported on token counting, and the inventory lists no conversation endpoints.

image_batches.notes: The Files API accepts purpose batch for "Batch input files", but the API reference and documentation index list no batch endpoint, so what a batch can run is unverified. RubyLLM declares no batch operation for Meta.

interactions_api.notes: The inventory lists Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages. It has no Interactions API.

json_mode.notes: The schemas describe text.format type json_object as the older JSON mode, active when a message asks for JSON. with_provider_options(text: { format: { type: "json_object" } }) forwards it.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row covers Amazon Bedrock Mantle, which Meta does not serve.

manual_compaction.notes: The Responses reference lists create, retrieve, delete, cancel, and count input tokens, with no compact endpoint. Meta tells applications to compact history themselves.

music_generation.notes: The inventory lists no music endpoint.

nonchat_batches.notes: The Files API accepts purpose batch for "Batch input files", but the API reference and documentation index list no batch endpoint, so what a batch can run is unverified. RubyLLM declares no batch operation for Meta.

omni_video_generation.notes: The inventory lists no video generation.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The API serves Meta models only. Its three request formats reach the same models.

prefix_completion.notes: The Chat Completions schemas and the inventory document no prefix parameter.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The inventory documents no tool that lets model-written code call other tools.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: with_caching(key:, ttl:) renders prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention, in_memory or 24h. Retention is a hint and applies on Responses. Other options raise ArgumentError.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Meta chat sends a cache key and retention without breakpoints
verification.notes: with_caching renders prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention, and no breakpoint.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The inventory documents no server-side model fallback.

realtime.notes: The /v1/asr/realtime WebSocket streams transcription only, recorded under Streaming transcription. Meta states it provides no speech-to-speech conversation API.

response_caching.notes: The inventory documents no whole-response cache. Prompt caching is a separate row.

responses.notes: Responses is the only protocol the Meta provider declares. RubyLLM runs it stateless with encrypted reasoning replay, the path Meta recommends.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: A recorded conversation through POST /v1/responses with store false.

responses_batches.notes: The Files API accepts purpose batch for "Batch input files", but the API reference and documentation index list no batch endpoint, so what a batch can run is unverified. RubyLLM declares no batch operation for Meta.

search_api.notes: The inventory lists no standalone search endpoint. Search runs through the web_search tool.

server_apply_patch.notes: The Responses tool union has no apply patch tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: Muse Image takes an image_generation tool on Responses, and rejects every other tool. Meta declares no alias for it, so with_provider_tools(:image_generation) raises. with_provider_tools({ type: "image_generation" }) forwards the raw tool, and image_generation_call items come back as ServerToolCall objects.

server_tool_search.notes: Deferred RubyLLM tools render with defer_loading and the hosted tool_search tool, and namespaces render as namespace tools. Meta documents this on Responses for any model with tool calling. No Meta recording covers it yet. Client-executed tool search is not implemented.

server_x_search.notes: The inventory lists no X search tool.

shell_computer_tools.notes: Meta documents the client-executed computer tool and no shell tool for callers. The raw computer tool reaches the API, but RubyLLM has no computer_call_output lifecycle. Muse Image runs code internally, which is not a tool for callers.

sound_effects.notes: The inventory lists no sound effects endpoint.

streaming_speech.notes: Meta offers no speech synthesis.

task_budgets.notes: The inventory documents no task budget. max_tool_calls caps built-in tool calls only.

text_intelligence.notes: The inventory lists no text analysis endpoint.

vector_store_management.notes: The inventory lists no vector stores.

video_batches.notes: The inventory lists no video generation to batch.

video_editing.notes: The inventory lists no video editing endpoint. Segmentation with SAM returns geometry, not video.

video_extension.notes: The inventory lists no video generation.

voice_cloning.notes: The inventory lists no voice endpoints beyond transcription.

voice_conversion.notes: The inventory lists no voice endpoints beyond transcription.

web_fetch_api.notes: The inventory lists no standalone web fetch endpoint.

websockets.notes: The Responses API documents server-sent events only. The one WebSocket in the inventory carries transcription.

gaps.notes: Transcription, Streaming transcription, Speaker identification, Dedicated transcription API: Meta transcribes at /v1/asr/transcribe and /v1/asr/realtime. RubyLLM.transcribe posts the inherited request to audio/transcriptions, which Meta does not document.
File upload, File download, File listing and deletion: Meta documents a Files API, and the provider declares no files protocol.
Background Responses jobs: raw options can start a job, with no retrieval, polling, or cancel lifecycle.
Computer use, Shell and computer tools: the raw computer tool reaches the API, with no way to return computer_call_output items.
Audio input, Video input: attachments raise on the Responses protocol, and raw options must replace the whole rendered input.
Image generation, Image editing: the operations reach the documented endpoints, and no recording covers them yet.
Image generation tool: raw tool only, because Meta declares no image_generation alias.
Context compaction: truncation auto works only on computer requests with limited access, and only through raw options.

providers.name: MiniMax
providers.notes: This covers the MiniMax API at platform.minimax.io: text, video, speech, image, music and file endpoints. RubyLLM connects to the Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint for chat, so the media, file, OpenAI-compatible and Responses endpoints have no route.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat reaches POST /anthropic/v1/messages, the route MiniMax recommends, for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3. The same text models also have OpenAI-compatible and Responses routes, which RubyLLM does not use. The endpoint ignores temperature, top_p, top_k and stop_sequences.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: POST /anthropic/v1/messages returns a text block and usage.

streaming.notes: A block on ask sends stream: true on the Messages endpoint and parses its server-sent events, including thinking and signature deltas.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash supports streaming responses
verification.notes: The stream returns Anthropic-style message and content block events.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends output_config.format with a JSON schema, but the Messages reference documents only effort under output_config. It does not say whether the field is honored or ignored, and no recording covers it. The Responses text.format enum lists only text. The Text Generation API documents response_format json_schema for MiniMax-Text-01 alone, which is not in the current model list.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as image blocks by URL or base64. MiniMax documents JPEG, PNG, GIF and WEBP for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3. The optional detail setting has no RubyLLM keyword.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can understand local images
verification.notes: A base64 image block returns a description of the image.

pdf_input.notes: RubyLLM renders PDF attachments as document blocks on this protocol. The compatibility page lists text, image, video, tool and thinking blocks and does not mention document blocks or PDFs, and no recording shows how the endpoint treats them.

audio_input.notes: The Messages, Chat Completions and Responses references list text, image and video input for the M3 family. They document no audio content block. Audio is an input only to the separate transcription and video generation operations.

video_input.notes: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3 accept video blocks by URL, base64 or an mm_file reference to an uploaded file; MP4, AVI, MOV and MKV are documented. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for a video attachment, because this protocol renders only images, PDFs and text. A provider-shaped video block reaches the wire only by replacing messages through with_provider_options or by editing the payload in before_request.

thinking.notes: Thinking blocks and deltas parse into Message#thinking with their signature, and stored blocks replay on later turns as MiniMax requires. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash always thinks; MiniMax-M3 thinks only on request.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash returns thinking when available
verification.notes: The response carries a signed thinking block before the text.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash streams thinking content when available
verification.notes: The stream carries thinking_delta and signature_delta events.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking maps to thinking.type adaptive or disabled and to output_config.effort. Effort tunes MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, from low to max. MiniMax-M3 has an on and off toggle and ignores effort. with_thinking(false) raises locally on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and the M2 family, whose API also cannot turn thinking off.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax chat asks for adaptive thinking with an effort
verification.notes: with_thinking(effort: :low) sends adaptive thinking and the effort.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax chat turns thinking off on models with a toggle
verification.notes: with_thinking(false) on MiniMax-M3 sends disabled.

citations.notes: with_citations marks documents as citable on this protocol, but the Messages reference documents no citations field or document block. The only trace of citations is url_citation annotations in a Responses web search example, which the schema does not define. Whether Messages text blocks can carry citations is unverified. The pages a web search used are available from Message#web_sources.

tools.notes: Ruby tools render as name, description and input_schema, and tool_use blocks round-trip with their tool results. MiniMax asks for the full assistant content in later turns, including thinking, and RubyLLM replays it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can use tools
verification.notes: A tool_use block runs a Ruby tool and its result returns a final answer.

tool_choice.notes: auto, the default, is the only tool_choice value MiniMax documents on any of its text routes, so there is no choice to control. with_tool_options(choice:) sends other values as given, and the documentation does not say how the endpoint answers them.

parallel_tools.notes: Several tool_use blocks in one response parse into separate tool calls. The MiniMax documentation does not describe this on the Messages route; the recording shows it, and the Responses reference reports parallel_tool_calls as always true.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: One response returns three dice_roll tool_use blocks.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls: :one) sends disable_parallel_tool_use inside tool_choice. The Messages schema defines only tool_choice.type and does not say whether the field is honored or ignored, and no recording covers it. On the Responses route, parallel_tool_calls is documented as ignored in requests.

server_web_search.notes: with_provider_tools(:web_search) sends web_search_20250305, the version MiniMax runs. Pause turns continue automatically, the search steps appear as server tool calls, and Message#web_sources lists the pages. MiniMax marks server tools as Beta.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax sends web search as the version MiniMax runs
verification.notes: The request carries the versioned web search tool.

server_web_fetch.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedServerToolError for this alias on MiniMax.

server_code_execution.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool, and the Messages route ignores container. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedServerToolError for this alias on MiniMax.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax rejects the other provider tools, which the endpoint does not run
verification.notes: with_provider_tools(:code_execution) raises at request time.

server_file_search.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool and offers no hosted file search.

server_mcp.notes: The Messages route documents mcp_servers as ignored, and web_search is the only server tool. MiniMax publishes MCP servers for client applications to run, which is not a hosted MCP tool.

prompt_caching.notes: MiniMax caches automatically from 512 input tokens by prefix, with no request option. RubyLLM reports usage.cache_read_input_tokens as cache_read, and input_tokens holds new input only, matching how MiniMax bills.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax chat parses thinking with its signature, and counts cached input
verification.notes: cache_read_input_tokens becomes tokens.cache_read.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: The response reports 197 cache read tokens on an automatic cache hit.

cache_boundaries.notes: The Messages schema documents cache_control markers on system and tool blocks and states that MiniMax-M3 and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash do not support them. That leaves the M2 family, whose M2.5 and M2.7 models MiniMax retires on November 18, 2026; the same page already lists them as retired. with_caching and cache_until_here render the markers.

explicit_cache.notes: The Prompt Caching page describes automatic caching only. The API inventory documents no cache resources to create or manage.

compaction.notes: The Messages route documents context_management as ignored, and the other text routes document no compaction or sliding window control. The Responses truncation field is documented as ignored too. with_compaction still sends context_management, which has no effect here.

token_counting.notes: chat.count_tokens posts to /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens, which MiniMax documents for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3. MiniMax also has a separate Responses estimate at /v1/responses/input_tokens. No recording covers this route.

image_generation.notes: POST /v1/image_generation generates images from text with the image-01 family. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

image_editing.notes: Image-to-image generation takes a subject_reference for people on POST /v1/image_generation. No mask is documented. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

video_generation.notes: POST /v2/video_generation creates asynchronous MiniMax-H3 tasks, and legacy Hailuo task endpoints remain documented. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

speech.notes: POST /v1/t2a_v2 synthesizes speech with the speech model family, and an asynchronous long text route is also documented. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

transcription.notes: POST /v1/speech_to_text transcribes audio files with asr-1.0, up to 500 seconds and 50 MB. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

streaming_transcription.notes: stream=true on POST /v1/speech_to_text returns incremental text deltas over server-sent events in the json format. Audio input cannot be streamed. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

diarization.notes: The verbose_json format returns n_speakers and a speaker tag per segment. It cannot be combined with streaming. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

moderation.notes: The inventory documents no moderation operation. Sensitive content flags on legacy text responses and the mask_sensitive_info option do not classify input on request.

ocr.notes: The inventory documents no OCR or document parsing endpoint. Reading an image through chat is not an OCR API.

embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no embeddings endpoint. RubyLLM raises on embed through this protocol.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no embeddings endpoint.

reranking.notes: The inventory documents no reranking endpoint.

file_upload.notes: POST /v1/files/upload stores files for voice cloning, long text speech, video understanding and video generation. RubyLLM declares no files protocol here, and the dialect turns provider file references off.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::MiniMax attachments never uploads files to the provider
verification.notes: The dialect reports no provider file references.

file_download.notes: GET /v1/files/retrieve_content downloads generated files, such as long text speech output. RubyLLM declares no files protocol here.

chat_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint for chat. Asynchronous long text speech is a single task, not a batch.

embedding_batches.notes: The inventory documents no embeddings or batch endpoint.

advisor_tool.notes: The inventory documents no advisor tool.

agent_responses.notes: The inventory documents no Perplexity Agent API; that row belongs to another provider.

agent_skills.notes: The inventory documents no agent skills, and the Messages route ignores container.

async_research.notes: The inventory documents no asynchronous research operation.

background_responses.notes: The Create Response reference documents no background parameter. Asynchronous video and long text speech tasks are separate operations.

browser_use.notes: The inventory documents no browser use tool.

classification.notes: The inventory documents no classification endpoint.

computer_use.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool, and tool definitions take a name and JSON schema only.

context_editing.notes: The Messages route documents context_management as ignored.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no contextual embeddings.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: POST /v1/speech_to_text is a dedicated transcription endpoint with JSON, verbose JSON, SRT and VTT output. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

dubbing.notes: The inventory documents no dubbing operation.

fast_inference.notes: service_tier: "priority" buys priority admission at 1.5 times the standard price on MiniMax-M3; MiniMax-M3.1-Flash does not support the field. with_provider_options(service_tier: "priority") forwards it, and RubyLLM has no shared keyword for it.

file_management.notes: GET /v1/files/list and POST /v1/files/delete manage stored files. RubyLLM declares no files protocol here.

file_search_store_management.notes: The inventory documents no file search stores.

fill_in_middle.notes: The inventory documents no fill-in-the-middle parameter or endpoint.

fine_tuning.notes: The hosted API documents no fine-tuning jobs. The LoRA recipe in the self-hosting guide trains open weights outside this API.

google_maps.notes: The inventory documents no maps grounding.

guardrail_configuration.notes: The inventory documents no guardrail configuration.

hosted_conversations.notes: The Create Response reference states that previous_response_id, conversation and store are not supported in requests and are ignored.

image_batches.notes: The inventory documents no image batches.

interactions_api.notes: The inventory documents no Interactions API.

json_mode.notes: No text route documents a JSON object mode. The Text Generation API accepts only json_schema, for MiniMax-Text-01 alone, and the Responses format enum lists only text.

mantle_protocols.notes: The inventory documents no Bedrock Mantle protocols; that row belongs to another provider.

manual_compaction.notes: The inventory documents no compaction operation.

music_generation.notes: POST /v1/music_generation is limited access: it closed to new users on August 20, 2026, and existing paying users keep it. The model list also marks the music models as retired, without a separate date for those users. RubyLLM has no music operation for MiniMax.

nonchat_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint. Asynchronous long text speech and video tasks are single tasks.

omni_video_generation.notes: MiniMax-H3 takes a content array that mixes text with reference images, videos and audio on POST /v2/video_generation. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

partner_model_protocols.notes: MiniMax serves its own models only, so no partner model routes exist in this inventory.

prefix_completion.notes: The text references document no assistant prefill or prefix parameter.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool and no programmatic tool calling.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: The Responses route takes prompt_cache_key as a cache routing identifier. RubyLLM does not speak that route, and the Messages route has no equivalent for current models.

provider_server_fallback.notes: The inventory documents no server-side model fallback.

realtime.notes: The inventory documents no realtime conversation session. Its WebSocket endpoints synthesize speech only, which the streaming speech row covers.

response_caching.notes: The inventory documents no whole response cache, only prompt caching.

responses.notes: POST /v1/responses is a documented stateless route with function tools, web search and token estimates. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol in RubyLLM, so it cannot be selected.

responses_batches.notes: The inventory documents no Responses batches.

search_api.notes: The pay-as-you-go inventory documents no search endpoint. The M Plan web_search is an MCP tool for subscribers to run in their own tools, and web_search on the text routes is a server tool.

server_apply_patch.notes: The inventory documents no apply patch tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: The inventory documents no hosted image generation tool.

server_tool_search.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool. RubyLLM treats this protocol as searching deferred tools itself, so deferred tools send a tool search definition that the documentation does not list.

server_x_search.notes: The inventory documents no X search tool.

shell_computer_tools.notes: MiniMax documents web_search as its only server tool, and tool definitions take a name and JSON schema only.

sound_effects.notes: The inventory documents no sound effect generation. The sound_effects setting on speech applies a filter to synthesized voice.

streaming_speech.notes: POST /v1/t2a_v2 streams audio with stream: true, and two WebSocket endpoints stream audio, one of them from streaming text input. MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol, so this operation has no route.

task_budgets.notes: The inventory documents no task budget control.

text_intelligence.notes: The inventory documents no text analysis endpoint.

vector_store_management.notes: The inventory documents no vector stores.

video_batches.notes: The inventory documents no video batches.

video_editing.notes: The inventory documents no general video edit. Video regeneration only turns a MiniMax-H3 768P result into 2K, and the page states that it does not process arbitrary videos.

video_extension.notes: The video references document no operation that extends an existing video.

voice_cloning.notes: POST /v1/voice_clone creates a voice_id from uploaded audio, after individual or enterprise verification. Cloned voices are deleted after 7 days without use. RubyLLM has no voice creation operation for MiniMax.

voice_conversion.notes: The inventory documents no speech-to-speech conversion.

web_fetch_api.notes: The inventory documents no standalone web fetch endpoint.

websockets.notes: The Create Response reference documents HTTP only. MiniMax WebSocket endpoints serve speech synthesis, not Responses.

gaps.notes: Video input: the M3 models take video blocks, but RubyLLM rejects video attachments on this protocol. Only a replaced messages value or a before_request edit can send one.
Tool choice: MiniMax documents only auto, so forcing or disabling a tool is not available.
Image generation, Image editing, Video generation, Omni video generation: MiniMax has image and asynchronous video endpoints, and RubyLLM routes neither paint nor animate to them.
Speech generation, Streaming speech generation: the T2A HTTP and WebSocket endpoints have no RubyLLM route.
Transcription, Streaming transcription, Speaker identification, Dedicated transcription API: POST /v1/speech_to_text has no RubyLLM route.
File upload, File download, File listing and deletion: the Files API has no RubyLLM protocol on this provider, so large videos cannot be attached by mm_file reference either.
Responses API, Prompt cache options: POST /v1/responses and its prompt_cache_key are documented, and MiniMax declares only the Anthropic protocol.
Music generation: limited to existing paying users since August 20, 2026, with no RubyLLM operation for it.
Voice cloning: MiniMax creates voices from uploaded audio, and RubyLLM has no voice creation operation for it.
Fast inference: priority admission needs service_tier through with_provider_options, on MiniMax-M3 only.

providers.name: Moonshot AI
providers.notes: Audited the Kimi API Platform at api.moonshot.ai: its REST inventory, OpenAPI file, guides, and changelog. RubyLLM integrates Chat Completions only. Admin API endpoints are out of comparison.

chat.notes: RubyLLM.chat calls /v1/chat/completions on api.moonshot.ai with Kimi K3.1 Pro, K3, K2.7 Code, and K2.6. kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.7-code are closed to new accounts, with deprecation expected in late December 2026.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: Successful Chat Completions text response.

streaming.notes: Chat streaming reads server-sent events, including reasoning_content deltas and usage from the final chunk. RubyLLM sends stream_options include_usage.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses moonshot/kimi-k2.6 supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Streamed text response.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends response_format json_schema. Kimi describes K2.6 as unstable with complex schemas; K3 and K3.1 Pro handle nested objects, arrays, and anyOf.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat #with_schema with moonshot/kimi-k3 accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: Parsed structured output on K3.

vision.notes: Image attachments travel as base64 data URIs in image_url parts. Kimi does not read image URLs, so RubyLLM downloads remote images and sends them inline. Referencing an uploaded image with ms://<file_id> needs raw messages, because RubyLLM has no Kimi file upload.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can understand local images
verification.notes: Local image sent as a data URI.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can understand remote images without extension
verification.notes: Remote image downloaded and sent inline.

pdf_input.notes: Chat content parts carry only text, image_url, and video_url. Kimi documents PDF questions as a two-step flow: extract text with the Files API using purpose file-extract, then place that text in messages. RubyLLM rejects PDF attachments for this provider and has no Kimi Files integration. Plain text files work as text parts.

audio_input.notes: The Chat Completions content types are text, image_url, and video_url. The audited API inventory documents no audio input, and RubyLLM rejects audio attachments for this provider.

video_input.notes: K3.1 Pro, K3, K2.7 Code, and K2.6 accept video_url parts as base64 data URIs or ms://<file_id> references. RubyLLM has no video attachment path for this provider: a video attachment raises UnsupportedAttachmentError. with_provider_options(messages: [...]) replaces the rendered messages, so a raw video_url part reaches the API.

thinking.notes: Message#thinking reads reasoning_content from complete and streamed responses, and RubyLLM sends it back on later assistant messages, as K3 and K2.7 Code require.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking moonshot/kimi-k2.6 returns thinking when available
verification.notes: reasoning_content on a complete response.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking moonshot/kimi-k2.6 streams thinking content when available
verification.notes: reasoning_content deltas while streaming.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking(effort:) sends reasoning_effort low, high, or max on K3 and K3.1 Pro, where the API default is max and thinking cannot be turned off. with_thinking(true) and with_thinking(false) send the thinking toggle on K2.6. K2.7 Code always thinks and offers no setting. The thinking keep field for K2.6 needs provider options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Moonshot chat turns thinking on and off on models with a toggle
verification.notes: Asserts thinking type disabled on kimi-k2.6.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Moonshot chat sets the effort of models that always think
verification.notes: Asserts reasoning_effort max on kimi-k3.

citations.notes: The Chat Completions reference documents no citations. The Responses output_text schema has an annotations array with no documented item shape, and include can return web_search_call.action.sources. That does not establish inline citations. RubyLLM parses annotations only from Chat Completions responses, and no recording shows one.

tools.notes: with_tools sends function tools and runs the tool loop, including in streaming conversations.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can use tools
verification.notes: Tool call and result turn.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can use tools with multi-turn streaming conversations
verification.notes: Streamed tool calls across turns.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice:) sends auto, none, required, or a named function. Forcing a named function returns a 400 while thinking is on, so it fails on K3 and K3.1 Pro, which always think. The reference says K2.6 and K2.7 Code reject required; a recording shows kimi-k2.6 accepting it with thinking off.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control moonshot/kimi-k2.6 respects choice: :required for unrelated queries
verification.notes: required with thinking disabled returned a weather tool call.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat tool choice and calls control moonshot/kimi-k2.6 respects specific tool choice
verification.notes: Named function with thinking disabled.

parallel_tools.notes: The model can return several tool_calls in one response, and RubyLLM runs them all.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: Three dice_roll calls in one response.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling moonshot/kimi-k2.6 can use parallel tool calls
verification.notes: Two different tools in one response.

parallel_tool_control.notes: The Chat Completions and Responses request schemas do not document parallel_tool_calls; the field appears only on the Responses response object. with_tool_options(calls:) sends it on Chat Completions, and the live calls: :one spec skips this provider, so whether Kimi honors it is unverified.

server_web_search.notes: The Responses API documents a server-side web_search tool, which RubyLLM cannot reach because this provider declares only Chat Completions. Chat Completions gets search through the moonshot/web-search official tool: a function declaration that the application runs through the Formula fibers endpoint. RubyLLM has no alias for either route, and with_provider_tools raises UnsupportedServerToolError.

server_web_fetch.notes: The moonshot/fetch official tool extracts a URL as Markdown. It is a function declaration that the application runs through the Formula fibers endpoint. RubyLLM has no integration; a local Ruby tool would have to call the endpoint itself.

server_code_execution.notes: The Responses tool types are function, custom (apply_patch only), namespace, and web_search. The official tool list has an Excel and CSV analysis tool but no general code execution tool.

server_file_search.notes: The Responses tool types and the official tool list contain no file search tool. File questions go through text extraction into messages.

server_mcp.notes: The Responses API says other tool types are not supported, so it has no remote MCP tool. MCP servers are documented only for Kimi Playground, not as an API tool.

prompt_caching.notes: Kimi caches matching request prefixes automatically, with a 5m default. RubyLLM reads prompt_tokens_details cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens into cache_read and cache_write. Cache Write applies to K3 and K3.1 Pro, not K2.7 Code or K2.6.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::Moonshot chat parses reasoning and counts cache reads and writes
verification.notes: Asserts cached and written tokens leave the input bucket.

cache_boundaries.notes: Caching matches prefixes with no explicit markers. prompt_cache_options.mode supports only implicit, and the Messages API ignores cache_control markers inside messages. RubyLLM sends no breakpoints for this provider.

explicit_cache.notes: The inventory has no cache resource endpoints. The caching guide says entries cannot be cleared manually and expire after inactivity.

compaction.notes: The audited API documents no compaction or context management control. The multi-turn guide leaves context length to the application, because the API is stateless.

token_counting.notes: POST /v1/tokenizers/estimate-token-count estimates input tokens for messages, including images and videos. RubyLLM has no count_tokens rendering for this provider, so RubyLLM::Chat#count_tokens cannot reach it.

image_generation.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no image generation operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

image_editing.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no image editing operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

video_generation.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no video generation operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

speech.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no speech generation operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

transcription.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no transcription operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no multimodal embeddings operation. Its endpoints cover chat, Responses, Messages, models, token estimation, tools, files, and batches.

file_upload.notes: POST /v1/files accepts purpose file-extract, image, video, or batch, up to 100 MiB per file. This provider declares no files protocol, so RubyLLM.upload raises.

file_download.notes: GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content returns extracted text and batch result files. This provider declares no files protocol, so RubyLLM cannot download them.

chat_batches.notes: The Batch API runs /v1/chat/completions requests from a JSONL file at 60 percent of standard rates, on K3.1 Pro, K3, K2.7 Code, and K2.6. This provider declares no batches module, so create_batch raises.

embedding_batches.notes: Create Batch accepts only /v1/chat/completions, and the API has no embeddings endpoint.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The audited Kimi API inventory documents no programmatic tool calling operation.

providers.name: TypeSafe
providers.notes: Covers TypeSafe's System One API at api.typesafe.ai, which has two endpoints: POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Its main value, typed judgments with probabilities, choices, and scores, has no row here: RubyLLM reaches it through RubyLLM.judge and RubyLLM::Judge, so most rows read as not in this API.

chat.notes: Jev does not generate text or hold a conversation, and the API has no chat endpoint. RubyLLM registers TypeSafe models as judgment models, so a chat cannot reach this provider.

streaming.notes: Jev does not stream text. POST /v1/systemone returns one JSON response.

structured_output.notes: The API has no schema-based generation. Its answers are always typed by question type, which RubyLLM exposes through judgments rather than chat.

vision.notes: The API has no chat, so it has no chat attachments. Jev does read PNG and JPEG images inside System One requests. That judgment path is a preview, and RubyLLM rejects attachments sent to it.

pdf_input.notes: The API has no chat attachments, and the Models page lists only text and images as Jev input.

audio_input.notes: The API has no chat attachments. The Models page states Jev does not natively accept audio.

video_input.notes: The API has no chat attachments. The Models page states Jev does not natively accept video.

thinking.notes: The System One response carries answers, the model, and input and output token usage. It documents no thinking content.

thinking_controls.notes: The System One request takes model, state, questions, and assets. It documents no thinking settings.

citations.notes: The System One response documents no citations. The citation cookbook checks citations supplied by an application with a Choice question.

tools.notes: The request has no tool definitions and the response has no tool calls. The function calling cookbook maps function names and arguments onto ordinary questions in application code.

tool_choice.notes: The API has no tool definitions, so it has no tool choice.

parallel_tools.notes: The API returns no tool calls. Several questions in one request are not tool calls.

parallel_tool_control.notes: The API returns no tool calls, so it has no limit on them.

server_web_search.notes: The API documents no provider-run tools, including web search.

server_web_fetch.notes: The API documents no provider-run tools, including web fetch.

server_code_execution.notes: The API documents no provider-run tools, including code execution.

server_file_search.notes: The API documents no provider-run tools, including file search.

server_mcp.notes: The API documents no provider-run tools, including remote MCP.

prompt_caching.notes: The API reference and Models page document no prompt caching. Caches in the cookbooks are local helpers in the example code.

cache_boundaries.notes: The API documents no cache markers.

explicit_cache.notes: The API documents no cache resources.

compaction.notes: The API is stateless per request and documents no context controls that reduce it. Long context raises the limits instead.

token_counting.notes: The API has no token counting endpoint. Each response reports input and output tokens after the judgment runs.

image_generation.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither offers image generation.

image_editing.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither offers image editing.

video_generation.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither offers video generation.

diarization.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither offers speaker identification.

moderation.notes: The API has no moderation endpoint. The guardrails cookbook builds screening from Noul and Score questions, which RubyLLM reaches through judgments.

ocr.notes: The API has no OCR or document parsing endpoint. The cookbooks read scanned pages by asking questions about images, and Box questions locate regions but do not return text.

embeddings.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither returns embeddings.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither returns embeddings.

reranking.notes: The API has no rerank endpoint. The re-ranking cookbook asks one question per query and candidate pair in application code.

file_upload.notes: The API has no file store. Images travel inside a single System One request, as base64 or multipart parts.

file_download.notes: The API has no file store to download from.

chat_batches.notes: The API has no chat and no batch endpoint. Several questions in one request are not a batch job.

agent_responses.notes: This row covers a Perplexity product. TypeSafe has no equivalent endpoint.

browser_use.notes: The API documents no browser tool.

classification.notes: Choice questions select one label from a defined set and return a probability for every label, with confidence. RubyLLM exposes them as `choice` on RubyLLM::Judge and RubyLLM.judge, through POST /v1/systemone. The API has no separate classify endpoint.

task_budgets.notes: The API documents no task budgets. Limits apply per request and per question through context length.

voice_conversion.notes: The API documents two endpoints, POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Neither offers voice conversion.

web_fetch_api.notes: The API has no web fetch endpoint.

websockets.notes: The API documents no WebSocket transport.

gaps.notes: Judgment images, Box questions: the API accepts PNG and JPEG images in a request and answers Box questions on Jev 1.14, both as a preview behind the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images header. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for attachments, has no Box question type, and cannot send the header from a judgment.
Long context: the TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context header raises both context limits to 262k tokens. A judgment has no way to send a request header, so RubyLLM stays within the default limits.

Judgment cost: TypeSafe publishes a per-token input price, but the registry holds no price for the jev-latest and jev-preview aliases, so a hosted judgment reports token counts and a nil cost. Versioned model IDs are absent from the listing and need assume_model_exists.

providers.name: Z.ai
providers.notes: This covers the Z.ai API documented at docs.z.ai: chat, media, tool and agent endpoints under api.z.ai. RubyLLM speaks a Chat Completions dialect at /api/paas/v4, so media operations reach Z.ai only where that shared protocol matches. Setting zai_api_base can point it at BigModel or the GLM Coding Plan endpoint; BigModel documents its platform separately, outside this comparison.

chat.notes: RubyLLM sends messages to POST /paas/v4/chat/completions through its Z.ai dialect of Chat Completions. Instructions keep the system role, and with_end_user sends user_id.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality zai/glm-5.3-flash can have a basic conversation
verification.notes: POST /paas/v4/chat/completions returns content and usage.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat basic chat functionality zai/glm-5.3-flash can handle multi-turn conversations
verification.notes: Earlier turns replay from the local transcript.

streaming.notes: stream: true returns server-sent chunks, parsed into RubyLLM chunks with usage on the final event. RubyLLM does not send tool_stream; a recording shows streamed tool calls without it, and with_provider_options can set it.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat streaming responses zai/glm-5.3-flash supports streaming responses
verification.notes: Text deltas and usage arrive over SSE.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling zai/glm-5.3-flash can use tools with multi-turn streaming conversations
verification.notes: Streamed tool calls without tool_stream.

structured_output.notes: with_schema sends response_format with type json_schema. The docs describe only json_object, for text models, and do not describe json_schema or say whether the schema is enforced. A recording on GLM-5.3-Flash returns JSON matching the schema.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat #with_schema with zai/glm-5.3-flash accepts a JSON schema and returns structured output
verification.notes: A strict json_schema request returns matching JSON.

vision.notes: Image attachments render as image_url parts, by URL or Base64 data URL. Vision models include the GLM-5.3-Flash series and the GLM-4.6V family.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat vision models zai/glm-5.3-flash can understand local images
verification.notes: A local image goes out as a data URL and the model describes it.

pdf_input.notes: The GLM-5.3-Flash series takes file parts with file_id, file_url or file_data, for PDF and Office formats up to 50 MB. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for PDF attachments on this provider. A provider-shaped part reaches the wire only by replacing messages through with_provider_options or by editing the payload in before_request. Text files are inlined as text parts.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::ZAI attachments rejects documents and audio
verification.notes: PDF attachments raise before a request.

audio_input.notes: The Chat Completion description lists audio among multimodal inputs, but its content schema defines only text, image_url, video_url and file parts, and the model pages list video, image, text and file. No audio request shape is documented, so availability is unverified. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for audio attachments on this provider.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::ZAI attachments rejects documents and audio
verification.notes: Audio attachments raise before a request.

video_input.notes: The GLM-5.3-Flash series takes video_url parts with an MP4, MKV or MOV URL up to 200 MB. RubyLLM raises UnsupportedAttachmentError for video attachments on this provider. A provider-shaped part reaches the wire only by replacing messages through with_provider_options or by editing the payload in before_request.

thinking.notes: reasoning_content is parsed into message.thinking, including on streams, and earlier reasoning replays as reasoning_content. Supported from the GLM-4.6 series up.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking zai/glm-5.3-flash returns thinking when available
verification.notes: reasoning_content appears as thinking text.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking zai/glm-5.3-flash streams thinking content when available
verification.notes: Thinking deltas arrive on the stream.

thinking_controls.notes: with_thinking sends thinking.type and reasoning_effort. Effort applies to GLM-5.2 and later; GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash take only low, high and max, and return an error if thinking is disabled. thinking.clear_thinking has no shared name and goes through with_provider_options.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat with extended thinking zai/glm-5.3-flash returns thinking when available
verification.notes: The request carries thinking.type enabled and reasoning_effort low.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::ZAI chat turns thinking off on models with a toggle
verification.notes: with_thinking(false) sends thinking.type disabled and no effort.

citations.notes: Web Search in Chat returns its sources in a top-level web_search array when the tool sets search_result. RubyLLM does not parse that array, so with_citations and message.citations stay empty; read it from message.raw after sending the raw tool.

tools.notes: Function tools render as type function, with up to 128 functions per request. Tool results and multi-turn tool loops run through the shared Chat Completions tools module.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling zai/glm-5.3-flash can use tools
verification.notes: A tool call runs and its result returns to the model.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling zai/glm-5.3-flash can use tools with multi-turn streaming conversations
verification.notes: Tool loop over a streamed response.

tool_choice.notes: with_tool_options(choice: :auto) sends tool_choice. Z.ai documents auto as the only accepted value, so other choices are left for the API to answer.

parallel_tools.notes: Recordings show several tool calls in one response, with different tools and with the same tool. The docs do not describe this behaviour.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling zai/glm-5.3-flash can use parallel tool calls
verification.notes: One response carries weather and best_language_to_learn calls.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Chat function calling zai/glm-5.3-flash can handle multiple tool calls in a single response
verification.notes: One response carries three dice_roll calls.

parallel_tool_control.notes: with_tool_options(calls:) sends parallel_tool_calls. The Chat Completion schema and Function Calling guide do not mention that field, and no recording shows whether the API honors it.

server_web_search.notes: Chat requests take a tool of type web_search with search options, priced per use. RubyLLM has no alias for it on this provider. with_provider_options(tools: [...]) forwards it, and that value replaces the rendered tools, so function tools must be included in the same array. Search results stay in the raw response.

server_web_fetch.notes: The chat tool list has no fetch tool. Web Reader is a separate endpoint, recorded under the standalone web fetch row.

server_code_execution.notes: The chat tool schema lists function, retrieval and web_search tools. No code execution tool is documented.

server_file_search.notes: The Chat Completion schema defines a retrieval tool with knowledge_id and prompt_template, while the same page says only functions are supported as tools. No guide or knowledge base API is documented, so availability on current models is unverified. If it works, with_provider_options(tools: [...]) forwards it.

server_mcp.notes: The chat tool schema has no remote MCP tool type. Z.ai hosts MCP servers for MCP clients to connect to themselves, which is a client integration and not a tool the model API runs.

prompt_caching.notes: Z.ai caches repeated context automatically, with no request option, and the FAQ describes the mechanism as an open beta. RubyLLM reads usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens as cache_read and removes those tokens from input.

verification.example: RubyLLM::Providers::ZAI chat parses reasoning and counts cached input
verification.notes: cached_tokens map to cache_read.

cache_boundaries.notes: The Context Caching guide describes implicit caching with no manual configuration, and the chat schema has no cache markers.

explicit_cache.notes: The API documents no cache resources to create or manage. Caching is implicit, and the pricing page lists cached input storage as free for a limited time.

compaction.notes: The API documents no summarization or sliding window control. thinking.clear_thinking only removes earlier reasoning and is recorded under context editing.

token_counting.notes: POST /paas/v4/tokenizer counts tokens for a messages array; its schema lists the GLM-4.6 model. The Z.ai dialect defines no token counting or tokenization seams, so count_tokens and RubyLLM.tokenize raise an error.

image_generation.notes: RubyLLM.paint posts to images/generations through the inherited Chat Completions image seams and reads the returned image URL. GLM-Image is not in the registry, so calls need provider: :zai and assume_model_exists: true. RubyLLM also sends n, which the schema does not list, and a null size when none is given; no recording covers this provider. The asynchronous image route has no integration.

image_editing.notes: The image endpoints take a model, prompt, quality and size only, and no edit endpoint or input image is documented.

video_generation.notes: POST /paas/v4/videos/generations creates CogVideoX-3 jobs from text or images, and async-result returns them. The Chat Completions protocol has no video seams, so RubyLLM.animate raises an error on this provider.

speech.notes: The Python and Java SDK pages list text-to-speech as a feature, but the docs index, OpenAPI file and pricing page show no speech endpoint or model. Whether this API serves it is unverified. RubyLLM.speak would post to audio/speech through the inherited protocol.

transcription.notes: RubyLLM.transcribe posts the file and model to audio/transcriptions through the inherited protocol and reads text. GLM-ASR-2512 is not in the registry, so calls need provider: :zai and assume_model_exists: true. Z.ai limits audio to WAV or MP3, 30 seconds and 25 MB. hotwords goes through provider_options. No recording covers this provider.

streaming_transcription.notes: A block on RubyLLM.transcribe sends stream=true and reads the documented transcript.text.delta and transcript.text.done events into TranscriptionChunk objects. This is server-sent events for a file, not a live session. No recording covers this provider.

diarization.notes: The transcription request and response have no speaker fields.

moderation.notes: The Python SDK page lists content moderation as a feature, but the docs index, OpenAPI file and pricing page show no moderation endpoint or model. Whether this API serves it is unverified. The sensitive finish reason and error code 1301 flag blocked content and do not classify input on request. RubyLLM.moderate would post to moderations through the inherited protocol.

ocr.notes: POST /paas/v4/layout_parsing parses images and PDFs with GLM-OCR and returns Markdown and layout details. The Z.ai dialect has no OCR seams, so RubyLLM.ocr raises an error.

embeddings.notes: The Python and Java SDK pages list text embedding as a feature, but the docs index, OpenAPI file and pricing page show no embeddings endpoint or model. Whether this API serves it is unverified. RubyLLM.embed would post to embeddings through the inherited protocol.

multimodal_embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no multimodal embeddings.

reranking.notes: The inventory documents no reranking endpoint. RubyLLM.rerank raises an error on this provider.

file_upload.notes: POST /paas/v4/files stores files for agents and user data, and the GLM-5.3-Flash series can reference them by file_id in chat. RubyLLM declares no files protocol for Z.ai, so RubyLLM.upload raises an error.

file_download.notes: The file API documents upload only, with no route for reading file content back.

chat_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint, and the pricing page lists no batch rate.

embedding_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint.

advisor_tool.notes: The chat tool schema has no advisor tool.

agent_responses.notes: This row is a Perplexity API. Z.ai agents are recorded under hosted conversations.

agent_skills.notes: The API documents no skills resource. Skills in the Coding Plan pages belong to the coding tools that run them.

async_research.notes: The inventory documents no research job endpoint.

background_responses.notes: The inventory documents no background job option for chat.

browser_use.notes: The GLM-5.3-Flash guide describes the model operating browsers inside agent environments. The chat schema has no browser tool.

classification.notes: The inventory documents no classification endpoint.

computer_use.notes: The GLM-5.3-Flash guide shows computer use prompts for agent environments. The chat schema has no computer tool.

context_editing.notes: thinking.clear_thinking controls whether reasoning from earlier turns stays in the context, and it defaults to clearing. with_provider_options(thinking: {clear_thinking: false}) forwards it. It covers reasoning only. No tool result or message clearing is documented.

contextual_embeddings.notes: The inventory documents no embeddings endpoint of this kind.

dedicated_transcription_api.notes: audio/transcriptions is a dedicated endpoint, and RubyLLM.transcribe reaches it. This overlaps the transcription row. No recording covers this provider.

dubbing.notes: The inventory documents no dubbing endpoint.

fast_inference.notes: GLM-5.3-FlashX is a faster model, documented at 200 tokens per second, and is selected by its model id in the registry. No speed tier request parameter is documented.

file_management.notes: The file API documents upload only, with no list or delete routes.

file_search_store_management.notes: The inventory documents no file search store API.

fill_in_middle.notes: The inventory documents no completions endpoint or suffix parameter.

fine_tuning.notes: The inventory documents no fine-tuning jobs.

google_maps.notes: The inventory documents no maps grounding.

guardrail_configuration.notes: The inventory documents no guardrail settings.

hosted_conversations.notes: The GLM Slide/Poster Agent, a beta, keeps a provider-stored conversation through conversation_id and a history endpoint at /v1/agents/conversation. This is outside RubyLLM coverage; conversation state stays in the application.

image_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint. Asynchronous image generation handles one request at a time.

interactions_api.notes: The inventory documents no such API.

json_mode.notes: response_format with type json_object turns on JSON mode, documented for text models. with_provider_options(response_format: {type: "json_object"}) forwards it. with_schema is the shared schema API.

mantle_protocols.notes: This row is a Bedrock route, and the inventory has no equivalent.

manual_compaction.notes: The inventory documents no compaction endpoint.

music_generation.notes: The inventory documents no music generation.

nonchat_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint.

omni_video_generation.notes: The video endpoint takes a prompt and first and last frame images, with no audio or video references.

partner_model_protocols.notes: The inference routes document GLM models and no partner model protocols. The Anthropic Messages endpoint is a compatible route for GLM models.

prefix_completion.notes: The chat schema has no prefix option, and the inventory documents no completions endpoint.

programmatic_tool_calling.notes: The inventory documents no programmatic tool calling.

prompt_cache_controls.notes: Caching is implicit and the chat schema has no cache key or lifetime option. RubyLLM sends no cache parameters on this provider, even with with_caching(key:).

provider_server_fallback.notes: The inventory documents no provider-managed fallback.

realtime.notes: The inventory documents no realtime session API. Streaming transcription uses server-sent events.

response_caching.notes: The inventory documents no generation response cache. The no_cache option on Web Reader controls page fetching only.

responses.notes: The API key guide and Coding Plan quick start list an OpenAI Responses endpoint at api.z.ai/api/v1. No API reference describes it, so its fields are undocumented. RubyLLM declares only Chat Completions for Z.ai, so protocol: :responses raises an error.

responses_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint.

search_api.notes: POST /paas/v4/web_search returns structured search results, separate from chat. RubyLLM has no search operation for it.

server_apply_patch.notes: The chat tool schema has no apply patch tool.

server_tool_image_generation.notes: The chat tool schema has no image generation tool.

server_tool_search.notes: The chat tool schema has no tool search.

server_x_search.notes: The chat tool schema has no X search tool.

shell_computer_tools.notes: The chat tool schema has no shell or computer tools.

sound_effects.notes: The inventory documents no sound effects generation.

streaming_speech.notes: No speech endpoint is documented, and the SDK pages that list text-to-speech say nothing about streaming it. A block on RubyLLM.speak would stream from audio/speech through the inherited protocol, which is unverified here.

task_budgets.notes: The inventory documents no task budget option.

text_intelligence.notes: The inventory documents no text analysis endpoint. The translation agent is a separate agent operation.

vector_store_management.notes: The inventory documents no vector store or knowledge base API.

video_batches.notes: The inventory documents no batch endpoint.

video_editing.notes: The inventory documents no video editing input on the video endpoint.

video_extension.notes: The inventory documents no video extension option.

voice_cloning.notes: The inventory documents no voice cloning.

voice_conversion.notes: The inventory documents no voice conversion.

web_fetch_api.notes: POST /paas/v4/reader fetches a URL and returns parsed content in selectable formats. RubyLLM has no operation for it.

websockets.notes: The inventory documents no WebSocket transport.

gaps.notes: Token counting: POST /paas/v4/tokenizer has no integration, so count_tokens and RubyLLM.tokenize raise an error.
Video generation: CogVideoX-3 jobs have no integration, so RubyLLM.animate raises an error.
OCR / document parsing: Layout Parsing with GLM-OCR has no integration, so RubyLLM.ocr raises an error.
File upload: POST /paas/v4/files has no integration, and chat cannot reference file_id through an attachment.
Responses API: the listed api.z.ai/api/v1 endpoint cannot be selected, because RubyLLM declares only Chat Completions here.
Standalone search API, Standalone web fetch API: Web Search and Web Reader have no RubyLLM operations.
PDF input, Video input: RubyLLM rejects these attachments, though the GLM-5.3-Flash series accepts file and video_url parts. Only a replaced messages value or a before_request edit can send them.
Web search tool, Citations: web_search has no alias, and its results stay in the raw response instead of message.citations.

Image generation, Transcription, Streaming transcription: these use inherited Chat Completions code with no recording for this provider. GLM-Image and GLM-ASR-2512 are not in the registry and need assume_model_exists: true. Paint also sends n, and a null size when none is given, which the schema does not describe.
Tool choice: Z.ai documents only auto, so other choices are left for the API to answer.
Thinking controls: GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash return an error if thinking is disabled and take only low, high and max effort.
